## Feature submission evidence

**Feature evidence last updated:** 2026-10-22.

The shared assessment status line and revision history are current upstream; this dated section records the submission's feature evidence and revisions without rescoring upstream or claiming a new combined build or runtime measurement.

- Current-main conflict reconciliation retains upstream and feature behavior; scores and estimates unchanged
- Superseded 2026-10-20 behavior, retained as history: Artboard Options shares existing presets and orientation controls and can fit artwork without moving it; artwork fitting uses the original target artboard and revision-scoped bounds caches (scores/hours unchanged)

- Artboard Options puts Fit to Artwork Bounds and Fit to Selected Art in the Preset menu. Artwork bounds cover all drawn document art, including other artboards and off-board art; selection bounds may span artboards. Fit changes only the active artboard and keeps artwork stationary, including position-only fitting with Move Artwork enabled. Existing Background Color and presets remain available; scores and estimates unchanged.

Artboard Options forwards the active Artboard tool's Scale Artwork with Artboard option for ordinary resizing. Fit to Artwork Bounds and Fit to Selected Art explicitly leave artwork stationary. Dialog regression coverage checks preset/orientation/typed-size intent with scaling on and off, draft cancellation, one-step Undo/Redo, and fitting while Move Artwork and Scale Artwork are enabled. This is a narrow follow-up to #3277; no parity score or estimate is reassessed.

## How this was measured (2026-10-10)

- **Target version.** Illustrator 2026, the 30.x line. Feature set from Adobe's public documentation and release
  announcements: 30.0 (October 2025: font browser, gradient dither and perceptual blending, tangent and
  perpendicular snapping, artboard locking and colours, Turntable beta, Firefly integration), 30.2 (TIFF in
  Export for Screens), 30.3, 30.5 (Concept to Vector, Prompt to Edit, Rewrite Text) and 30.7 (Blend panel with
  ease in/out). Sources: the [30.0 announcement](https://community.adobe.com/questions-652/illustrator-2026-v30-0-font-browser-color-snapping-artboards-enhancements-turntable-and-more-1546612),
  the [30.7 announcement](https://community.adobe.com/announcements-651/illustrator-30-7-new-blend-panel-ease-in-out-blends-generate-artwork-with-firefly-bug-fixes-and-more-1635245)
  and helpx feature pages.
- **The installed Illustrator was not inspected.** Illustrator 2026 is installed on the owner's Mac, but this
  repo's clean-room rule ([`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md), from the project owner) forbids reading anything inside an
  Adobe install, its `Info.plist` and `.lproj` folders included, and forbids launching or measuring it. So
  nothing here is a menu dump or a side-by-side measurement: the numbers come from our own code against
  Illustrator's public documentation.
- **From the code (measured, origin/main `01e165af`):**
  - Menu tree (`crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs`, laid out in Illustrator's menu order): 348 items bound to
    commands, 26 stubs (`todo(…)`/`todos(…)`), so 93.0% of menu items do something (348 and 26 after Snap to Glyph shipped in #3124; 348 and 27 after the
    Revolve merge; 350 and 25, 93.3%, after Graph › Design and Marker; 353 and 22, 94.1%, after Extrude & Bevel, Inflate and Rotate). The stubs: Effect › 3D and Materials › Materials, Effect › SVG Filters, Edit › Spelling (3), Graph › Column, Live Paint
    Gap Options, Optical Margin Alignment, global and video rulers (2),
    Window › Arrange (4), SVG Interactivity, the library placeholders (3), Other Script…, Help.
    Gap Options, Optical Margin Alignment, Start Global Edit, global and video rulers (2),
    Window › Arrange (4), SVG Interactivity, the Brush Libraries placeholders (3; Window › Symbol Libraries works since 2026-10-23), Other Script…, Help.
  - Engine commands: ~710 ids registered with `cmd!` across `crates/engine/src/cmd` (plus macro-generated
    families), and 85 UI-only commands (`UI_COMMANDS`).
  - Tools: 91 in `crates/tools/src/catalog.rs`; Touch Type is listed but not implemented, and the Dimension
    tool (added in Illustrator 28.x) is absent.
  - Effects catalogue (`crates/effects/src/lib.rs`): see [effects-parity.md](effects-parity.md).
  - Tests: 4,924 `#[test]` functions plus 40 property-test blocks (was "~2,840" in the last estimate).
    ~354k lines of Rust (was ~221k on 2026-10-07).
  - Formats: the `FORMATS` table in `crates/engine/src/cmd/fileio/mod.rs`, see
    [file-format-parity.md](file-format-parity.md).
  - Languages: row counts of `crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/*.tsv`, see [localization-parity.md](localization-parity.md).
- **From users:** the 71 open GitHub issues on 2026-10-10, which show what real users hit first (Illustrator
  `.ai` files opening with the wrong layer structure #951/#868, guides lost from `.ai` #779, Shape Builder
  region detection #937/#893, launch failures on some Windows and Linux machines #858/#964/#620, pen pressure on
  macOS #852, Preferences options that do nothing #394).
- **Presence is not parity.** Each area is scored by behaviour against the public documentation, and an area is
  100% only when every feature in it behaves like Illustrator. Scores were set by the agents that built the
  features, so they are upper bounds; this pass lowered the ones contradicted by open issues.

~220–360 h. With 4–6 agents on disjoint crates, wall-clock time divides by about 3.5–4 (shared files such as
`menus.rs` and the i18n catalogs serialize some work): ~95–165 h to full parity.

**Why the totals moved up from ~320–500 h (2026-10-05):** the target moved (30.x added gradient dither,
perceptual blending, new snaps, artboard locking, the Blend panel, Turntable), open issues lowered three areas,
the raster-effects row was re-counted bottom-up from measured filter throughput, and generative AI is now
counted. Work that landed since (Variables, Distort/Pixelate/Texture filters, Object Mosaic, German, placed
documents) moved other rows up.

## Ready for real work

Three audiences, each with its own readiness and its own hours to ~95%. Essentials ⊂ mainstream ⊂ full, so the
hours nest. Hours are calibrated as in [Calibration](#calibration). They divide by about 3.5–4 across 4–6 agents
for the feature and fidelity work; stability on users' hardware, the real-file corpus and native-language
review parallelize less and need humans.

| Audience | Ready % | Opus 5.5 agent hours to ~95% (one agent) | With 4–6 agents | Work that dominates |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| **Full Illustrator** (ready for real work; decides the stage) | **~62%** (57–67%) | **~340–560 h** | ~95–160 h | the mainstream work below, plus 3D (50–85 h), raster effects (24–40 h), advanced type (20–28 h), generative AI (30–60 h), localization (55–90 h) and ecosystem |
| **Mainstream illustrator** | **~65%** (60–70%) | **~230–380 h** | ~65–110 h | the interaction-fidelity pass (60–90 h), hardening and QA (30–50 h), stability (20–35 h), performance budgets (15–25 h), `.ai` exchange (10–20 h), the remaining depth of the everyday areas |
| **Essentials user** | **~75%** (70–80%) | **~60–105 h** | ~25–45 h | launch and stability on Windows (20–35 h), in-app help and onboarding (8–15 h), basic QA (10–15 h), Shape Builder regions (4–8 h), UI polish |

### Full Illustrator: additive weighted sum over the dimensions

The standard's method, the same in every app: a weighted **sum** over the dimensions, with written weights.
Values are from [By dimension](#by-dimension).

| Dimension | Weight | Value | Contribution |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Features (depth) | 35 | 75% | 26.3 |
| UI/UX fidelity | 15 | 55% | 8.3 |
| File formats | 12 | 75% | 9.0 |
| Stability | 10 | 60% | 6.0 |
| Performance | 8 | 60% | 4.8 |
| Platforms | 5 | 80% | 4.0 |
| Hardware | 4 | 35% | 1.4 |
| Localization | 4 | 74% | 3.0 |
| Ecosystem and plug-ins | 4 | 15% | 0.6 |
| AI features | 3 | 0% | 0.0 |
| **Ready for real work** | **100** | | **~62%** |

The weights put most of the number on what professionals use daily (features, interaction, files, stability).
Generative AI also sits inside the features row at weight 2 of 105, so it is counted slightly twice; that costs
under a point.

### Mainstream illustrator and essentials user

Both start from feature depth over the areas concerned. **Mainstream:** ~83% over 16 areas (weight 83 of 105:
selection, drawing, path operations, colour, strokes, appearance, live effects, type core, symbols and blends,
layers and artboards, view, guides, file formats, Export for Screens, UI chrome, print). That is discounted
×0.9 for interaction fidelity, ×0.92 for stability on real machines and ×0.92 for Illustrator-file exchange
(83 × 0.9 × 0.92 × 0.92 ≈ 63). The dimensions a typical illustrator rarely hits (plug-in ecosystem,
generative AI, pen tilt, languages beyond their own) are left out. **Essentials:** see [Essentials user](#essentials-user).

The discounts, with the evidence:

- **Illustrator's own files (×0.92).** `.ai` and EPS open as editable art by reading their PDF/PostScript and the
  structure of the editing data. Users do open legacy files a lot: 28 of the 350 issues (8%, ~22 people) are
  about `.ai`/EPS, the most common single format theme. 20 of the 28 are fixed (often the same day). The 8 open
  ones are about structure, not missing art: layers flattened or multiplied (#951: 109 layers instead of 14;
  #868), guides lost (#779), slower opening (#758), live effects, brushes and symbols as their drawn look
  (#637). VectorCraft can't write Illustrator's editing data (undocumented), so its PDF-compatible `.ai` opens
  in Illustrator as plain art; the legacy `.ai` of version 7 it also writes keeps layers, groups and type as text (one
  artboard per file, no transparency) but hasn't been tested by users yet (#868). That blocks beta (the main-format rule) for people who hand files back to Illustrator users,
  but it doesn't stop someone opening and reworking their own archive.
- **Interaction fidelity (×0.9).** Pen, Direct Selection, smart guides and snapping are deep
  ([ui-parity.md](ui-parity.md)), and there has never been a side-by-side session. The issue tracker says the
  details mostly hold: 79 issues are about core drawing (pen, paths, selection, snapping, transform), 68 of them
  (86%) closed, 11 open (#991, #975, #955, #973 among them). One practitioner wrote "0 learning curve from
  pretty heavy AI use over last 20+ years" (#541).
- **Stability on real machines (×0.92).** The code never panics by design, and the main platform (macOS) starts
  reliably, but 26 issues mention a crash, freeze or failed launch (8 open: #858, #964 fixed the day of this
  review, #620, #818, #905 on Windows 7, #834). There is no field record and no real-world file corpus yet.
- **Performance unverified.** Budgets (`vectorcraft-cli perf`) were all met at 25k paths on 2026-10-11; runs of
  0.10.0 on Linux with 4 logical CPUs, reported in #1172 on 2026-10-13, missed all three render budgets at 20k
  paths. Performance is not discounted separately. Open user reports of slowness in mainstream work include #575
  (Linux AppImage), #758 (`.ai` open time), #1097 (zoom and pan in 0.9.0) and #1731 (a drag that stutters as it
  starts).
- **Missing subsystems** a minority need daily (3D, CJK vertical composition, scripting)
  pull the full number below the mainstream one.

### Essentials user

A beginner or casual user who touches only the core features, at their default settings. Excluded: advanced
options, pro workflows, file-exchange edge cases, and everything the mainstream number already leaves out.
Depth here is "does the basic use work", not the area's full score.

| Core feature | Weight | Depth | Evidence |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| New, open and save documents | 8 | 95% | New Document presets, Open for SVG/PDF/`.ai`/images, lossless native save, Data Recovery |
| Shape tools (rectangle, ellipse, polygon, star, line) | 9 | 95% | all shape tools, Live Corners |
| Selection, move, scale, rotate | 9 | 92% | bounding box, smart guides, transform tools |
| Pen and Pencil, basic use | 7 | 88% | [ui-parity.md](ui-parity.md); a few Pencil and Curvature options missing |
| Fill, stroke, colour, swatches | 9 | 95% | M3 done; highlighted-text Eyedropper font/paint and source/target transparency refusal regression-tested; scores and hours unchanged |
| Gradients, basic | 4 | 90% | Gradient panel and on-canvas annotator |
| Type: point and area text, font, size | 8 | 88% | font menu with previews; Hyphenation… and Justification… options per paragraph (#2310, #2755) |
| Align, group, arrange | 6 | 95% | |
| Layers, basic | 4 | 85% | Layers panel rework; no row context menus |
| Shape Builder | 5 | 70% | beginners lean on it; region detection failed on art of thousands of segments (#937's reproduced case, fixed; unconfirmed on the reporter's file) |
| Pathfinder | 4 | 95% | exact booleans |
| Place images, Image Trace | 4 | 85% | 13 trace presets |
| Export PNG/JPG/SVG/PDF, print | 8 | 92% | Art Optimized supersample closes Asset Export ghost borders (#983 / #1037) |
| Undo and redo | 4 | 100% | unlimited, property-tested |
| Zoom, pan, fit | 4 | 95% | |
| Artboards, basic | 4 | 88% | |
| **Weighted depth** | **97** | **~91%** | |

The discounts a beginner actually hits:

- **Launch and stability, ×0.93:** fine on macOS, but some Windows machines fail to start (#858, #620, #818).
- **Discoverability and UI clarity, ×0.92:** the layout follows Illustrator's and comes in 11 languages, but
  there is no in-app help (Help › VectorCraft Help… is a stub), no Learn panel or tutorials, and a newcomer
  meets Illustrator's density without Illustrator's learning material.
- **Opening files people send them, ×0.96:** PDF, SVG, images and most `.ai` files open as editable art.
  Layer-structure problems (#951) matter less to a beginner.

91 × 0.93 × 0.92 × 0.96 ≈ 75: **~75% (70–80%), estimated.**

### User sentiment (measured 2026-10-10)

All 350 issues and 964 issue comments on GitHub (Discussions are off), authors other than the maintainers:

- **Praise:** 17 issue threads from 15 people ("Great work on this. It's kind of amazing" #954; "really great
  job" #841; "I really love this project" #620; "0 learning curve from pretty heavy AI use over last 20+ years"
  #541).
- **"Replacing Illustrator" reports:** none found in the tracker. Praise is for the app as it is, not reports
  of having switched on paid work. Owner reports from practitioners outside GitHub aren't counted here.
- **Themes of the 350 issues:** core drawing 79 (11 open), import/export 59 (17 open), launch/crash/platform/
  performance 51 (12 open), UI chrome and layers 46 (10 open), type 28 (4 open), colour 12 (5 open), other and
  requests 75 (24 open). 35 are titled as feature requests. The open set is mostly core-path bugs and
  file-exchange problems, not niche features.

**Stage: alpha.** All six core workflows pass the core-workflow gate end to end on macOS with save and reopen
([roadmap.md › Alpha gate](roadmap.md#alpha-gate)); file exchange with Illustrator users is partial, which is
what keeps it from beta, not from alpha.

## Calibration

Hours come from this repo's own history (git log and merged-PR timestamps, `gh pr list`):

- **Raster filters**, one agent working serially on [gap 2](gaps.md): Pixelate (4 filters, merged 2026-10-10
  08:47), Texture (6, 12:44), Distort (3, 16:24). About 4 h per batch, **0.7–1.2 h per Photoshop-style
  filter** including dialog, catalogue row, menus and translations into 11 languages.
- **M3 (paint and appearance):** a 92-task plan whose packages were planned at 5–11 h each took about
  1–1.5 agent hours each, on 2026-10-04/05 with 6–8 agents.
- **Medium features:** about 0.8 h each (Text Wrap, Graphs, Effect › Pathfinder…: ~20 in ~16 h on 2026-10-02).
- **Whole repo:** 1,671 commits and 592 merged PRs from 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-10, with several agents in
  parallel and a dozen community contributors.

Large subsystems (3D, CJK composition, generative AI) have no comparable history and are counted bottom-up,
with a wider range. What needs a human: native-speaker review of the translations, an owner decision on
generative models, real Illustrator files that users own (used locally, never committed), and Wacom/pen
hardware for tilt and rotation.

## Where we already beat Illustrator

Exact curve booleans, off-thread multithreaded rendering, unlimited undo, lossless SVG/PDF export of live effects,
a documented JSON format, Affinity 1–3 import, the same app on the web and on Linux/FreeBSD, scrubby numeric fields,
sandboxed WebAssembly plug-ins, and every command, gesture and dialog drivable by agents (MCP, CLI, control channel).

## Out of scope (by design or by law)

- **Adobe cloud services** (Libraries sync, Adobe Fonts, Projects, Express templates, Firefly): pluggable
  provider APIs at most, never built in.
- **Adobe's bundled assets** (swatch, brush, symbol libraries, presets, icons): ours are original.
- **Illustrator's private editing data, beyond its structure:** see
  [file-format-parity.md](file-format-parity.md#illustrators-private-editing-data).

Film Grain (G2, 2026-10-12) is the first Artistic filter: deterministic document-space monochrome
grain, transparency-preserving tone controls, a bounded live dialog, undo and appearance editing,
with PNG rendering and SVG/PDF raster baking. Evidence: `crates/effects/src/pixel/artistic.rs`,
its `film_grain_*` tests and the canvas/export cases in `crates/engine/src/tests_rasterfilters.rs`.
This raises the measured Photoshop filter count to 29/57; the depth estimate is conservatively 49%.
The full feature/readiness headline remains unchanged at its existing rounding.

Cutout, Neon Glow and Poster Edges (G2, 2026-10-16) follow as original Artistic filters with live
preview, undo, appearance editing and save/reopen, keeping coverage at any Document Raster Effects
resolution. Evidence: `crates/effects/src/pixel/artistic.rs`, its `cutout_*`, `neon_glow_*` and
`poster_edges_*` tests, and `artistic_settings_survive_a_save_and_open` in
`crates/engine/src/tests_rasterfilters.rs`. Smudge Stick, Sponge and Watercolor follow (G2, 2026-10-16) as original Artistic filters with the same
live preview, undo, appearance editing and save/reopen; evidence: `crates/effects/src/pixel/paint.rs`,
its `pixel::tests_paint::*` tests and `tests_rasterfilters`. Measured Photoshop filter count 36/57; depth unchanged.
`crates/engine/src/tests_rasterfilters.rs`. Bas Relief, Charcoal, Photocopy and Stamp (G2, 2026-10-16, #2527) follow as original Sketch filters
(`crates/effects/src/pixel/sketch_ink.rs`, `pixel::tests_sketch::*`). Measured Photoshop filter count 37/57; depth unchanged.

## Detailed missing items per area (2026-10-05 table, still current unless the area table above says otherwise)

> **Duplicated rows (2026-10-14):** this table lists "Selection, transform & align tools" three times and "Drawing tools"
> twice, each time with different text, as merges that each edited the table left them. Which text is current needs the
> owner's judgement, so the rows are kept as they are.

The previous estimate's per-area missing lists, kept as evidence. Scores in it are superseded by the table above.

_Method (2026-10-02; M3 rows re-derived 2026-10-04, file, export, print, links and UI-chrome rows after M4 on 2026-10-05):_ Illustrator's feature surface is split into 22 areas, weighted by how much of the app (and of
real users' work) each represents. Each area is scored by depth of behaviour, not by presence of a menu item: an area
is 100% only when every feature in it behaves like Illustrator. Feature parity = Σ weight × score / Σ weight. Remaining
time is counted per area from what is missing, calibrated on measured throughput: in the last session one agent landed
about 20 medium features (Text Wrap, Graphs, Effect → Pathfinder, export baking…) in ~16 h wall clock including builds
and CI on a heavily loaded machine — about 0.8 h per medium feature; large subsystems (3D, raster filters, vertical type)
are counted bottom-up. The M3 rows (colour, strokes, appearance) come from a detailed 92-task M3 plan whose review
found more missing depth than the first estimate; all 92 tasks landed on 2026-10-04 and 2026-10-05 with 6–8 agents in parallel; its packages, planned at 5–11 h each, took
about 1–1.5 agent-hours each, so the other rows (estimated on the older scale) are likely high.

## Honest assessment by dimension (2026-10-05)

The previous assessment's evidence per dimension, kept as it was; the [By dimension](#by-dimension) table above supersedes its numbers.

**In one line:** about two-thirds to three-quarters of Illustrator's features exist and work, and for everyday
vector illustration (drawing, paths, paint and appearance, SVG/PDF/print) VectorCraft is close to usable. Measured
against "a power user can't tell the difference", it is closer to 40–55%. What stands between here and "anyone can
switch" is a handful of large subsystems plus a fidelity pass, not a long tail of small fixes.

**How much to trust the numbers:** area scores are graded by the agents that built the features, from behaviour docs
(`plan/illustrator/`) and tests, not by side-by-side use of Illustrator. Treat them as upper bounds. Look & feel is
the only dimension measured against the reference app. Performance budgets haven't been re-run on an idle machine
since 2026-10-01.

| Dimension | Estimate | Evidence and what's missing |
|---|---|---|
| **Breadth:** menus, tools and panels exist | ~90% | 13 menu items still stubbed; every tool implemented except Touch Type; 51 panel modules |
| **Depth:** each feature behaves like Illustrator | ~69–75% | Strong: paint, appearance and colour (M3), Pathfinder and booleans, selection, drawing, files (M4). Weak: advanced type (~45%; inline symbols in text are beyond parity and don't raise it), brushes and symbols (in progress), raster effects (~20%; since 57/57 filters and the Effect Gallery, #2883, see the area table above) |
| **Large missing subsystems** | 0–20% | 3D & Materials (~25%, initial 3D types without materials), SVG Filters (Photoshop-style raster effects (57/57) and the Effect Gallery (#2883) have since shipped), CJK composition (vertical type with kinsoku, tate-chu-yoko and the font's vertical metrics; mojikumi open), scripting |
| **Interaction fidelity:** modifiers, cursors, small behaviours | ~30–40% | The dedicated pass hasn't started, and there has been no side-by-side session with Illustrator yet. A power user notices this first |
| **Look & feel** | ~75–80% | Measured against Illustrator 2026 screenshots (2026-10-02); the panels added since haven't been re-measured |
| **File interop** | ~85% | SVG/SVGZ, PDF and PDF-compatible `.ai` (and legacy version 7 `.ai` out, keeping layers, groups and type as text), EPS, DXF, EMF/WMF, raster formats, PSD export and PSD/PSB placement (merged image), Place and Links, Package, Print, clipboard flavours. Affinity documents (Affinity 1–3) open natively as editable art, checked against 51 pinned public files (33 current `.af`), with selected saved-thumbnail comparisons and every-board native/SVG/PDF/PSD checks for current files; Affinity export is missing and effects, adjustments and brushes don't import. Affinity isn't an Illustrator feature, so this doesn't raise the parity score. The editing copy inside an Illustrator EPS or `.ai` is read for its structure: layers, groups, names, hidden objects and type, colours, gradients, transparency, images and every artboard (see Out of scope for what it doesn't read yet); DWG has no open spec |
| **Bundled content:** brush, symbol, style and swatch libraries | ~30% | Ours are original and generated in code, and far fewer than Illustrator ships; symbol libraries have one (Basic Shapes) beside User Defined and Other Library…; brush libraries are still missing |
| **Performance** | unverified | Multithreaded, off-thread rendering and caches are in place. The last budget run (2026-10-01, loaded machine) measured 290 ms for a 50k-path fit against a 16 ms budget. Re-run `vectorcraft-cli perf` on an idle machine |
| **Robustness** | good, new | ~2,840 tests, property tests, no panics in shipped code (lints, the `guard` safety net, import fuzzing), Data Recovery. Missing: a corpus of real-world files, Windows/Linux/browser QA |
| **Platforms and 1.0 polish** | ~60% | The macOS app and the web build work, and Finder opens every readable format with the macOS app (#295, #354); on macOS the menus are in the system menu bar, laid out as a Mac app's, with the in-window menus as a fallback (`--in-window-menus`; verified on Windows and by cross-compilation, not yet by hand on a Mac); hybrid-graphics laptops render on the power-saving GPU by default on Windows and macOS (#306), and Windows starts on Direct3D 12, falling back to OpenGL, and loads no Vulkan driver unless `WGPU_BACKEND` asks for it (#545: Vulkan flickered black on an Intel GPU, DX12 and OpenGL didn't; #806: a faulty Vulkan driver crashed the app before its window appeared; verified by unit tests and the reporter's runs with `WGPU_BACKEND`), and Linux on the GPU the desktop runs on, since a Wayland compositor may refuse frames from the other one; a window that fails on its GPU while starting up starts again on the next one instead of crashing (#502; the dual-GPU Wayland case is verified by unit tests and cross-compilation, not on such hardware); web drops land in the document they were dropped on (#359); desktop drops carry no pointer position (winit 0.30), so a dropped document opens as a tab of its own and a picture or text is placed in the middle of the view, while the web places anything dropped on the canvas and opens what is dropped off it, as Illustrator does (#472); a web page that loses its WebGPU device or WebGL context restarts its graphics with the same documents (#369); on Linux/Wayland the clipboard reads the compositor's own (data-control) and copied image files paste, but files can't be dropped on the window under native Wayland until eframe moves to winit 0.31 (#398; the Wayland side is verified by compilation only), so Preferences › Performance › Linux Display Server › X11 (XWayland) opens the window through XWayland, where drops work (#1151; verified by unit tests and cross-compilation, not on a Wayland desktop); on Linux the Paste menu checks the system clipboard on a background thread, so a clipboard owner that never answers no longer freezes the window, while Windows and macOS keep their quick in-line check (#510; the X11 hang verified by the contributor, here by headless tests); on KDE Plasma 6.3+ under Wayland, pens and pen displays reach the app only under XWayland (`WAYLAND_DISPLAY=`) or with KWin's `KWIN_WAYLAND_EMULATE_TABLET=1`, since winit 0.30 has no Wayland tablet input (#491, not verified on hardware); Windows/Linux packaging and accessibility are pending; an experimental, unsupported Windows 7 x64 OpenGL build exists (community-contributed, not verified by maintainers) |
| **Agent automation** | beyond Illustrator | Every command, gesture and dialog is drivable over MCP, the CLI and the control channel; synthetic-input counts, pending events and per-frame control requests are bounded (#1709); what an agent reads and writes on disk can be confined to chosen folders (`--automation-read-root` / `--automation-write-root`, as in PhotoCraft, #832) |
| **Scrubby numeric fields** | beyond Illustrator | As in Photoshop, dragging a numeric field's label (`W:`, `Opacity:`, the Character panel's icons) left or right steps its value live; one undo step per drag, Escape cancels (#400) |
| **Align Stroke on live type** | beyond Illustrator | The Stroke panel's Align Stroke works on type's character stroke: inside or outside the glyphs without Create Outlines, the type staying editable (as InDesign does; users have asked Illustrator for it since 2010, e.g. [redd.it/1dwhos6](https://redd.it/1dwhos6)). Canvas, PDF and EPS clip it to its side of the glyphs; SVG keeps the text live and draws the stroke on the glyph outlines (#2294) |

## Evidence: what ships today, by area

- 3D lighting presets: `crates/effects/src/lighting_presets.rs`, `crates/engine/src/cmd/tests_lighting_presets.rs` and the pointer tests in `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs/tests_revolve.rs` cover recognition, atomic targeting, native round trips, preview, Cancel, reset and Undo.

- **Status-bar pointer readout (2026-10-18):** uses the same effective ruler origin as the position fields, then formats the relative X/Y in General units. The absolute pointer position, document, selection, Undo/Redo and saved state are preserved. Three `chrome::tests::status_coordinates_*` painted-text regressions cover zero/positive/negative origins, unit conversion, global/artboard mode, active artboard, reset and missing pointer/document. Original headless status-bar captures were reviewed before and after the change. Scores and hours are unchanged.

**Drawing tools — Polygon and Star counts:** The existing canvas placement dialog reads the stored count and saves it only after successful placement. `polygon_and_star_canvas_counts_persist_without_new_toolbar_dialogs` covers both tools, repeated drags, tool switching, reopening and Cancel. Counts remain session tool options. Existing click and toolbar gestures are retained; no score or hour change.
**Live trace result bounds and selection highlights exclude the retained bitmap except in source-image views:** `live_trace_result_bounds_exclude_the_retained_bitmap_at_any_angle` checks every TraceView, geometric and visual bounds and rotated result bounds. `live_trace_selection_highlight_excludes_the_retained_source_rectangle` checks result highlights and the existing ordinary-group policy. Shared editing-child traversal also preserves Shaper handling.
**Artboard Options shares existing presets and orientation controls and can fit artwork without moving it; artwork fitting includes all drawn document art across artboards and off-board; artwork bounds are cached by active document and revision, and selection uses the shared bounds cache across artboards:** Shared existing preset definitions are reused; no external preset assets are added. Presets preserve each selected artboard's orientation, and orientation choices apply even when the active board already matches. Fit operations draft bounds until OK, affect only the active artboard and leave artwork in place. Regression coverage checks draft/Cancel, selected-set application, active-only fitting and Undo.

**Review follow-up:** The fit-query follow-up covers fitting after draft dimensions change, updated artwork after a document revision, cache scope and new-artboard fitting/history. Selection uses the existing application bounds cache; global artwork queries include all drawn document art and are cached by active document and revision; draft geometry and target artboards do not limit membership. This is not a native timing claim.

- **Stable status-bar readouts:** The status message keeps its left anchor and clipping allocation as live values, canvas hover and background-job state change. Coordinate and spinner slots stay reserved; narrow windows hide optional diagnostics, then coordinates, to preserve message space. Widths are measured from the active font, translated labels and fixed numeric samples, never current readings. Coordinates through +/-9999.99 selected units, timings through 9999.9 ms and FPS through 9999 remain readable. Extreme values are elided with full tooltip/accessibility text; only elided fields show a tooltip. Coordinate inspection retains the last point per document and clears on PointerGone. Regressions cover message origin/clip/bounds/elision invariance, all registered languages and ten units, responsive layouts, coordinate inspection and document switching, and accessible busy transitions. The contributor rebuilt and confirmed the original status-bar issue is fixed with their own artwork on 2026-10-19; the subsequent upstream rebase is checked by regressions and full CI. The artwork stays local. Scores and estimates are unchanged. Sample widths use a bounded single-entry UI cache keyed by language, unit and pixels per point; two regressions verify reuse during live updates and invalidation after each display-setting change.

- **Canvas review follow-up:** Cached canvas dimensions match the renderer limit before cache-key creation, view construction and worker submission. Controlled-worker regression checks oversized width and height, high DPI and the render transform without allocating oversized images. Scores and estimates are unchanged.
- **Cached canvas frames during viewport changes:** Cached screen textures use their own raster dimensions and pixels-per-point when reprojected. `canvas::tests::cached_frames_keep_their_scale_during_resize_rotation_and_dpi_changes` holds the worker and checks every UV corner against the cached render transform, including isolated viewport-only resize at zero/30-degree rotation, fractional raster dimensions, zoom/pan, changed rotation, monitor-DPI changes in both directions, Pixel Preview and replacement-frame delivery. The contributor rebuilt and confirmed the original resize issue is fixed with their own artwork on 2026-10-19; the subsequent upstream rebase is checked by regressions and full CI. The artwork stays local. Scores and estimates are unchanged.
- **PDF editable import:** Place from bytes or a path with `link: false`, and `clipboard.importPdf` followed by Paste, preserve live type on the selected page. Place still honors `textAs: "outlines"`. Synthetic two-page regressions: `crates/engine/src/cmd/fileio/tests_pdffidelity.rs`. No change to the PDF reader's existing fallback rules.
- **Selected Mirror Repeat handles:** a headless canvas regression creates the default mirror repeat and drags its Top bounding-box handle where the axis crosses it; the repeat grows vertically while its width stays fixed. Existing mirror-axis checks cover center movement and end-handle hit priority. The focused UI mirror tests pass. Scores and hours unchanged.
- **Transform effect options (#885):** Effect › Distort & Transform › Transform… has visible Transform Objects, Transform Patterns and Scale Strokes & Effects checkboxes (`distort.transform` params `objects`, `patterns`, `strokes`; files without them draw as before). With Transform Objects off the geometry stays and makes no copies; Scale Strokes & Effects scales stroke weights, dashes and the fills' and strokes' effect distances by the mean scale, and Transform Patterns moves pattern tiles, each copy `k` by the transformation `k` times. Such objects draw, export and expand through the same per-copy art, so the canvas and Expand Appearance agree (engine `tests_transformfx`, effects `tests_transformfx`, the dialog test). Not yet: a Transform in a fill's or stroke's own effects ignores the two options, and object effects after it keep their distances. Public reference: [Transform objects](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/transforming-objects.html), [Summary of effects](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/summary-of-effects.html). Scores and hours unchanged.
- **Warp Options (#1760):** Effect > Warp and existing Appearance effect links share the fifteen existing styles, original schematic previews, orientation choices and percent Bend/Distortion controls. Focused tests passed for real numeric entry and slider input, Preview/Cancel, immediate Enter/OK, mixed-style edits, target/slot/visibility preservation and Undo/Redo. Each applied style stays unchanged until an explicit Style choice. Original style-menu and live-preview captures were reviewed; their numeric values were supplied programmatically. Public references: [Reshaping with effects](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/reshaping-objects-effects.html) and [Using effects](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/effects.html). Warp geometry, optional Properties integration and remembered defaults are unchanged; no broader parity claim.
- **Constrain Angle (#394):** General › Constrain Angle turns the arrow keys' axes (guides stay on the page's), holds Shift drags of the Selection, Direct Selection, Free Transform, Slice Selection, Reshape and Measure tools and the Pen's handles to the turned axes, and new rectangles, rounded rectangles, ellipses, grids, point and area type, Shift-drawn polygons and stars and the shape size dialogs are drawn along it with their bounding box turned; 0° and whole turns are exactly as before, quarter turns exact (<https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/manage-objects/arrange-objects/rotate-objects-by-specific-angles.html>). Tests: `tests_constrain_tools`, `tests_constrain_new` (engine), `geom` `constrain_axes` / `rotate_deg`, the shape, grid and type tool tests.

- **Clipping paths on their outline (G1):** the selection tools (Selection, Direct Selection, Group Selection), Object Highlighting and a right-click take a clipping path on its outline before the art it clips; Select Behind lists the same; the eyedropper, the tools that act on what is drawn and the selection tools' double-clicks, loaded text and guide release take the art. Doc and tool regression tests; score unchanged.
- **Existing-guide Escape cancellation (G1):** Escape clears a pending guide press or drag through Selection and Direct/Group Selection, cancelling a begun preview. Eight app-input regressions cover both axes, move/copy, temporary selection-tool borrowing from idle Pen, preselected-guide document/interaction-start selection and Undo/Redo/saved-state preservation, later on-canvas motion/release, Shift-press cancellation, and ordinary-release/Enter/idle controls. Historical focused checks on `8ab574b7` recorded five expected RED failures with three passing controls, then all eight GREEN tests and the Direct Selection Escape control passed. All nine also passed in current full CI. A full CI retry on the five-unit combined source at `a0671777` passed all seven stages with 6,613 test outcomes on 2026-10-14. An earlier full-CI run on the identical source panicked in the randomized `ai_mutated_save_never_panics` test; the cause remains unresolved. This five-fix batch does not claim to repair that failure. The original 1280×960 headless app capture from `b076025a` was reviewed for one vertical Selection guide after Escape; source review found its scene unchanged on `a0671777`. Scores and hours unchanged.
- **TIFF in screen and asset export:** both format menus expose the existing TIFF encoder and Format Settings. Headless UI regressions choose TIFF and check scaled dimensions, artboard selection, filenames, encoding options, saved settings and collected-asset output. Public reference: [Export for Screens](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/save-and-export/export-files-to-different-formats/export-for-screens.html), updated 2026-09-28, lists TIFF for both artboards and assets. Adobe staff [confirmed support in 30.2.1](https://illustrator.uservoice.com/forums/333657-illustrator-desktop-feature-requests/suggestions/49081034-add-tiff-format-into-export-for-screens-assets-d) on 2026-02-19; the older 2025 Collect assets guide omits TIFF.
- **Export for Screens of the selected artboards:** while the Artboard tool is in use, File › Export › Export for Screens… (`file.exportForScreens`) opens with the artboards the tool has selected checked on its Artboards tab, and Export Artboard writes only those. Shift-clicks on the canvas, or Shift- or Ctrl/Cmd-clicks on the Artboards panel's rows, select several. The other fields show the settings the document last exported with. With another tool in use, the dialog takes its artboard choice from those settings too. Public reference: [Export selected artboards](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/create-manage-artboards/organize-manage-artboards/export-artboards.html).

- **Effects in Export Selection and asset crops:** File › Export Selection, Asset Export, Export for Screens' Assets tab and CSS Properties' rasterized art crop each object to the bounds the renderer measures for what it draws: drop shadows, glows, geometry effects such as Offset Path, a group's own effects and the effects in a symbol's art. A brushed path is cropped to its visual bounds, and a Shaper group is cropped to the art it shows. `assets.list` reports the same crop. Engine tests export a square with each effect, a group with a shadow and an asset with a shadow, and check that the effect is inside the image. Public reference: a [Community Expert answer](https://community.adobe.com/t5/illustrator-discussions/exporting-assets-adds-transparent-borders/m-p/10708713/highlight/true) traces the extra area of exported assets to the raster effects' area (Document Raster Effects Settings › Add Around Object).

- **Effects in the art's bounds:** Export with Use Artboards off, Fit to Artwork Bounds, and the other exports of the whole art (EPS without artboards, Export for Screens' Full Document, Save for Web (Legacy) with Clip to Artboard off) measure each visible object as the export crops above do. The drop shadows and other effects of groups, layers, type and images are inside the image or the artboard. A Shaper group without effects of its own is measured by the art it shows, and the hidden members of a group with a drop shadow, a glow or another raster effect do not count unless it is a Shaper group or also has a geometry, Pathfinder, Crop Marks or 3D effect or a visible effect on its own fill or stroke. The SVG of an artboard keeps an object whose effects alone reach the artboard. Tests measure a group, type and an image with a drop shadow, export a group and type with Use Artboards off and fit an artboard to them.

- **Selected artboard deletion:** the Artboards panel menu, panel trash button and Properties use the same selected set; selecting all retains artboard 1. Pointer-event tests cover nonadjacent and single selections, the original first-board survivor, ordinary artwork, Undo/Redo and the single-board guard. Measured by `tests_svg_glyphs`, `svg/tests/it/svg_glyphs.rs`, `tests_colourfonts::create_outlines_turns_svg_glyphs_into_groups`, `tests_colourfonts::pdf_real_text_draws_svg_glyphs_as_art_and_keeps_their_characters`. - **Character-style Auto leading:** capture and explicit style attributes retain Auto as a reset, distinct from omitted leading. Redefine and later numeric updates preserve local leading overrides; the Character Styles marker recognizes Auto correctly. Regression assertions cover partial definitions, Undo/Redo and native save/load serialization. Public references: [Character and paragraph styles](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/character-paragraph-styles.html) and [Leading](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/line-character-spacing.html).
- **Text styles redefined to the defaults:** New and Redefine Character Style and Paragraph Style capture every attribute of the selected text, including those at their defaults (Auto kerning, Roman baseline alignment, the default Hyphenation options, the Every-line Composer, no tab stops), and `charStyle.setAttrs` and `paraStyle.setAttrs` keep an attribute set to its default value. After a redefinition, text whose value still equals the old definition's takes the new value, a default included; local overrides and attributes the new definition leaves out stay. The style panels show "+" only where the text differs from its style, including type with Auto alignment. Public reference: [Character and paragraph styles](https://web.archive.org/web/20260825113735/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/character-paragraph-styles.html).

Evidence: `ParaStyle::effective_leading` (`crates/doc/src/text.rs` test `paragraph_effective_leading_follows_auto_leading`), `tests_prefs::auto_leading_steps_and_fills_from_the_paragraph_auto_leading`, `panels::character` test `leading_field_shows_the_paragraph_auto_leading`.
- **Names of new styles and symbols:** `charStyle.new` and `paraStyle.new` trim the white space around the name they are given, as `charStyle.rename` and `paraStyle.rename` do, and refuse a name that is then empty; Duplicate names its copy from the trimmed name. `symbol.new` and `symbol.duplicate` trim the name as Symbol Options does, and `library.use` adds a library's text style under its trimmed name. Public reference: [Character and paragraph styles](https://web.archive.org/web/20260825113735/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/character-paragraph-styles.html).
- **Width Point Edit:** Shift-double-click enables Adjust Adjoining Width Points; plain double-click and direct opening retain the default. Tool dispatch and headless dialog tests cover neighboring widths, Undo/Redo and Cancel. Public reference: [Variable-width strokes](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/stroke-object.html).

Tool and egui event tests exercise both rulers, modifier changes, cancellation and one-step Undo/Redo; existing-guide Alt-copy and ruler-origin gestures are unchanged.
