- **Rulers (#1212):** drag the intersection to preview and set a document zero point, or double-click it to reset to the active artboard's top-left. Transform, Properties and Control X/Y fields measure from it and convert entered positions back to absolute command coordinates. The origin survives every native format version and compression; geometry, guides and patterns stay in place. Public reference: [Use rulers](https://helpx.adobe.com/ca/illustrator/desktop/measure-and-align/grids-and-guides/use-rulers.html).
- **Global and artboard rulers:** View › Rulers › Change to Global / Artboard Rulers (Cmd+Alt+R, `view.globalRulers`). A new document has artboard rulers: the rulers and the Transform, Properties, Control and Info X/Y count from the active artboard's top-left corner, or the zero point dragged out for that artboard, which moves with it; with global rulers one document zero point serves every artboard. Guide readouts and Shift ruler-tick snapping follow the same zero point. The mode is saved with the document; files from before it open with global rulers, as they measured. Regression tests: `engine/tests/it/ruler_origin.rs`, `ui-egui/src/tests_ruler_origin.rs`, `tools/src/rulerguide.rs`. Public reference: [About rulers](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/measure-and-align/grids-and-guides/about-rulers.html).
- **Video display options (#2849):** Artboard Options' Show Video Safe Areas and Video Ruler Pixel Aspect Ratio, and View › Rulers › Show Video Rulers ([Set video display options for artboards](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/create-manage-artboards/organize-manage-artboards/set-video-display-options-for-artboards.html)). Each artboard has its own (`artboard.setProps`/`artboard.new` `showVideoSafeAreas`, `videoRulerPixelAspectRatio` 0.1–10, default 1), set in one undo step and written to the native format only when on or not 1, so other documents save byte for byte as before. The help page names the safe areas without numbers; our choice is [EBU R 95](https://tech.ebu.ch/docs/r/r095.pdf)'s (note 5): the canvas outlines the action-safe area 3.5% and the title-safe (graphics-safe) area 5% in from each edge, 1 point wide and turned with the view; exports and print leave them out. Show Video Rulers (`view.videoRulers`) shows the rulers counting the active artboard in pixels from its top-left corner, whatever the ruler origin: a pixel is as many points wide as the ratio and one point tall, so a 720 × 480 pt artboard at 0.9 reads 800 × 480. Hide Video Rulers returns them to the General unit; Shift ruler-tick snapping of new guides keeps the General unit. Regression tests: `tests_panelcmds.rs` (`artboard_video_display_options_*`, `artboard_display_marks_stay_out_of_exports`), `tests_docsetup.rs` (`an_artboard_shows_its_video_safe_areas`), `canvas.rs` (`video_rulers_count_the_artboard_in_pixels_of_its_aspect_ratio`), `tests_ruler_origin.rs` (`show_video_rulers_counts_the_active_artboard_in_pixels`), `dialogs/tests.rs` (`artboard_options_show_video_display_options`).

- **Document Setup modal handoff:** Document Setup → Edit Artboards applies valid settings, closes the dialog and activates the Artboard tool. Pointer-click tests cover successful handoff, invalid settings, OK, Cancel and Undo in `dialogs/document_setup.rs`.
- **Control bar with the Artboard tool:** while the Artboard tool is in use, the Control bar shows the active artboard's controls in place of the object controls: Preset, Portrait and Landscape, New Artboard, Delete Artboard, the Name field, Artboard Options, Rearrange All Artboards, the Transform link, Move and Scale Artwork with Artboard and, while the bar has room, the reference point with X and Y, and W and H with the Constrain Width and Height Proportions link. Each runs the command its Properties or Transform panel counterpart runs (`artboard.setProps`, `artboard.new`, `artboard.delete`, `tool.options {tool: "artboard"}`), and the reference point is the one the Transform panel uses. In an 800-point window the controls up to the Transform link fit, Move and Scale Artwork with Artboard show as their boxes alone with their names in tooltips, and the link opens the Transform panel with the artboard's position and size. Pointer and key tests in `panels/artboards.rs` cover the controls, W about the reference point, the orientation and the name. Public reference: [Using multiple artboards](https://web.archive.org/web/20210925094818/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/using-multiple-artboards.html) (archived copy).
- **Names of new and renamed artboards, brushes and patterns:** `artboard.new` and `artboard.setProps` trim the white space around the name they are given, as the Artboards panel's rename does, and a blank name gives the artboard its default name, Artboard N for the Nth artboard. `brush.new`, `brush.duplicate`, `brush.options`, `object.pattern.make`, `object.pattern.saveCopy` and `pattern.options` trim the name as the Brush Options dialog and the Pattern Options panel do, and compare the trimmed name with the names there are; a blank name gives the name each command gives when there is none, and Brush Options and Pattern Options keep the name. Tests in `tests_panelcmds.rs`, `tests_brushsym.rs` and `tests_pattern.rs` cover each command. Public references: [Using multiple artboards](https://web.archive.org/web/20210925094818/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/using-multiple-artboards.html), [Brushes](https://web.archive.org/web/20251018101754/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/brushes.html) and [Create and edit patterns](https://web.archive.org/web/20211031180358/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/create-edit-patterns.html) (archived copies).
- **Pattern names and swatch names:** `pattern.options` refuses a new name that another pattern, a swatch or a color group has. It takes a name that only the pattern's own swatches have. The reference page does not say what happens when the new name is taken; the refusal follows VectorCraft's rule that swatches and color groups share one namespace (`Document::swatch_name_taken`), which `swatch.new` and `swatch.edit` also follow. A rename gives the new name only to the pattern's swatches that had the old one; any other swatch with the old name keeps it, and art linked to that swatch stays linked. `object.pattern.make` and `object.pattern.saveCopy` number a color group's name as they number a swatch's. Tests in `tests_pattern.rs` cover each command. Public reference: [Create and edit patterns](https://web.archive.org/web/20211031180358/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/create-edit-patterns.html) (archived copy).
- **A clip group in Properties:** with one clip group selected, the panel has Edit Clipping Path and Edit Contents at its top, under the Clip Group heading, which select the clipping path or the clipped art for the selection tools to transform alone, as Object › Clipping Mask does (<https://www.adobe.com/learn/illustrator/web/crop-using-masks>: with a clip group selected, the tutorial uses Edit Clipping Path at the top of the Properties panel to select the mask for editing, and uses Edit Contents to select the masked art). Edit Contents shows only when the group clips something. Not checked against the reference app: whether Properties keeps the buttons while the clipping path or the contents is selected; the Control bar has no clip-group buttons here. Evidence: `panels::properties::tests::one_clip_group_has_edit_clipping_path_and_edit_contents_at_the_top`.
- **Contextual controls in Properties:** the [Properties panel overview](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/get-started/learn-the-basics/properties-panel-overview.html) lists controls that appear for particular selections and tools; Properties has them, each running the existing command. Quick Actions has Blend Options for one selected blend while the Blend tool is in use (the Blend Options dialog, OK one undo step) and Merge Live Paint when a Live Paint group is selected with more paths and nothing Live Paint refuses (`livePaint.merge`). Appearance has the stroke's Variable Width Profile list, the Control bar's, with the Width tool or when the stroke has a variable width (`stroke.set {profile}`), and beside fx the Delete icon: with one effect on the one selected object (its own or a fill's or stroke's) its name and an icon that removes it (`effect.remove`), with several an icon that opens the Appearance panel, as the overview describes. With Direct Selection and corners of one path selected, Corner and Corner Radius set the kind and radius of those corners (`object.setLiveShape`); a live rectangle's and polygon's own rows already do. Each edit is one undo step. The overview's Variable Font icon was already in Character. Not checked against the reference app: whether Merge needs two Live Paint groups (the overview speaks of several selected groups; `livePaint.merge` takes a group and paths), and where exactly each control sits in its section. Evidence: `panels::properties::tests::{blend_options_is_a_quick_action_for_one_blend_with_the_blend_tool, merge_live_paint_is_a_quick_action_for_a_live_paint_group_and_more, the_width_profile_shows_for_a_variable_width_or_the_width_tool, direct_selected_corners_show_their_kind_and_radius, one_effect_has_a_delete_icon_in_appearance}`.
- **Edit Artboards in Properties:** the active artboard's name is a field. Typing a new name and pressing Enter or clicking elsewhere renames that artboard in one undo step, as the Artboards panel's rename does (`artboard.setProps {index, name}`); pressing Escape or leaving the field empty keeps the old name. A click on the Artboard Options icon beside the field opens Artboard Options for the active artboard, as double-clicking the Artboard tool's button does (`tool.options {tool: "artboard"}`). Pointer and key tests in `panels/properties.rs` cover both. Public references: [Resize artboards](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/create-manage-artboards/add-edit-artboards/resize-artboards.html) and [Create and add new artboards](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/create-manage-artboards/add-edit-artboards/add-new-artboards.html).
- **Artboard background colors:** each artboard can have a background color (`artboard.setProps {index, color}`, `color: null` removes it). With the Artboard tool, Properties has a Fill row: its list sets None, White or Black, and its chip and its Color Picker… item open the Color Picker for the artboard. Artboard Options has a Background Color row with a list that sets None, White or Black, and a color button. The canvas draws the artboard's paper in the color, multiplied with the paper color while Simulate Colored Paper is on, and the transparency grid still covers it. The native format saves the color, and a document without colors saves as before. Exports and print do not draw the color. Engine, canvas, Properties, Color Picker and Artboard Options tests cover it. Public reference: [Apply colors to artboards](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/create-manage-artboards/organize-manage-artboards/add-background-color-to-artboards.html).
- **Resizing several artboards:** with several artboards selected with the Artboard tool, a new W or H in Properties, the Transform panel or the Control bar, a preset or an orientation in Properties or the Control bar, and a new Width or Height in Artboard Options resize every selected artboard in one undo step (`artboard.setProps {artboards}`); with Scale Artwork with Artboard on, Properties, the Transform panel and the Control bar scale each object once, with the artboard it was inside before the change. The Transform panel, the Control bar and Artboard Options resize each one about its own reference point, a preset sizes each one in its own orientation, and X and Y still move the active artboard alone. Pointer and key tests in `panels/properties.rs`, dialog tests in `dialogs/tests.rs` and an engine test in `tests_xform.rs` cover them. Public references: [Artboard Enhancements In Illustrator CC](https://blog.adobe.com/en/publish/2017/11/10/artboard-enhancements-in-illustrator-cc) (a height and a width entered once resize every selected artboard) and [Using multiple artboards](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/using-multiple-artboards.html) (2019).
- **Artboard Escape routing:** Escape leaves Artboard editing for Selection; during a drag it first cancels the gesture. Headless egui key events cover idle Escape, active-drag cancellation and a subsequent Escape in `tests_distortkeys.rs`.
- **Shift with the Artboard tool:** a Shift-click adds an artboard to the selection or takes it out when the button comes up. A Shift-drag inside an artboard draws a new artboard there, and a Shift-drag on the pasteboard is a marquee that toggles the artboards it touches, as the [default keyboard shortcuts](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/default-keyboard-shortcuts.html) (a Shift-drag draws an artboard within an existing one) and [Using multiple artboards](https://web.archive.org/web/20210925094818/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/using-multiple-artboards.html) (archived copy) describe. Shift no longer keeps an artboard move at 45° steps or a drawn artboard square. Escape during a marquee or while a new artboard is being drawn cancels it and keeps the Artboard tool. Pointer and key tests in `crates/tools/src/xform/artboard.rs` cover the four gestures and Escape.
- **Artboard deletion keys:** Delete/Backspace delete selected boards in one Undo step, retaining the original first board in the current order when all are selected, as in the public [Delete artboards guide](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/create-manage-artboards/add-edit-artboards/delete-artboards.html). The last board and active drags stay protected; neither key clears selected artwork. Headless shortcut regressions in `tests_distortkeys.rs` cover reordered boards, artwork, saved state and Undo/Redo.
- **Locked artboards:** a click in the Artboards panel's lock column locks or unlocks an artboard in one undo step (`artboard.setProps {index, locked}`), and the native format saves the lock. The Artboard tool doesn't move, copy, resize or delete a locked artboard, Rearrange and Fit to Artwork Bounds leave it as it is, and its name isn't edited on the canvas. The art on it (each object whose bounds overlap it, a group as one object) acts as locked art until it is unlocked: clicks, marquees, `select.set`, `select.all` and the tools pass over it, and commands that act on the selection leave it; art drawn or pasted onto it stays selected and editable until the selection leaves it out. Tests in `crates/doc/src/lib.rs`, `tests_panelcmds.rs`, `xform/artboard.rs`, `panels/artboards.rs` and `canvas.rs` cover them. Public references: [Lock artboards](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/create-manage-artboards/organize-manage-artboards/lock-artboards.html) and [Managing Artboards in Illustrator](https://creativepro.com/managing-artboards-in-illustrator/).
- **Linux RPM packaging:** 64-bit runtime capabilities replace Fedora-specific required package names (#1275); glibc 2.35, libm and libgcc_s are declared alongside dynamically loaded xkbcommon and Vulkan/EGL. Generated x86_64/aarch64 metadata and isolated synthetic-provider resolution checked; real-distro install/start-up QA remains pending.
- **Linux file associations:** the desktop entry lists the MIME type of every format File › Open reads but PSD, PSB, `.ps` PostScript and Targa, `.ai`, `.ait` and EPS included, and the MIME package declares the types shared-mime-info lacks (VectorCraft documents and templates, `.ait`, Affinity), so file managers list VectorCraft under Open With for them, as Finder does on macOS. `the_linux_desktop_entry_opens_every_readable_format` in `apps/vectorcraft/src/main.rs` checks both files against `OPEN_EXTS`. On Debian 13, Ubuntu 24.04 and Fedora 42, `desktop-file-validate` accepts the desktop entry, `update-mime-database` accepts the MIME package, and `gio` registers the app for every one of these types.

- **Architecture:** 19+ crates with enforced layering (`cargo xtask layers`). Every action is a command (~400 engine + ~50 UI). Undo is unlimited via structural sharing. `command.batch` runs several commands as one transaction.
- **Automation:**
  - Variables: Update Data Set writes what the art holds into the active data set for the variables that data set holds, and keeps the data set's value for a variable whose objects are locked or inside a locked layer or group; `dataset.update {all: true}` also adds the other variables that the art reports a value for.
  - Variables: `dataset.select`, `dataset.next` and `dataset.prev` rewrite type and apply the other values on hidden objects and in hidden layers and groups, which stay hidden unless a visibility value shows them, so a layer shown later holds the selected data set's text; objects that are locked or in a locked layer or group are skipped.
  - Variables: `dataset.select`, `dataset.next` and `dataset.prev` name the area type and type on a path whose text they rewrote and that doesn't fit, in the reply's `overflow` key, as `text.setText` does.
  - Variables: when no object is bound to a variable that the data set has a value for, for example after Import Data Sets… defines new variables without binding them, choosing the data set in the Variables panel or stepping to it with the panel's arrows shows a status message, and `dataset.select`, `dataset.next` and `dataset.prev` add the message to the reply as `warning`.
  - Variables: Lock Variables (`variable.lock`, in the Variables panel's bottom bar and menu) stops variables from being defined, deleted or renamed until they are unlocked, while objects can still be bound and unbound and data sets still change and apply; the lock is saved with the document.
  - Batch…: Override Save and Override Export name each file with the extension of the format the step writes, however the step spells the format (`.svg` and `SVG` give `.svg`, `png8` gives `.png`), in `action.batch`.
  - Actions panel (record/playback, persisted), generic parameter dialogs for every "…" command.
  - Batch… over data sets names each file after the document and the data set (`action.batch`). It writes `/`, `\`, `:`, `<`, `>`, `"`, `|`, `?`, `*` and control characters in the data set's name as `-`, and adds `-2`, `-3`… to a name an earlier data set used.
  - Export for Screens: the dialog's Example line shows the path of the file the export writes first, sub-folder included, named as the export names it, for the first chosen artboard, asset, layer or object (`document.exportForScreens`).
  - Save for Web: Preview in Browser writes each preview's page and images to a folder of its own inside `VectorCraft Save for Web` in the system's temporary folder. A later preview, from the same app or another one running, does not overwrite an earlier one. Each preview first removes the preview folders there that are an hour old or older and, on Linux, macOS and FreeBSD, belong to the current user; it leaves other files and folders alone. The folders a preview makes there are open to their owner only on those systems. When `VectorCraft Save for Web` is a link or is not a folder, or on those systems belongs to another user or can be written by other users, the preview goes to a new folder of its own in the temporary folder, which a later preview removes once it is an hour old (`file.saveForWeb.browser`).
  - Export for Screens, Save for Web (slice images, and files named after the document's title) and the Libraries panel name files with the characters Windows does not allow written as `-` and with a `-` after a Windows device name such as `CON`, on every platform (`document.exportForScreens`, `document.exportForWeb`, `library.create`).
  - Variables (data merge): text, visibility and image variables bound to objects (an object may carry several), dataset rows applied in one undo step (`variable.*`, `dataset.*`) from a Variables panel and Window › Variables, with dialogs to define, bind and edit, Make Text/Visibility/Image Dynamic, Capture/Update Data Set, CSV import/export (`dataset.import` / `dataset.export`), and a row in italics when an edit leaves the art not matching it; an image dataset value is a file path and apply keeps the object's bounds; bindings let go of deleted art and locked art is left alone; every command, like the rest, is drivable over MCP and the CLI.
  - Variables: Import Data Sets… (`dataset.import`) reads tab-separated files as well as comma-separated ones, and files without a `name` column, whose rows take the first free names Data Set 1, Data Set 2 and so on. An import error about a row's values or name gives the file line the row starts on.
  - Variables: Import Data Sets… (`dataset.import`) defines the variables a file's header names that the document lacks, unbound. `#Shown` defines a visibility variable, `@Photo` defines an image variable, and a header without a prefix defines a text variable. A header that is a variable's exact name keeps naming it, and any other `%` header (graph data files) is refused.
  - Variables: Load Variable Library… in the Variables panel menu (`variable.loadLibrary`) replaces the document's variables and data sets with a variable library's, read from its XML file, in one undo step: every variable is deleted with its bindings and values, and every data set is deleted; then the library's text variables are defined, unbound, and its data sets take the text of each value's `p` elements, one paragraph each. Variables of other kinds are left out with a warning that names their kinds.
  - JSON-lines control channel with real egui pointer and keyboard injection.
  - Synthetic input validates complete gestures before queue mutation: at most 256 drag steps, 16 clicks and 1,024 pending events; up to 64 control requests per frame, with later requests retained for the next frame (#1709).
  - The control server writes each reply through a 64 KiB buffer. On Windows 11 it sends the 17 MB `document.inspect` reply of a document with 50,000 objects on one layer to a client over loopback in 0.09 s instead of 34 s.
  - MCP server with 25 tools (drawing, text, effects, Pathfinder, transforms, graphs, text wrap, export, screenshots, any command), attached to the running app or headless. Tool descriptions and replies agree with the engine: format lists come from its format table, `save_file` says it keeps the document's own format, `inspect_document` reports the paint type's characters show, and selection exports report the encoder's warnings. `--automation-read-root` / `--automation-write-root` (on `vectorcraft-cli mcp` and on `vectorcraft --control`) confine the files commands read and write to chosen folders, links followed, with the flags PhotoCraft takes (#832); each flag may be given more than once, a path inside any of its folders being allowed (#3546, `file_access::tests::several_roots_of_a_kind_each_grant_their_access`, `cli::mcp_automation_roots_take_several_folders`). A long export can be cancelled (`notifications/cancelled` stops it at the next page or group and writes nothing), reports page progress to a client that sent a progress token, and does not make other requests wait: engine-free ones answer at once, the rest are refused as busy after two seconds (#2165, #2171, #2172).
  - MCP protocol: five prompts (`prompts/list` / `prompts/get`: poster, icon set, recolour, trace-and-style, export set), `completion/complete` for prompt arguments and template variables read from the live catalogues (formats, effect ids, command ids, trace presets, swatch and object ids), four resource templates (`vectorcraft://object/{id}`, `//command/{id}`, `//effect/{id}`, `//swatch/{name}`) so an agent reads one thing instead of the whole document, and `logging/setLevel` with `notifications/message`. `window.panel` ids are case-insensitive (display labels work too), `vectorcraft://object/{id}` reads through `document.node {summary: true}` (the same reply bytes from one lookup instead of summarizing the whole document: a leaf read on a 2,000-object document drops from ~20 ms to ~0.06 ms), large containers slice with `document.node {depth?, childLimit?}` (truncated levels report `childCount`), `document.inspect` and the `inspect_document` tool slice the same way so a depth-0 read is the layer skeleton (~9.7 KB instead of ~2 MB on a 2,000-object document), `document.find` locates nodes by name/kind/text with ancestor paths, and the CLI sweeps the protocol surface over stdio against the compiled binary. `docs/mcp.md` has a Protocol section covering the capability table and what is deliberately absent (subscriptions, progress, cancellation, sampling, elicitation, Streamable HTTP — all of which need the transport to interleave reads).
  - Headless CLI (`vectorcraft-cli run`, `convert`, `info`, `bench`, `perf`, `mcp`). A `run` step, like a `command_batch` step over MCP, can use an earlier step's result (`"$1.id"`, #785); `run --commands FILE` (or `-` for standard input) reads the steps from a JSON array or JSON Lines, past the Windows command-line limit (#3147, `apps/vectorcraft-cli/tests/it/cli.rs` `run_reads_*`, `run_refuses_malformed_commands_naming_the_step`).
  - File › Scripts › Check Script… reads a script written for Illustrator (`.jsx`, `.jsxinc` or a compiled `.jsxbin`) without running any of it and reports what it needs (the document model, files, dialogs, menu commands, features only Illustrator has), what it would do outside the document, the menu commands and document-model members it uses, its directives and included files, and the problems that would stop it loading (`script.check`, which also reads `.js` files); File › Open and drag-and-drop show the report for `.jsx`, `.jsxinc` and `.jsxbin` files.
- **UI:** Illustrator 2026 layout restyled to measured values:
  - Medium Dark theme, categorized and Advanced toolbars (a tool group's flyout opens on a right press, a long press or a press on its corner triangle), 35 pt document tabs, 33 pt panel tabs.
  - Hint bar, contextual task bar, 19 dock panels with ≡ menus.
  - Window › SVG Interactivity attaches JavaScript to the selected objects' events (`onclick`, `onmouseover` and 17 more) and links JavaScript files to the document (Link JavaScript Files…); SVG export writes the events as event attributes and the files as `<script xlink:href>`, SVG import reads both back as text without running them, and the native format keeps them (`svgInteractivity.*`).
  - Numeric fields keep the pointer's pressed character as the text-drag start when movement exceeds the click threshold (#1326, in part); a completed focus click selects the unit too. Pixel/point, plain and optional fields are regression-tested in both directions, before/after focus, with replacement text; keyboard focus, double-click, arrows and wheel keep their prior behavior. Native egui input confirms partial replacement gives 17 px instead of 700 px, one Undo/Redo, window captures and an exact saved-document read in a separate CLI process. Short movements still counted as clicks can select all; that case remains open.
  - Unit fields and length strings take `%` in arithmetic: `3cm*50%` reads as 1.5 cm, and `50pt+25%` reads as 62.5 pt.
  - The contextual task bar's handle drags it anywhere on the canvas (kept whole on it as the window resizes); unpinned it keeps that offset as it follows the selection, and its More Options menu hides it, pins its position across selection changes (`window.taskBar.pin`), resets it under the selection (`window.taskBar.reset`) and shows the Properties panel. As in Illustrator the position isn't kept across launches. Not done: the bar's variants for other tools (only the selection tools and the Artboard tool show it).
  - With one image selected, the contextual task bar offers Image Trace, which traces the image at once with the Default preset (the Image Trace panel is left as it was), and Crop Image; with an Image Trace object it offers Expand, which keeps only the traced paths. This follows Illustrator's bar: for a selected image it includes Image Trace, Retype and Crop Image, and traced artwork can be expanded from it ([Contextual Task Bar announcement](https://community.adobe.com/announcements-651/contextual-task-bar-in-illustrator-2025-quick-actions-when-you-need-them-1546580)). Offset Path and Simplify, which don't apply to an image, aren't offered for one. Not done: Retype, which the app doesn't have.
  - With the Artboard tool, the contextual task bar sits under the selected artboards and offers Resize (Artboard Options for the active artboard), Duplicate (each selected artboard, in one undo step, the copies then selected), Rearrange All (with two or more artboards) and Export (Export for Screens with the selected artboards checked). This follows Illustrator's bar: while the Artboard tool is in use, it has options for resizing, duplicating and exporting artboards (the [Contextual Task Bar announcement](https://community.adobe.com/questions-652/contextual-task-bar-in-illustrator-2025-quick-actions-when-you-need-them-1546580); Rearrange and Export on the bar: [Managing Artboards in Illustrator](https://creativepro.com/managing-artboards-in-illustrator/)).
  - The contextual task bar offers more next steps by selection (<https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/get-started/learn-the-basics/contextual-task-bar-overview.html>): an open path Join and Edit Path (the Direct Selection tool), a closed path Edit Path, a compound path Edit Path and Release Compound Path, a clipping group Edit Clipping Path and Release Clipping Mask instead of Ungroup and Isolate, an image selected with vector art Make Clipping Mask instead of Unite, and point or area type Convert To Area Type or Convert To Point Type beside Create Outlines. Evidence: `crates/ui-egui/src/tests_taskbar.rs`.
  - With anchor points selected with Direct Selection, the contextual task bar offers Remove Anchor Points, Connect (`path.join`), Cut Path, Corner and Smooth (`path.convertAnchors` with `to` set to `corner` or `smooth`), the commands of the Control bar's anchor buttons. As in Illustrator ("Remove selected anchor points, Connect selected end points, Cut path at selected anchor points, Convert selected anchor points to corner, and Convert selected anchor points to smooth": [Contextual Task Bar overview](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/get-started/learn-the-basics/contextual-task-bar-overview.html)). Not done: Simplify, which the bar offers only while no anchors are selected, and the bar's Smooth item that adjusts a path's curvature, a command the app doesn't have (Object › Path › Smooth).
  - Tool flyouts tear off: dragging or clicking the tear-off bar on a flyout's right side (or releasing the long press over it) floats its group as a strip of tool buttons, moved by the same bar and put back in the toolbar by the × at its top (`window.floatTools`). While a group floats, the presses that would open its flyout raise the strip instead. Floating strips are kept with the preferences and in user workspaces. Not done: turning a strip vertical, docking it.
  - Screen readers get a name for the Tools panel's tool buttons, flyout rows, floating strips and tear-off bars, and for the icon buttons, text buttons, toggles, checkboxes, radio buttons, tabs, chips, sliders, angle dials and combo boxes that panels and dialogs draw with `crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs`: the text, label or tool tip each one shows, or a name of its own where it shows none (the angle dial, the spinner, the preset arrow, the color wheel and the Reference Point's squares). The tool buttons, toggles, checkboxes, radio buttons, tabs and the Reference Point's nine squares also report whether they are on, an icon button that is lit, such as the chosen Align To button, reports that it is pressed, and the angle dial reports its angle. The status bar's First, Previous, Next and Last Artboard buttons have tool tips.
  - These dialog sliders, each beside a number field, respond to the keyboard: those of the effect, tool option, brush and transform dialogs, the Perspective Grid, the 3D dialogs, and the flattener options, which the Flattener Preview panel also shows. A click, or Tab, gives a slider the keyboard focus, and an outline shows it. Then → and ↑ step the field's number up to the next whole number and ← and ↓ step it down to the next whole number, Shift with an arrow and Page Up and Page Down step it by ten, and Home and End set the slider's first and last value; no step goes past either end. Screen readers' increment and decrement actions step the slider as → and ← do. The Color panel's, Swatch Options', the Navigator's and the Character panel's sliders, and the Color Picker's channel slider, respond only to the pointer. The keys follow the WAI-ARIA slider pattern (<https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/slider/>); the reference app's help does not describe keys on a dialog's slider, so the step sizes are VectorCraft's own.
  - Screen readers get the value of the color and channel sliders that panels and dialogs draw (the Color panel, the Color Picker, Swatch Options, the Navigator's Zoom, the Character panel's variable font axes, the Perspective Grid and flattener options, and the sliders of the effect, tool option and transform dialogs): the number and text of the field beside each one, such as 128 for G or 50% for an opacity, with the slider's range, which extends to include a number past the slider's end. The harmony wheel's Brightness slider, which has no field, reports its brightness in percent.
  - Panels undock (#495): a dock tab, a panel icon or a popped-out panel's title dragged out of the dock floats that panel inside the window, and the strip right of the dock's tabs floats the whole tabbed group. A floating group moves by its title bar, a tab dragged out of it floats on its own, and dropped on another group's title bar or tabs it stacks with that group; dropped on a dock group's tabs, which light up under the pointer, its panels join that group, and on the group's upper or lower half they make a new group above or below it (`window.panel.dock {anchor, zone}`); dropped on the icon column they become icons there, the tabbed group's panels too (`window.panel.dock {icon: true}`); dropped anywhere else on the dock, which lights up, they go back where they live (the tabbed group or the icon column), as its × and the panel menus' Float Panel / Dock Panel do (`window.panel.float`, `window.panel.dock`). The Tools panel floats by its title bar and docks again on the window's left edge. Floating groups stack into sets: dropped on the upper or lower half of another group (a line shows where), a group joins it right above or below it, and the set's groups stack top to bottom, each showing one panel, moving together by the top group's title bar, whose × docks them all; a group dragged by its tab strip leaves the set (`window.panel.float {below, above}`). A double-click on a tab collapses a floating group to its tabs (`collapsed`), and a dock group too, a group below it moving up into the room; a second double-click, or a click on another of its tabs, expands it (`window.panel.collapse`, kept with the preferences and in saved workspaces). Sets dropped on the left edge of the icon column or of another dock column dock as dock columns (a multi-column dock, `window.panel.dock {column}`), whose groups stack, tab and tear out as a floating set's do, and whose top strip floats the column again. Floating panels, their sets and the Tools panel's position are kept with the preferences and in user workspaces, and clamped into a smaller window. Not done: panels in separate OS windows, reordering tabs by dragging, collapsing a set or dock column to icons, dock columns right of the default dock, resizing floating panels and the groups of a set.
  - The dock's double arrow collapses Properties, Layers and Libraries to icons at the top of the icon column, popping out like the other icon panels, and expands them again (`window.collapseDock`, kept with the preferences and in saved workspaces). The icon column's own arrow (expanding the icon panels into a full column) is not done.
  - Czech render-site labels: desktop/web file filters, diagnostics, suggested preset names and contributor tooltips/plurals now use catalog lookups; gradients have Czech adjective agreement and printer marks have a separate context (PDF/Print and Summary). Search, Home, toolbar/panel tooltips and Preferences already look up their labels. Every complete catalog has rows for these labels and for the Roman and Japanese printer mark styles. Evidence: `i18n::tests::czech_render_site_follow_up`, `i18n::tests::complete_catalogs_translate_render_site_labels`, `dialogs::tests_modal::printer_mark_labels_are_distinct_from_language_names`; see [localization-parity.md](localization-parity.md).
  - The History panel, Edit › Undo and Edit › Redo translate the names of the steps that apply or redefine a character or paragraph style and of the step that redefines a graphic style: each such step keeps its template (`Apply {name}`, `Redefine {name}`, `Redefine Graphic Style “{name}”`) and the style's name, every complete catalog has a row for each template, and the panel and the menu show the style's name as the document holds it, except the Normal styles' names, which they show in the interface language (`steps_named_after_a_style_list_the_template_around_the_name`, `undo_and_redo_name_a_style_step_around_the_style_name`).
  - Localised UI: menus (in-window and native), panels, dialogs, toolbar and Preferences read from per-language catalogs (`crates/ui-egui/src/i18n`, see `docs/development.md`); Traditional Chinese (Taiwan), Simplified Chinese (mainland), Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Polish, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Ukrainian and Georgian ship complete, and Czech covers every menu label (and more), with system-locale detection on macOS, Windows, Linux and the web (the browser's languages, or `?lang=`), a Language preference and, on macOS, a VectorCraft ▸ Language menu. Names are never translated (fonts and their styles, layers, artboards, saved presets, user libraries, custom workspaces, recent files, plug-ins).
  - Edit › Undo and Edit › Redo, in the in-window and native menus, name the step in the interface language as the History panel lists it (`panels::history::step_name`), so when the catalog has no plain row for a step named after an effect, such as Feather, the menu shows the translation of the effect's menu row without its ellipsis (`undo_and_redo_name_the_step_as_the_history_panel_does`).
  - The History panel translates the undo step names the engine, the tools and the shell write as literals: the untranslated report (`untranslated_report`) lists any a complete catalog lacks, and a step whose catalog row exists only with an ellipsis (such as an effect's menu name) shows that row without the ellipsis.
  - The History panel menu has Step Backward and Step Forward, which run Edit › Undo and Edit › Redo and are disabled when there is no step to undo or redo, and Set History Limit…, which opens Preferences at Performance, where History States is set. Not done: a new document from the selected state.
  - The History panel menu's Clear History (`edit.clearHistory`) removes every step to undo and to redo and leaves the document as it is; it is not an undo step itself, and it is disabled when there is no step to clear.
  - Native macOS menu bar, vector tool cursors, a ⌘K command palette, middle-button panning with any tool. Native menus explicitly end tracking on command selection, outside window presses and Escape; menu updates wait until tracking ends, and a dismissing press never starts a canvas gesture (M14.8).
  - The errors of the blend spine commands (Move Spine Point, Reshape Spine Segment, Add Spine Point and Delete Spine Point) show in the status bar in the interface language: each has a row in every catalog that translates all status and error messages and in Bulgarian (`blend_spine_param_errors_are_translated`).
  - The errors of the parameter checks that many commands share show in the status bar in the interface language: a value that is not a number where a number goes (`object.move` with `"dx": "60 mm"`, and `object.rotate`, `object.setBounds` and the other commands that call `check_numbers`), a missing number or index, `ids` that are not a list of object ids, an object id that is not a non-negative integer or names no object, and a date that is not Unix seconds. Each has a row in every catalog that translates all status and error messages, and in Bulgarian, Danish, Indonesian and Dutch (`shared_param_check_errors_are_translated`).
  - An EPS or PostScript file that stops on a PostScript error gives the error's name as PostScript spells it (`typecheck`, `rangecheck` and the other names the reader raises, except `undefined`, whose message names the unknown name) followed by what it means, in the warning after opening and in the error when the file can't be opened. The status bar and the open-error dialog show the meaning in the interface language: each meaning has a row in every catalog (`postscript_error_meanings_are_translated`).
  - The macOS menu bar is built from the in-window menus (one model, `native_menu`) and laid out as a Mac app's: the VectorCraft menu holds About, Settings ▸ (each Preferences page, General… ⌘K), Language ▸, Appearance ▸ (UI brightness), Services, Hide VectorCraft ⌃⌘H (⌘H stays Hide Edges), Hide Others, Show All and Quit; Window gains Minimize ⌃⌘M, Zoom and Bring All to Front, and Help the system's search field. Its key equivalents go back to egui as key presses, so user shortcuts, focused text fields and the Type tool's input method behave as in the window, and nothing fires twice; enabled, check marks and labels update in place. `--in-window-menus` or `VECTORCRAFT_IN_WINDOW_MENUS=1` keeps the menus in the window; `ui.inspect` reports `nativeMenuBar`.
  - macOS: Finder opens every format File › Open reads with VectorCraft (double-click, Open With, a drop on the Dock icon, `open -a`), at launch or while it runs; the release and `cargo xtask bundle` apps share one `Info.plist` that declares those document types, owning only VectorCraft's own formats. The DMG opens on a designed Finder window, VectorCraft.app beside the `Applications` link over a background with the app icon (#493).
  - Swatch and graphic style libraries, Libraries panel files, presets and plug-ins open wherever they are dropped on the window, as File › Open opens them.
  - **Symbol libraries** ([public source](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/manage-objects/traces-mockups-symbols/create-or-import-symbol-libraries.html)): Window › Symbol Libraries and the Symbols panel's Symbol Libraries Menu open each library in a library panel of its own, as swatch and graphic style libraries do. The built-in library, Basic Shapes, is original art generated in code (`crates/engine/src/cmd/symbollib.rs`). A click on a symbol adds it to the document's Symbols as one undo step, with its Symbol Options (size, registration, export type, 9-slice guides) and every resource it uses (the symbols it nests, patterns, swatches, brushes, graphic styles, images), and makes it the current symbol; a symbol the document already has is not added again and another symbol of the same name keeps its name, the library's comes in numbered. Thumbnails, in the library panels and the Symbols panel, draw a symbol with the symbols it nests and the patterns and images it uses. Dragging a library symbol onto the canvas also places an instance there, in the same step ([placing from a library](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/manage-objects/traces-mockups-symbols/create-and-place-symbols.html)). Save Symbols (the library menu) and Save Symbol Library… (the Symbols panel menu) write the document's symbols as a `.vectorcraft` document holding only them, into the user library folder (listed under User Defined) or a file; Other Library… reads the symbols of any document VectorCraft opens; a file it can't read is an error and opens no panel.   - A canvas context menu: right-click selects the object under the pointer and lists what applies to the selection (Undo/Redo, clipboard, group, isolation, join, Remove Anchor Points when anchors are selected, masks, compound paths, guides, Transform, Arrange, Select, Export Selection), or the view commands on empty canvas.

The submenu lists up to 20 locked objects under the pointer, topmost first, by the name the Layers panel shows, and choosing one unlocks it (`layer.setProps`). A locked group is listed as one item. Objects on hidden, locked or template layers are not listed.

Then Guides & Grid › Gridline every and Subdivisions (changing either sets the grid of every open document; new and opened documents take that grid too, except a native file and the native document an SVG, PDF, `.ai` or EPS file carries, which open with the grid they were saved with; `file.new`, `document.open`, `file.newFromTemplate`, `file.revert`, #394). About 14 stored options still do nothing yet (the rest of #394: East Asian Type units, Open Documents As Tabs, Real-time Drawing and Editing, GPU Performance beyond Animated Zoom, hyphenation language, scratch disks, the legacy clipboard, Touch Workspace).
  - Preferences that act (#394, in part): Show Tool Tips, Double Click To Isolate, Zoom with Mouse Wheel (the wheel zooms about the pointer, Shift-wheel scrolls up and down, Cmd/Ctrl-wheel sideways; Alt/Option-wheel and a trackpad pinch zoom about the pointer either way), Use Precise Cursors; Selection & Anchor Display › Tolerance (objects, anchors and handles), Object Selection by Path Only, Command Click to Select Objects Behind (cycling down the stack), Zoom to Selection, anchor Size, Highlight anchors on mouse over; Type › Number of Recent Fonts (up to 15); Guides & Grid › guide and grid Color and Style (lines or dots) and Grids In Back. Then Snap to Point (its distance, for moves, drawn points and reference points), Move Locked and Hidden Artwork with Artboard, Enable Rubber Band for the Pen and Curvature tools, Handles style, Show handles when multiple anchors are selected, Hide Corner Widget for angles greater than; General › Transform Pattern Tiles (the transforms' and dialogs' Transform Patterns, Align and Distribute, art moved or duplicated with an artboard, and objects moved whole with direct-selected anchors) and Select Same Tint %; Type › Size/Leading, Tracking and Baseline Shift increments (`type.step`, Cmd+Shift+. and Cmd+Shift+, for the size, the Type tool's Alt+arrows), Enable Missing Glyph Protection and Fill New Type Objects With Placeholder Text. Then Smart Guides › Color, Alignment Guides, Anchor/Path Labels, Measurement Labels, Transform Tools, Object Highlighting (with Smart Guides on) and Snapping Tolerance (4 px by default, for every smart guide snap), then Construction Guides and their Angles (#506: a drawn point near a line at one of those angles through the point it leaves from lands on it). Then Type › Type Object Selection by Path Only (type is picked on the baseline of any of its lines, area type's frame or the path of type on a path, no longer anywhere in its bounds; the Type tools and the Eyedropper still take a click among the characters). Then General › Anti-aliased Artwork (off, the canvas draws the art with hard edges). Then Guides & Grid › Show Pixel Grid (Above 600% Zoom), a line at every document pixel over the art in Pixel Preview, turning with a rotated view as the document grid now does too. Then General › Show The Home Screen When No Documents Are Open (off, closing the last document leaves an empty window; the Home button still opens the screen). Then Units › Numbers Without Units Are Points (on by default: a number typed with no unit into a field in picas is read in points, a typed unit still wins; dimmed unless a unit is Picas). Then User Interface › Auto-Collapse Iconic Panels (off by default: on, a click away from a panel popped out of the icon column puts it away). Then Performance › Animated Zoom (on, with GPU Performance, which it needs and which dims it when off: the Zoom tool dragged sideways zooms about the press, right in and left out, and held still zooms on, Alt out; off, a drag zooms to the area dragged across, now drawn as a marquee), User Interface › Large Tabs (taller document tabs) and Scale Cursor Proportional to UI (off, the tool cursors keep their size whatever the UI Scaling), and File Handling › Display Bitmaps as Anti-aliased Images in Pixel Preview (off by default: Pixel Preview draws images with each pixel taking its nearest image pixel). Type › Auto Size New Area Type works too (new area type gets Auto Size). They reach agents too (`prefs.set`, then `pointer_gesture` or `press_key`; `ui.wheel` on the control channel). Then Smart Guides › Spacing Guides (moves space the selection evenly with its row or column, see Drawing aids). Then Hyphenation › Exceptions (comma-separated words that never break, or break only at their hyphens; `prefs.set` and restore push them into the hyphenator, #394). Then Type › Show Font Names in English (off, font menus label a family by its native-language name when the font has one; documents still use the English family, #394). Then General › Display Print Size at 100% Zoom (off by default: View › Actual Size is one document point per screen point; on, one document inch fills 96 screen points, an inch at the reference density display scaling is set against; `view.actualSize` / `prefs.set`, #394). Then Guides & Grid › Gridline every and Subdivisions (changing either sets the grid of every open document; new and opened documents take that grid too, except a native file and the native document an SVG, PDF, `.ai` or EPS file carries, which open with the grid they were saved with; `file.new`, `document.open`, `file.newFromTemplate`, `file.revert`, #394). Then Appearance of Black › On Screen (Display All Blacks Accurately by default: pure CMYK black shows through the CMYK profile, a dark grey; Display All Blacks as Rich Black shows it on the canvas as RGB black, also in CMYK documents drawn by ink planes, while rich blacks, black tints and images show as before; `RenderOptions::rich_black`, #394). Then Appearance of Black › Printing / Exporting (Output All Blacks Accurately by default; Output All Blacks as Rich Black draws pure CMYK black as RGB black in RGB raster exports and Print as Bitmap; CMYK ink exports and the document stay unchanged; `prefs.blackOutput` / `richBlack`, #394). Then Units › Identify Objects By (Object Name by default: Layers, Variables and Layer Options show and edit free names; XML ID shows and edits AI-style XML ids, `_` for a space and `_xHH_` escapes, and `layer.setProps` / rename refuse invalid ids; the document still stores the object name, #394). Then Type › Highlight Alternate Glyphs (on by default: pink behind OpenType substitutions on screen — ligatures, contextual forms; Document Setup's Highlight Substituted Fonts / Glyphs stay separate; `prefs.set`, #394). About 14 stored options still do nothing yet (the rest of #394: East Asian Type units, Open Documents As Tabs, Real-time Drawing and Editing, GPU Performance beyond Animated Zoom, hyphenation language, scratch disks, the legacy clipboard, Touch Workspace).

About 15 stored options still do nothing yet (the rest of #394: Highlight Alternate Glyphs, East Asian Type units, Open Documents As Tabs, Real-time Drawing and Editing, GPU Performance beyond Animated Zoom, hyphenation language, scratch disks, the legacy clipboard, Touch Workspace).
  - Dialogs move by dragging their heading (the band down from the top edge, as a title bar), stay on screen and keep where they were moved for the session; the form dialogs' choices are dropdowns (Offset Path's Joins, Average's and Shear's and Reflect's axis), and Offset Path lists Offset, Joins, Miter Limit and previews (#423).
  - Dialogs open with their first field focused and its value selected: type a value and press Enter (Move, Rotate, Scale…). A dialog opened from a menu takes the keyboard focus every time it opens, not only the first (#1367), and one whose first field starts greyed out (Blend Options on Smooth Color, Layers Panel Options) gives the focus to that field once it is enabled (#1395). Number fields in panels, the Control bar and dialogs (preferences too) step with Up/Down, or with the mouse wheel over the focused field (#485: a notch a step; the panel under it then stays put, and an unfocused field leaves the wheel to scrolling) (Shift: ten, Ctrl/Cmd: a tenth of their unit), applied at once.
  - A plain step of a number field (Up/Down or a wheel notch) goes to the next whole unit in its direction and a Ctrl/Cmd step goes to the next tenth, so 5.1 mm steps up to 6 mm and down to 5 mm (#2881). A Shift step adds or takes ten and keeps the fraction.
  - In the number, text and color fields of the panels and the Control bar, Shift+Enter (Shift+Return) applies the value and keeps the field active with its value selected; a text box of several lines takes it as a line break. In a dialog, Shift+Enter applies the value and confirms the dialog, as Enter does.
  - The Pattern Options panel's Name field and the name fields that a double-click opens in the Layers, Artboards and Asset Export panels take Shift+Enter (Shift+Return) the same way: it applies the name and keeps the field active with the name selected.
  - Scrubby labels (#400, beyond Illustrator, as in Photoshop): dragging a numeric field's label left or right (the ↔ cursor shows over it) steps the value one unit every 2 points (Shift: ten, Ctrl/Cmd: a tenth; counts stay whole), in the field's unit and within its limits, applied live as the art follows; the whole drag is one undo step and Escape puts the value back. A click on the label focuses the field; the text box itself never scrubs, and a field with no label doesn't. Text labels before a field (Transform, Properties, Control bar, Stroke, Transparency, form rows in dialogs) and the Character and Paragraph panels' icons act as labels. Preferences › General › Scrub Numeric Fields by Dragging (on by default) turns it off.
  - In the Transform panel, the Properties panel's Transform section and the Control bar, Alt+Enter (Option+Return) applies a value to a copy of the selection and selects the copy, in one undo step. With anchor points selected with Direct Selection it applies the value to them, as Enter does. Ctrl/Cmd+Enter in W or H applies the value and scales the selection proportionally with the link off. With the Artboard tool, it scales the active artboard proportionally. A percentage typed alone in W or H (`50%`) is that share of the size the field shows, and the link and Ctrl/Cmd+Enter keep the proportions as with a length (#2401).
  - The Control bar's underlined Transform link opens the Transform panel in a popover under it (reference point, X/Y/W/H, Rotate and Shear with their icons and angle presets, flips, shape properties, Scale Corners and Scale Strokes & Effects), as its Stroke link does the Stroke panel; X/Y/W/H also show inline while the bar has room. The reference point locator is nine squares, the outer eight joined around the box.
  - In isolation mode the Control bar has an Exit Isolation Mode button (`object.exitIsolation`), except while a pattern is edited. Outside isolation mode, with one group, compound path, path, image, mesh or placed file selected, it has an Isolate Selected Object button (`object.isolate`), which also isolates a path inside a group that Direct Selection selected.
  - Tab shows and hides the panels (in the Type tool it types a tab) without moving the keyboard focus onto a field, so the next shortcut or letter still works; in dialogs and panel fields it moves between fields.
  - Shift+Tab (`window.panels`) shows and hides the dock and the floating panels and leaves the toolbar and the Control bar as they are; hiding the panels with Tab or Shift+Tab also closes a panel popped out of the icon column.
  - The second Tab (`window.dock`) shows again only the bars the first Tab hid, after a restart too: a Control bar that was off stays off, a toolbar hidden with Window › Tools stays hidden, and panels shown with Shift+Tab in between stay shown.
  - Cmd/Ctrl+A follows the keyboard: in a panel, dialog or search field it selects the field's text, while the Type tool edits it selects all of that text (also `select.all` over MCP), and only otherwise every object. On macOS the menu bar's Select All, Cut, Copy and Paste (keys or clicks) act on a focused field too, and elsewhere the in-window menus' do: the field that had the keyboard when the menu opened gets them, with its selection, and the keyboard back (#516). Not yet: Select All across threaded frames (one frame's text is selected).
  - While the Type tool edits text, a character typed with AltGr is typed and runs no command. Firefox on Windows reports AltGr as Ctrl and Alt held, so in the web build AltGr+L (ł on a Polish layout) does not also open Layer Options for a new layer, and AltGr+Q (@ on a German layout) does not also run Reset Tracking and Kerning. A Ctrl+Alt chord that types no character runs its command.
  - With the Artboard tool, Cmd/Ctrl+A after a click on a row of the Artboards panel selects every artboard, as the macOS menu bar's Select All does then; the active artboard stays active, and the art's selection does not change. After a press outside the panel's list, Cmd/Ctrl+A selects every object again. It used to select every object after a click in the panel too. Public reference: [Select artboards](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/create-manage-artboards/add-edit-artboards/select-artboards.html).
  - Cmd/Ctrl+/ (`appearance.addFill`) and Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+/ (`appearance.addStroke`) add a new fill and a new stroke to the selected objects, as the Appearance panel's Add New Fill and Add New Stroke buttons do, on the keys the reference app's [Default keyboard shortcuts](https://web.archive.org/web/20260726060015/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/default-keyboard-shortcuts.html) page lists for adding a new fill and a new stroke. Keyboard Shortcuts lists both under Window › Appearance.
  - Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+Shift+. and , (`type.size.increaseByFive`, `type.size.decreaseByFive`) step the font size of the selected type, or of the text the Type tool has selected, by five times the Size/Leading increment (Preferences › Type); Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+. and , still step it by one increment.
  - Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+Q (`type.resetTracking`) sets the tracking of the selected type, or of the text the Type tool has selected, to 0 and its kerning to Auto (0 in the Character panel), in one undo step; at a caret it resets the kerning of the character before it.
  - Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+L (`ui.newLayer`) opens Layer Options for a new layer, as an Alt-click on the Layers panel's New Layer button does, on the key the reference app's [Default keyboard shortcuts](https://web.archive.org/web/20260726060015/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/default-keyboard-shortcuts.html) page lists for adding a layer through the New Layer dialog box. OK adds the layer above the current layer, and Cancel adds none. Cmd/Ctrl+L still adds a layer without the dialog.
  - F8 (`ui.symbolOptions`) opens Symbol Options for a new symbol made from the selection, as the Symbols panel's New Symbol button does, on the key the reference app's [Default keyboard shortcuts](https://web.archive.org/web/20260726060015/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/default-keyboard-shortcuts.html) page lists for making a new symbol. OK makes the symbol and puts an instance of it in place of the art, and Cancel makes none. With nothing selected, F8 opens no dialog, and the status bar says that nothing is selected. Shift+F8 and Cmd/Ctrl+F8 still show the Transform and Info panels.
  - Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+X (`type.resetHorizontalScale`) sets the horizontal scale of the selected type, or of the text the Type tool has selected, to 100% as the Character panel shows it (the object's own stretch included), in one undo step; at a caret it leaves the text as it is.
  - Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+N (`file.newWithoutDialog`) makes a document without opening the New Document dialog, on the key the reference app's [Default keyboard shortcuts](https://web.archive.org/web/20260726060015/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/default-keyboard-shortcuts.html) page lists for making a new document with no New Document dialog box. The page does not say which settings the document gets. VectorCraft gives it the settings the dialog opens on (the first Recent entry, or the Print category's Letter while Recent is empty) and the next untitled name.
  - Shortcut sets other apps save as text (`.kys`) open in Import Shortcut Set from File › Open, from Edit › Keyboard Shortcuts › Import… in the desktop app, or from a drop on the window. It matches each entry to a tool, command or panel by name and decodes the file's key and modifier codes where VectorCraft's default shortcuts agree on them; the user answers the rest, and Apply fills the Keyboard Shortcuts dialog's working set. The answers are kept with the preferences for the next import (`shortcutSet.read`, `importMatches.*`).
  - On Windows and Linux the app bar is the window's title bar (its own minimize, maximize and close buttons, drag to move, edges to resize), with the dragon app icon as the brand mark; dialogs and menus size to their content. As on a native menu bar, once one menu is open, moving the pointer onto another title opens that one.
- **Tools:**
  - **Shaper:** uneven squares and rectangles become live rectangles even when drawing begins mid-edge. Recognition uses uniformly spaced samples and closed-loop corners, fits rectangle edges/angles rather than requiring a nearly perfect bounding-box fill, and includes the pointer-release position. Rectangles/squares and ellipses snap to 45° steps, hexagons to 90°, and triangles point up or down; lines keep their free angle even with Shift. Shaper Groups retain the live originals, merge regions with the gesture-origin fill, punch fills independently from strokes, remove boundaries on exiting scribbles and trim protruding stroke pieces. Source moves/resizes re-evaluate the result in the same undo step; double-click enters construction editing, and with the Shaper or Selection tool a click on the arrow widget beside a Shaper Group's original shapes switches the group between Face Selection and Construction mode. Native save/reopen, face recoloring, Release and Expand are covered. Finer gesture heuristics remain.
  - **Selection:** Selection, Direct/Group Selection, Magic Wand, Lasso. A Shift-drag marquee toggles what it reaches: objects with the Selection tool, anchors with Direct and Group Selection (#483); the Lasso adds with Shift and subtracts with Alt. Dragging a path segment with Direct Selection bends it when it's curved (its anchors stay) and moves its two anchors when it's straight, one undo step; the fill, Shift or Alt still pick the whole path (Alt-drag copies it).
    With the Selection or Group Selection tool, pressing E while dragging a marquee makes the marquee select only the objects that lie entirely inside it. Pressing E again switches the marquee back to its default selection.
    The Lasso picks anchor points only on art a click can pick, and the Add Anchor Point, Delete Anchor Point, Anchor Point and Scissors tools pick anchor points and segments only on the selected paths and on art a click can pick: not on a Shaper Group's original shapes outside Construction mode, and in isolation mode only inside the isolated group or object. Smart Guides and Snap to Point do not snap to a Shaper Group's original shapes, and the reference point of the transform tools snaps to one only when it is selected, or under the pointer in Construction mode.
    A marquee selects a clip group, or an object on a layer with a clipping mask, only when it reaches the area inside the clipping path, and it measures the art only within that path's bounds. Within the bounds of a mask that is not a rectangle, it can still select art that the mask hides. Direct Selection's marquee still selects the hidden anchor points inside it (#2345).
    A marquee selects a Shaper Group only when it reaches the art the group shows, not the original shapes kept under it, and Direct Selection's clicks and marquee do not select those shapes' anchor points. In Construction mode a marquee selects the original shapes, and Direct Selection selects their anchor points.
    A marquee selects an Intertwine group only when it reaches one of the group's members, as for a plain group, and it selects a repeat only when it reaches one of the copies the repeat draws. Direct and Group Selection's marquees select the anchor points of an Intertwine group's members, not the group, and Group Selection's E marquee selects the members inside it.
    A key object needs another selected object outside it. A Shift-click or any other change that leaves one object selected clears the key, and `select.key` sets none on one object or on a group selected with only its own members. With one object selected, the Align panel, the Control bar and the Properties panel align it to the artboard whatever Align To is set to.
    With two or more objects selected and no key object, Align to Key Object makes the topmost of them the key, whatever order they were selected in, and the Align panel, the Control bar and the Properties panel align to it. Align To keeps its Selection or Artboard choice and shows it again once the key is cleared.
    Object › Align aligns objects as the align buttons do: it aligns one object to the active artboard whatever Align To is set to, and otherwise it aligns to the key object while there is one, else to the Align To choice, which is saved with the preferences (`ui.inspect` → `ui.align_to`). With direct-selected anchor points, Object › Align aligns the points to their own bounds. While one object is selected, Align To shows Artboard.
    Edit › Keyboard Shortcuts lists each of the Align panel's Align Objects, Distribute Objects and Distribute Spacing buttons under Align, with no default shortcut, as the reference app's [release notes](https://web.archive.org/web/20261006170350/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/new-features/release-notes.html) describe for its Align and Distribute commands. A shortcut set there runs what a click on the button runs, with the Align To choice, the key object and the Distribute Spacing value (`align.horizontalLeft` and the other `align.*` UI commands).
    The command palette lists `select.key` as Cancel Key Object, and a pick cancels the key object (#541).
    Agent selection commands validate every object id before changing the selection and report the resulting count and ids (#784).
    Agents read the key object: `select.key` returns it, and `document.inspect` and the `ui.pointer` and `pointer_gesture` replies report it as `key`. `select.key` with an id that isn't a selected top-level object returns an error and leaves the key unchanged.
    The Select menu's Same commands, its Object commands that select art, Next Object Above and Below, saved selections and the Magic Wand (#2655) select only objects that Select All selects and objects inside them: nothing hidden or locked, nothing in a hidden or locked group, layer or sublayer, nothing on a template layer, and in isolation mode nothing outside the isolated group or layer. In isolation mode Select All, All on Active Artboard and Inverse select nothing while the isolated group or layer, or a group or layer it is in, is hidden, locked or a template layer.
    Select ▸ Object ▸ Bristle Brush Strokes selects the objects whose topmost stroke has a bristle brush, whatever the brush is named, and leaves out objects whose brush is of another type, also when its name has "Bristle" in it.
    Align and Distribute Spacing keep a compound path or selected group that contains the key object in place, as they keep the key object itself.
    Anchor Align moves the selected points to their bounds or the artboard (#1180). Repeating it, or moving by at most 1e-9 pt on both axes as whole-object Align does, leaves the document, Undo, Redo and saved state unchanged; actual moves still take one undo step. `crates/engine/src/tests.rs` covers repeated alignment, rounding-only alignment, unchanged handles, saved state, command recording and Undo/Redo.
    A symbol instance is measured by its symbol's art, as its transform places it, for clicks, the marquee, the bounding box, the Transform panel, Align and Distribute (the art's strokes too with Use Preview Bounds), Fit to Artwork Bounds, exports of the art, thumbnails and canvas culling; one whose symbol is missing is measured as the 20 × 20 square around the origin.
    A selected clip group shows the outline and anchors of its clipping path, not of the art the path clips, and its hover highlight and key object outline follow the clipping path too. That art shows its whole outline when it is selected on its own: with Edit Contents, Direct or Group Selection, or in isolation mode (#2422).
    Clear deletes individual selected compound-path members without deleting their siblings, and explicit object ids work without a selection; Cut still removes the same objects it copies (#786).
    A command that leaves out an object selected inside a selected group also leaves it out when `ids` list it together with a group that holds it. Make Repeat and Live Paint no longer fail on such a list, New Symbol no longer stores the object twice, and `object.transform` no longer moves it twice.
  - **Compound paths:** Make keeps the backmost object's appearance and each contour; selecting a member in Direct Selection reads and changes the compound's fill rule in Attributes. Direction remains a per-member edit. Rendered holes, unchanged contour geometry, no-op history and Undo/Redo are covered by `engine/tests/it/compound_attributes.rs` (#1197). Behaviour reference: [public compound-path documentation](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/manage-objects/reshape-transform-objects/create-compound-paths.html). Make Compound Path on a group (such as outlined type) keeps the paint of its backmost path instead of drawing nothing, and compound paths joined into one keep their holes (#1537).
  - **Saved selections:** Select ▸ Save Selection… asks for a name and keeps the selection in the document (saved with the file, undoable, up to 25); each one is listed at the bottom of the Select menu and a click selects its objects again; Edit Selection… lists them to rename or delete, applied together on OK. A file's saved selections are capped and checked against its objects when it opens.
    Select ▸ Update Selection replaces the objects of the saved selection last recalled with the selected objects, in one undo step that marks the document changed (`select.update`). After Edit Selection… renames that saved selection, Update Selection replaces it under the new name; after Edit Selection… deletes it, Update Selection is disabled until another saved selection is recalled or the delete is undone. Undo and Redo do not change which saved selection is recalled.
  - **Drawing modes:** in Draw Inside, a double-click with a selection tool outside the object being drawn into sets the drawing mode to Draw Normal, as Shift+D does. Pastes follow the drawing mode ([drawing modes](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/draw-shapes-and-paths/learn-drawing-basics/drawing-modes-overview.html)) (#3705): in Draw Inside, Paste, Paste in Place and Paste on All Artboards put the copies inside the object drawn into, in one undo step, Paste Remembers Layers aside; in Draw Behind, Paste in Place and Paste on All Artboards put them just below the selection; Paste in Front and Paste in Back ignore the mode. Shift+D cycles Draw Normal → Draw Behind → Draw Inside → Draw Normal, skipping Draw Inside unless one path, compound path or type is selected. With the object drawn into isolated (a double-click on it with the Selection tool), art drawn or pasted inside it takes isolation mode into its clip group, so it can be clicked and isn't dimmed, as art added in isolation mode belongs with what is isolated ([isolation mode](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/manage-objects/select-objects/isolate-objects.html)) (#3705); undo or redo that removes the isolated object ends isolation mode.
  - **Drawing:** Pen, Curvature, anchor tools, Pencil, Paintbrush, Blob Brush, Smooth, Path Eraser, Join. Direction handles dragged with Direct Selection or the Anchor Point tool snap to smart guides, and Shift keeps them at 45° steps from their anchor. The Pen continues any open path from the end clicked, and while drawing, a click on an end of another open path joins the two into one (#776). The Curvature tool edits any selected path, whatever drew it, keeping its shape except where edited (#798): a click on a point makes it current and a drag moves it, re-curving only its two segments; Alt-click or double-click toggles it smooth or corner and Delete removes it; a click on a segment adds a point without changing the shape; with an end of an open path current, clicks go on from it and its other end closes it (`path.curvatureEdit`). Every point a drawing tool places snaps to Smart Guides through one snapper (#506): the Pen's and Curvature tool's anchors, the Pencil's ends, the shape tools' start and dragged corner or radius (Rectangle, Rounded Rectangle, Ellipse, Polygon, Star, Line Segment, Arc, Spiral, the grids), the Type tool's click and frame, a new artboard's corners. A filled Pencil path keeps a stroke of None (#1804, part of #1679). While a Pencil or Paintbrush stroke is drawn back to within Close Paths When Ends Are Within of its start, the cursor shows the closing ring and a release there closes the path, as [Draw straight lines with the Pencil tool](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/draw-shapes-and-paths/draw-shapes/draw-straight-lines-with-the-pencil-tool.html) describes for the Pencil. The [ and ] keys reach the Blob Brush, the Eraser and the Symbolism tools in the app (#1734, part of #1661).
    With the Blob Brush, Shift held during a drag keeps the stroke on the horizontal or vertical line through the press point, whichever is nearer to the pointer (90° steps from the Constrain Angle preference), and the points dragged since Shift went down move to the other line when the pointer crosses to it; the points dragged while Shift is up follow the pointer.
    Curvature point markers are circular, with no direction handles. While drawing, its own point feedback replaces generic selection markers; existing paths use the selection overlay, including partial selections and Hide Edges. Anchor Size applies, and Direct Selection and Pen retain their handles. The real egui-frame regressions in `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs` verify marker positions, counts and unchanged documents (#1236, in part); the existing-path interpolation request remains open. The curve through the points (`curvature_spline` in `crates/tools/src/draw2.rs`) makes each stretch of three points follow the circle through them: a smooth point's handles lie along that circle's tangent, each `chord / (3 cos²(α/2))` long (α between handle and chord, capped at 90°), and the ends of an open path mirror their neighbour's tangent in their chord, so a J or a U curves evenly, a turn tighter than 30° comes to a point, and uneven spacing doesn't loop; the rubber band, a dragged or inserted point and `path.convertAnchor` to smooth use the same rule, while the Pencil's fitting keeps its own; `tests_draw2.rs` checks that the rubber band is the path the click makes (#1236, in part). The Smooth tool smooths only the stretch of path under the drag (#1547, fixes #1512).
    While Alt is held, the Paintbrush, and the Pencil with Alt key toggles to Smooth Tool off, show a closing cursor (a crosshair with a ring); releasing the mouse button with Alt still held closes the path.
    With Shift held at the press, the Pencil draws a straight line from the press point to the pointer at 45° steps from the Constrain Angle, as [Draw straight lines with the Pencil tool](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/draw-shapes-and-paths/draw-shapes/draw-straight-lines-with-the-pencil-tool.html) describes; pressed on an end of a selected open path, the line continues the path from that end (part of #3799). While Shift is held before the press, the Pencil shows a straight-line cursor (a crosshair with a short line). Option/Alt's unconstrained straight line waits for #3959: Alt still closes the path or lends the Smooth tool.
    With Shift held at the press, the Pencil draws a straight line from the press point to the pointer at 45° steps from the Constrain Angle, as [Draw straight lines with the Pencil tool](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/draw-shapes-and-paths/draw-shapes/draw-straight-lines-with-the-pencil-tool.html) describes; pressed on an end of a selected open path, the line continues the path from that end (part of #3799). While Shift is held before the press, the Pencil shows a straight-line cursor (a crosshair with a short line). Option/Alt's unconstrained straight line remains: Alt still closes the path or lends the Smooth tool.
    While Alt is held, the Paintbrush (before a press and while drawing) shows a closing cursor (a crosshair with a ring), and so does the Pencil with Alt key toggles to Smooth Tool off when Alt is pressed after the drag starts; releasing the mouse button with Alt still held closes the path. A Pencil drag started with Shift or Alt held draws a straight line instead, which stays open.
    With Shift held at the press, the Pencil draws a straight line from the press point to the pointer at 45° steps from the Constrain Angle, as [Draw straight lines with the Pencil tool](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/draw-shapes-and-paths/draw-shapes/draw-straight-lines-with-the-pencil-tool.html) describes; pressed on an end of a selected open path, the line continues the path from that end (part of #3799). With Option/Alt held at the press and Alt key toggles to Smooth Tool off, the Pencil draws a straight line at any angle, whose ends snap to Smart Guides, and it stays open when Alt is still held at the release; Shift and Alt together keep the 45° steps (#3799). The straight-line cursor remains.
  - **Shapes:** all shape tools (including Flare) and the line, arc, spiral and grid tools. Space held while dragging out a shape, line, arc, spiral or grid moves it at its current size. While a grid is dragged out, Up/Down change its rows (concentric dividers) and Left/Right its columns (radial dividers). A click with a grid tool asks for the size, the divider counts and the grid options (#1377, in part): a skew for each set of dividers, Use Outside Rectangle As Frame or Create Compound Path From Ellipses, and Fill Grid; they are parameters of `shape.rectangularGrid` and `shape.polarGrid`, stay as the tool's options and apply to drags too. The curve a skew percentage follows and the direction of the radial skew are our own (the public documentation gives neither), and the dialogs have no reference point locator. An ellipse's Pie Start and End Angle and Invert Pie (Transform and Properties panels' Ellipse Properties, `object.setLiveShape {pieStart, pieEnd, invertPie}`) cut it as a pie (#812).
