With the bounding box showing, the Selection tool shows a selected ellipse's two pie widgets just outside it; dragging one sets its angle in one undo step and double-clicking one makes the ellipse whole again. A live polygon's Polygon Properties there: side count, angle, corner type and radius, radius, side length and Make Sides Equal once an uneven scale has made its sides differ (`object.setLiveShape {sides, polygonAngle, polygonRadius, sideLength, makeSidesEqual}`, part of #812); a star is a plain path, as in Illustrator. The Flare Tool Options last as the tool's options: the next flare dragged out uses them, a click's dialog shows them and double-clicking the tool opens them (part of #812).
  - **Cutting:** Eraser, Scissors, Knife, Mirror & Cut, Line Cut and Rectangle Cut (real geometry, compound paths keep their holes).
  - **Transform:** Rotate, Reflect, Scale, Shear (click or Alt-click snaps the reference point to anchors and centres; Alt-click opens the tool's dialog, and a drag with Alt down at the release, from the press or pressed mid-drag, transforms a copy), Reshape, Free Transform (free and perspective distort and shear, switched by the keys held during a handle drag).
    Align, Distribute, Distribute Spacing, Reflect and Shear return an error for any `horizontal`, `vertical`, `to`, `axis`, `bounds` or `spacing` value they don't take, listing the choices, and Align returns one when a call gives neither `horizontal` nor `vertical`; nothing moves and no undo step is recorded. Align and Distribute act on the anchor points selected with Direct Selection: the points of one path align to each other, not to the artboard, and Distribute spaces them (#1641, fixes #1636; aligning to a key anchor is still missing).
    Transform Again uses the Copy, Transform Patterns, Scale Strokes & Effects and Scale Corners choices of the transform it repeats; after a bounding-box handle drag on area type, it resizes the type area again and the type keeps its size (`object.transformAgain`). With anchors selected with Direct Selection, Move, Rotate, Scale, Reflect, Shear and Transform Again (the commands, their dialogs and the four tools' drags) transform only those anchors, their handles with them, about the centre of the box around them unless a point was clicked; a copy still copies the whole object (#1408; behaviour reference: [adjust path segments](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/adjust-path-segments.html); the default reference point and the copy are our choices). The Move, Rotate, Scale, Reflect and Shear dialogs have a Preview checkbox, off when they open: while it is on the canvas follows the values, Cancel rolls it back and OK is still one undo step; Up/Down step the Rotate and Shear angles and the Scale percentages by 1, Shift by 10 (#1412). The five dialogs and Transform Each have Transform Objects beside Transform Patterns: off, the art stays and only its pattern tiles transform (`objects` on the transform commands), and Transform Again repeats the choice (#1448; behaviour reference: [scale objects](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/manage-objects/reshape-transform-objects/scale-objects.html); the checkboxes are always enabled and the Scale page's pair is applied to all of them, our choices). Reflect's axis is Horizontal, Vertical or an angle (#1460; [reflect objects along an axis](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/manage-objects/arrange-objects/reflect-objects-along-an-axis.html)). The link that keeps Transform Each's two scales equal is not built.
  - **Pen:** Alt pressed in the middle of dragging out an anchor splits its handles and keeps the curve already shaped into it (only the outgoing handle follows the pointer); Space held while dragging out an anchor moves it, handles and all. A press on the first anchor of the path being drawn closes it whatever the drag then does: the drag shapes the closing curve (symmetric handles, Alt breaks them) and the release closes the path wherever it ends (#501). Clicking the last anchor of the path being drawn retracts its outgoing handle (convert cursor), and dragging from it pulls out a new one on its own. Auto Add/Delete: over a selected path, a click on a segment adds an anchor and a click on an anchor deletes it (add and delete cursors); Shift held, or Preferences › General › Disable Auto Add/Delete, starts a new path instead. Alt held over a handle end or an anchor of a selected path (the one being drawn too) works as the Anchor Point tool, with its convert cursor: dragging a handle moves it alone, clicking a smooth anchor makes it a corner, dragging an anchor pulls out new symmetric handles, dragging a segment reshapes it; drawing then goes on. Cmd (Ctrl) held drags with the selection tool chosen last, Direct Selection until one is (handles, anchors and segments of the path being drawn or another), and the Pen then goes on drawing its path while that stays selected; the pointer shows that tool's while Cmd is held. The same holds for agents (`pointer_gesture` with `mods.cmd`), as the borrowing now lives in the engine (#494). A drag's preview (the Pen's, the Anchor Point tool's, Direct Selection's handles and anchors) follows every position the pointer is seen at (#834): the canvas sends the tool a drag whenever the pointer's document position differs from the last one it sent, not only when egui's frame delta is non-zero (zero when a compositor coalesces motion and in the frame the pointer comes back into the window after leaving it), and a move that arrives in the release's own frame shapes the preview before the release commits it, once the press has dragged. With the Pen, a press that moves under 3 screen pixels is a click (a corner without handles), and a Precise Cursors command toggles the existing preference and can take a shortcut (#1663).
  - **Direct Selection (#1278):** clicking a segment picks its connection, with hollow endpoint anchors and only that curve's direction handles. Delete leaves the neighboring curves and appearance intact, opens/splits contours in one undo step, and another Delete removes the remaining selected path. A whole-path drag and deliberate anchor selection keep their existing behavior; egui frames and native control/art checked, OS mouse/visual QA pending. Where anchors of overlapping objects coincide, a click or drag takes the anchor of the selected object, also when another object lies over it (#1509, fixes #1508). Delete removes every selected anchor of a closed path (it used to remove the wrong ones), removes objects selected whole along with the selected anchors of others, and keeps the remainder selected so a second Delete removes it (#1674). In isolation mode Direct Selection and Group Selection pick only inside the isolated object (#1666). Escape cancels a Direct Selection drag (#1803, #1743). Double-clicking type (including type nested inside a group) switches to the Type tool and puts the caret at the clicked character.
    A path segment with a control point whose x or y is infinite or larger in size than `f64::MAX / 16` is measured by its control points, so its bounds hold the whole curve and the canvas check refuses an edit that leaves such a path selected (`path.create` included).
    With Direct Selection, the Pen and the anchor tools, a group, compound path or clip group selected whole shows the anchors of its paths filled, as a path selected whole does; the direction handles still show only on a path that is selected itself. Public references: [Adjust anchor point, handle, and bounding box display size](https://web.archive.org/web/20251114182206/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/draw-shapes-and-paths/learn-drawing-basics/adjust-anchor-point-handle-and-bounding-box-display-size.html) and [Drawing basics](https://web.archive.org/web/20231130064834/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/drawing-basics.html) (archived copies).
    `path.curvatureEdit`, `path.removeAnchor`, `path.convertAnchor`, `path.reshapeSegment`, `path.split`, `path.setHandle`, `path.moveAnchor` and `path.insertAnchor` refuse a `subpath` that is not a whole number of 0 or more, and `path.split` refuses such an `anchor` or `segment`; without a `subpath` they edit subpath 0.
    `path.reshapeSegment` refuses a delta of 1e9 pt or longer, as `object.blend.spine.reshapeSegment` does, and `path.convertAnchor` and `path.freehand` refuse a point whose x or y is 1e9 pt or more in size.
    `path.reshapeSegment`, `object.blend.spine.reshapeSegment`, `path.convertAnchor`, `path.curvatureEdit`, `path.insertAnchor`, `path.moveAnchors`, `path.reshape`, `path.close` and the Pencil, Curvature, Knife, Eraser, Path Eraser, Smooth, Join and Blob Brush commands refuse a number, point or handle given as text, such as "10", and leave the document unchanged; `path.convertAnchor` refuses an `x` without a `y`, or a `y` without an `x`.
    `path.close` and `path.setHandle` (`independent`), `path.moveAnchors` (`patterns`), the Pencil (`closed`, `keepSelected`, `fill`), Curvature (`closed` and a point's `corner`), `path.curvatureEdit` (`corner`), `path.reshapeSegment` (`perpendicular`) and the Blob Brush (`keepSelected`, `mergeOnlySelection`, `merge`) refuse a value other than true, false or null, such as "true", and leave the document unchanged.
  - **Group Selection (#2441):** a click picks one path of a compound path (its outline within the pick tolerance, else the innermost path whose area holds the click: the outer shape or a hole), Shift-click adds another, and a click on a selected path adds the compound path, as a click on a group member climbs to its group. A path selected this way moves, rotates and scales on its own; paint still goes to the compound path.
    With Direct Selection, Shift pressed during the drag of a curved segment keeps both of its handles at right angles to the line between its anchors, on the same side and at the same length (`path.reshapeSegment {perpendicular}`). Shift held while any segment is dragged with the Anchor Point tool or the Pen with Alt does the same. With the Anchor Point tool, Shift held at the press on an anchor (or a selected blend's spine point) moves it, handles and all, instead of pulling out handles; Shift kept down keeps the move at 45° steps, and a Shift-click that doesn't move leaves the anchor as it was (`path.moveAnchor`). A selected blend spine's segment dragged with the Anchor Point tool, or a curved one dragged with Direct Selection, bends the same way (`object.blend.spine.reshapeSegment`).
  - **Live Corners:** drag a live rectangle's corner widgets (Selection or Direct Selection) to round all corners, with a radius readout; with Direct Selection, select corner anchors to show and round just those corners (#381). Each corner keeps its own radius and kind (Round, Inverted Round, Chamfer): Alt-click a widget to cycle the kind, double-click it for the Corners dialog, and the Properties and Transform radius fields set the selected corners (`object.setLiveShape {corners, radius, kind}`). A link toggle behind Corner Radius (the `singleCornerRadius` preference) switches the panels to a field for each corner of a live rectangle: Top Left, Top Right, Bottom Right and Bottom Left. Corners stay circular when the rectangle is scaled unevenly or along its own sides when rotated (the radius keeps its size, or scales by the mean scale with Scale Corners on); only a shear distorts them. On a rectangle that isn't square every corner is the same circle: a radius past half the shorter side stops there for all of them, the widgets sit on the corners as drawn and turn the edited corners red at that limit, CSS export writes the drawn radii, and rectangles saved stretched by older versions get circular corners when their corners are next set (#442). Live Corners work on any path's corners too, as on a rectangle's (#511): a star's, a live polygon's (which also shows them to the Selection tool, has a Corner Radius field in the Properties and Transform panels and keeps its radius as its sides change) and a pen path's, wherever two sides meet at an angle at an anchor that isn't smooth: curved sides too, trimmed to what the cut leaves of them (#1144). Direct Selection shows the widgets of every corner, or of the corners holding selected anchors; each corner is a circle tangent to both sides, drawn no larger than takes its cut halfway along its shorter side; a path keeps its uncut outline so its corners stay editable, and the same command, dialog, angle preference and View › Hide Corner Widget apply. With Direct Selection a click on a widget (no drag) selects its corner, as a click on the corner's anchor does, so the next drag on it rounds that corner alone; Shift-click toggles it (#1239). While a corner widget is dragged with the Selection tool the bounding box hides, so the rounding shows against the path alone (#1229). A round corner next to a curved side curves smoothly instead of sticking out of the shape (#1547, fixes #1512).
    View › Hide Edges hides the Live Corners widgets, the bounding box and the type widget, and the selection tools then do not answer a press on them or change the cursor over them.
  - **Blend spine Anchor Point tool (#2544):** on a selected blend, dragging a spine corner makes symmetric Smooth handles; the tool displays and picks existing spine handles when switched to, drags one independently or retracts it on click, and clicking a point with handles retracts both. The spine is edited live without moving its key objects. Windows native canvas checks and screenshots reviewed: symmetric and independent handles, corner/retraction, Shift constraints and perpendicular reshaping, tool switching, key preservation, Undo/Redo, save/reopen, hidden handles and overlapping Path/Blend priority (PR #2643). Behaviour reference: [public path-editing documentation](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/adjust-path-segments.html).
  - **Path editing (#494):** the handles shown are the handles that drag: Direct Selection drags those of a path selected as a whole (as the Pen leaves it), the Anchor Point tool and Pen+Alt no longer grab handles that Show handles when multiple anchors are selected hides, a handle shorter than the tolerance leaves its anchor to be picked, and the anchor tools pick within Selection & Anchor Display › Tolerance. A dragged segment keeps a smooth anchor at either end smooth. With Direct Selection, the Pen, the Curvature and the anchor tools, a path selected as a whole shows all its anchors selected, and the Control bar and the Properties panel offer Convert (corner, smooth) for them too; Remove and Cut wait for anchors direct-selected (#504). A handle drag gathers its snap targets once per drag (it took 21 ms per pointer move on a 20,000-path document, now 1 ms; `vectorcraft-cli perf` measures handle and segment drags on a 5,000-anchor path). Join merges the selected anchor points that lie on one another, as after Average, into one anchor (#1582, fixes #1533); Average and Join in one step, with a corner or smooth choice for the joined anchor, is missing ([gap 1](gaps.md)).
  - **Graphs:** Column, Stacked Column, Bar, Stacked Bar, Line, Area, Scatter, Pie and Radar graph tools with Graph Data and Graph Type. A series starts in greyscale; Group Selection's fill and stroke are kept separately on the graph and reapplied when its data, type or size changes, and through save, open and undo. Graph Type's Override Calculated Values (both `axisMin` and `axisMax`) uses exactly that value-axis range, split into the tick count (5 when automatic). Line graphs take Edge-to-Edge Lines (off by default: the points sit at the centres of their categories; graphs saved before the option keep their edge-to-edge lines), and radar graphs follow Mark Data Points and Connect Data Points. Blank cells (an empty CSV cell or `null`) are values left out, not zeros: columns, bars and stacked segments skip them, lines and scatter lines break around them and the value axis ignores them, while area, pie and radar draw them as 0; a number in straight quotes is a label, and the data window writes it back quoted. Graph types combine: Graph Type on series picked with Group Selection (or `series` indexes) draws them as their own type, with column, stacked column, line and area mixing on the vertical value axis and bar and stacked bar on the horizontal one; stacked columns take one slot of the cluster, lines draw in front of columns and areas behind. The value axis goes on the left, the right or both sides (column, stacked column, line, area and scatter graphs; bar graphs keep theirs along the bottom), and Separate Scales gives the series assigned to the right axis a scale of their own with its own tick values. Each value axis takes tick marks of no, short or full (across the plot) length and a count per division, and a prefix and suffix for its numbers; the category axis takes tick marks too (none by default), at or between its labels. Graph designs: Object › Graph › Design lists the designs with a preview of the selected one, and New Design (the selected art), Rename, Delete Design, Paste Design (a copy back to edit) and Select Unused, and Marker draws the data points and legend swatches of line, scatter and radar series with a design, scaled so its backmost object fills the default marker's square. Graph Data transposes rows and columns and switches a scatter graph's x and y, and a `|` in a category or series label starts a new line. Pie graphs take Legends in Wedges, Position (Even, Ratio sized by area, Stacked on one centre) and Sort (None, All, First). Graph Type takes column and cluster widths up to 1000% (overlapping past 100%) with First Row and First Column in Front (First Row orders each series' categories; across series the series order decides, so series stay one group each for Group Selection), draws filled lines, adds drop shadows behind columns, bars, lines and wedges, and puts the legend in rows across the top. Text formatted with the Character or Appearance controls, on the whole graph or on labels picked with Group Selection, is kept per kind of label (value axis numbers, category labels, legend labels) through the graph being drawn again. Object › Graph › Data opens a worksheet: cells picked with a click and edited above the sheet (Tab moves right, Enter down, the arrows between cells), Import Data from a tab-separated text file, Transpose, Switch x/y, Cell Style (decimals shown, column width), Revert and Apply. `graph.setData` returns and takes the data as CSV with each value written exactly, not rounded to two decimals, so applying the returned CSV changes nothing (#1485).
  - **Graph column designs:** Object › Graph › Column (`graph.column`) draws the columns, bars or stacked segments and the legend swatch of the series picked with Group Selection with a graph design: Vertically Scaled stretches it to each column's length, Uniformly Scaled scales it both ways and centers it, Repeating stacks a copy for each Each Design Represents value and chops or scales the last one (For Fractions), and Sliding keeps the part above the design's guide line in proportion and stretches the part below. The dialog lists the designs with a preview; the choice is saved with the graph and follows the design's rename and delete.
    Type in a column design that holds a `%` followed by two digits shows each column's value in place of the `%` and the digits: the first digit is the least number of places before the decimal point (zeros are added in front; 0 gives as many as the value needs), and the second digit sets the places after it, rounded. Unless it is inside a group that clips or has its own opacity or appearance, or inside a blend, compound shape, envelope, repeat or intertwined objects, the type keeps its size and is drawn once per column in a repeating design. The legend swatch leaves it out.
  - **Other:** Eyedropper, Gradient annotator, Artboard (Alt-drag duplicates an artboard, and its art with Move/Copy Artwork with Artboard on; Copy, Cut and Paste take the artboard with its art, Paste right of the last artboard, Paste in Place where it was, into this or another document, #446; Object › Artboards › Rearrange All Artboards lays them out in a grid by row or by column, in one row or one column, left to right or right to left, from the menu, the Artboards panel or Properties' Rearrange All, #681; Scale Artwork with Artboard, in the Control bar and Properties beside Move Artwork with Artboard, resizes the artboard proportionally with the art fully inside it and its guides, strokes and corners per the Scale preferences, #602), Measure, Type, Hand, Zoom, Rotate View.
    While a drag rotates the view, a dial at the center of the canvas shows the angle.
  - **Editing type:** double-clicking type with a selection tool (Selection or Direct Selection) switches to the Type tool with the caret where it was clicked; pressing Escape finishes editing and switches back to the selection tool used before double-clicking it (when in isolation mode, the first Escape exits text editing while preserving isolation mode, and a second Escape exits isolation).
    While a Type tool edits type, a click that lands on no type ends the editing without making new type, and that tool stays active; the next click makes new type (#2871, #2854).
    Duplicate Artboards, the Artboard tool's Alt-drag and Paste give the new artboard an id that no other artboard has, also when an artboard's id is the largest possible value (#1718). Deleting the copy or the original then leaves the other's guides.
  - **Touch Type:** a click with the Touch Type tool (Shift+T) selects one character and shows a box around it. Dragging the box or its lower-left handle moves the character. The upper-left handle scales it vertically, the lower-right handle scales it horizontally, the upper-right handle scales it proportionally, and the upper-middle handle rotates it. Each drag is one undo step that sets the character's kerning, baseline shift, scales or rotation, and the type stays editable (`text.touchType`; behavior reference: [Touch Type tool](https://web.archive.org/web/20261007185617/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/tool-techniques/touch-type-tool.html), [Add text with the Type, Area Type, and Touch Type tools](https://web.archive.org/web/20260926095922/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/design-with-text/add-manage-text/add-text-illustrator-text-tools.html)).
  - **Temporary tools:** Cmd with any other tool drags with the selection tool used last (Selection, Direct Selection or Group Selection). Held Space pans and Cmd+Space zooms (Cmd+Alt+Space out) whatever the tool.
    A Space+Shift drag rotates the view whatever the tool, as a Rotate View tool drag does, and Shift does not round the angle to 15°.
  - **Swatches panel clicks:** Ctrl/Cmd-clicking New Swatch makes a spot color, and Ctrl/Cmd+Shift-clicking it makes a global process color.
  - **Panel drag and drop:** art dragged off the canvas onto the Symbols panel becomes a symbol, art dragged onto the Swatches panel becomes a pattern swatch, and art dropped on the Brushes panel opens New Brush for that art; a symbol dragged onto the canvas places an instance where it is dropped, and a brush dragged onto a path is applied to it.
    New Brush asks for the type of brush first, as the [Brushes](https://web.archive.org/web/20241230205225/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/brushes.html) page (archived copy) describes. The Brushes panel's New Brush button, its menu's New Brush… and art dropped on the panel open the New Brush dialog, where Scatter Brush, Art Brush and Pattern Brush need selected or dropped art. OK opens that type's Brush Options for the new brush, and their OK makes the brush with the name and options set; Cancel in either dialog adds no brush (`ui.newBrush`). The menu's New Calligraphic Brush, New Bristle Brush and New Art, Scatter and Pattern Brush from Selection items still make a brush at once.
  - **Panel drag and drop:** art dragged off the canvas onto the Symbols panel becomes a symbol, onto the Swatches panel a pattern swatch and onto the Brushes panel an Art brush; a symbol dragged onto the canvas places an instance where it is dropped, and a brush dragged onto a path is applied to it.
    In the Brushes panel, a brush dragged onto another brush of its type goes before or after it, by the half of the tile or row the pointer is over, and a bar marks the slot while the brush is held there (`brush.move`); the move is one undo step. Brushes move only within their type, as the [Brushes](https://web.archive.org/web/20241230205225/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/brushes.html) page states: a brush dropped on a brush of another type stays where it is, and the status bar shows "brushes move only within their type".
    In the Swatches panel, Alt-dragging a swatch onto another swatch of its kind (not a tint swatch) replaces that swatch's color, gradient or pattern, and the swatch keeps its name and place.
  - **Tool double-clicks:** double-clicking a tool's button opens its options: Hand fits the artboard in the window, Zoom shows 100 %, Rotate, Scale, Reflect and Shear open their Object › Transform dialogs, the Selection, Direct Selection and Group Selection tools the Move dialog (Enter opens these seven tools' dialogs too; Move opens on the offset of the last drag or Move and with the checkboxes it was last confirmed with, so Enter, Enter repeats a move or a copy at the same spacing, as [an Adobe Community thread](https://community.adobe.com/questions-652/move-tool-771221) describes), Gradient, Eyedropper, Blend and the Liquify tools their panels or options, the Pencil, Paintbrush, Smooth, Blob Brush and Eraser tools their Tool Options (Fidelity, fill, Keep selected, the tolerances, the brush size), and (#812) the Flare tool its Flare Tool Options, the Artboard tool the active artboard's Artboard Options, the graph tools Graph Type for the selected graph, the Symbolism tools the Symbolism Tools Options (Diameter, Intensity, Symbol Set Density) and the Magic Wand tool its panel.
    Double-clicking the Line Segment, Arc, Rectangular Grid or Polar Grid tool opens its Tool Options, as step 3 of the [Rectangular Grid tool](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/tool-techniques/rectangular-grid-tool.html) and [Arc tool](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/tool-techniques/arc-tool.html) pages and the [Tools](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/tools.html) page describe (#2691): the dialog a click with the tool opens, without a place to draw. Line Segment Tool Options has Length, Angle and Fill Line (a new line takes the current fill, `shape.line` `fill`); Arc Segment Tool Options its lengths, Reference Point, Type, Base Along, Slope and Fill Arc; the grids' Tool Options the Reference Point, Default Size, dividers, skews and switches. OK draws nothing: the next drag draws with the options and a click's dialog opens at them, the Length, Angle and Default Size included; Cancel changes nothing. Tests: `toolbar::tests::double_clicking_the_line_arc_and_grid_tools_opens_their_tool_options`, `line_segment_options_and_fill_line`, `grid_default_size_is_an_option_the_drag_leaves_out`, `fill_line_gives_a_new_line_the_current_fill`.
    In the Pencil and Paintbrush Tool Options, Edit selected paths within 0 px turns editing off, so a stroke that starts exactly on an end of a selected open path draws a new path; Close paths when ends are within 0 px turns closing off, so a stroke that ends exactly where it started stays open.
    Keep selected in the Pencil and Paintbrush Tool Options is on by default; while it is off, the path a stroke draws or continues is not selected afterwards and the rest of the selection stays as it was (`path.freehand` `keepSelected`).
    Double-clicking the Shape Builder tool opens Shape Builder Tool Options ([Shape Builder tool options](https://web.archive.org/web/20260105172244/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/building-new-shapes-using-shape.html)): with Consider Open Filled Paths as Closed off, a filled open path cuts regions as an unfilled one does; Pick Color From Color Swatches fills merged shapes with the current fill, the Left and Right arrow keys step it through the document's color swatches, and Cursor Swatch Preview shows the current fill and the swatches before and after it above the pointer; Selection Straight Line merges what the line from a drag's first point to its last crosses ([Setting Illustrator's Shape Builder Options](https://web.archive.org/web/20260615204453/https://creativepro.com/setting-illustrators-shape-builder-options/)); with Highlight Fill off, merge mode shades no regions (`shapeBuilder.merge` `openFilledAsClosed` and `pickColorFrom`).
    With In Merge Mode, Clicking Stroke Splits the Path on in the same dialog, a click on a stroke in merge mode splits its path into the run of stroke under the pointer and the rest of the path, as the [Shape Builder tool options](https://web.archive.org/web/20260105172244/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/building-new-shapes-using-shape.html) page describes; the run goes from the anchor or crossing point before the pointer to the one after it, and the pointer shows scissors over it. Highlight Stroke When Editable draws that run in the color chosen in its Color list (Red by default), and with Pick Color From Color Swatches the run takes the current fill as its stroke (`shapeBuilder.merge` `splitStroke`).
    With Pick Color From Artwork, a merged shape takes the appearance, opacity and blending mode of the object where the drag starts, else of the object where it ends, else of the front-most selected object, as the [Shape Builder combine page](https://web.archive.org/web/20251006211643/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/draw-shapes-and-paths/draw-shapes/combine-shapes-with-shape-builder-tool.html) describes. A click in an area that no selected object covers, such as a hole other shapes enclose, takes the front-most selected object's look (`shapeBuilder.merge` `points`: the first point is where the drag starts, and the last point is where it ends).
    A Shift-drag with the Shape Builder tool draws a rectangular marquee for merging many paths at once, as [Combine shapes with the Shape Builder tool](https://web.archive.org/web/20251006211643/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/draw-shapes-and-paths/draw-shapes/combine-shapes-with-shape-builder-tool.html) describes: the regions it reaches are shaded while it is drawn and merge into one shape on release, or with Alt they are deleted. The marquee reaches each region whose outline crosses it or has an anchor inside it, and the region that holds the whole marquee; this rule is VectorCraft's own. For Pick Color From Artwork, the marquee's starting corner is where the drag starts and the opposite corner is where it ends (`shapeBuilder.merge` `rect`).
    Shape Builder pieces on dense hatches (lines at exact 0.25 or 0.5 pt steps across another line) come back one per stretch between crossings, with no speck where the sweep cut a line's two passes a rounding error apart: the planar map contracts the stub between such cuts into one vertex, bounded by each cluster's extent so a run of tiny level segments keeps its length (`crates/pathops/src/planar.rs` tests `a_dense_hatch_at_exact_binary_steps_cuts_each_line_once_per_crossing`, `a_run_of_tiny_level_segments_is_not_contracted_as_stubs`, `a_line_crossed_where_its_two_passes_part_is_cut_once`).
    The Blob Brush Tool Options have Keep selected and Merge only with selection, both off by default: while Keep selected is off, the blob a stroke draws or merges into is not selected afterwards, and while Merge only with selection is on, a stroke merges only with selected blobs of its color that it touches (`path.blob` `keepSelected` and `mergeOnlySelection`).
- **Ruler guides as layer objects:** a guide goes on the current layer, shows, hides, locks and is deleted with it, is listed in the Layers panel (its row selects it) and moves to another layer (`guide.setLayer`, or its row dragged onto that layer's rows); guides on a hidden or locked layer can't be selected, moved or deleted, Duplicate copies a layer's guides and Merge Selected and Flatten Artwork keep them on the merged layer; guides from files saved before guides had layers go on the top visible, unlocked layer when the document opens. Not done: guides stacked among the art of their layer (they are listed above it), a guide row's own eye and lock. Lock Guides also locks the objects made into guides: they can't be selected, moved or deleted (#1543); they are drawn in the guide colour and style of Preferences, and a dragged selection snaps to ruler guides with Smart Guides on (#1583, fixes #1534). The Transform panel shows a selected ruler guide's X or Y, and typing a value moves it (#1659, part of #1597). This is not established by the documentation we could find: the public help pages on guides, rulers and the Transform, Control and Properties panels (read again on 2026-10-14) describe selecting and dragging unlocked guides and the panels' X and Y for a selection, not a guide's position in a panel, and the one public statement of it is a user's [community answer](https://community.adobe.com/questions-652/adding-a-new-custom-guide-785586), which is not documentation. It is kept as a convenience pending the owner's decision, with no parity claim and nothing counted towards a score.
- **Releasing ruler guides:** View › Guides › Release Guides turns the selected ruler guides into paths with no fill or stroke. An artboard guide becomes a line across its artboard, and a canvas guide becomes a line across the artboards (`view.guides.release {index?, ids?}`). A Cmd/Ctrl+Shift double-click with the Selection, Direct Selection or Group Selection tool releases the ruler guide or guide path under the pointer.
- **Layers panel:** every layer, sublayer, group and object is a clickable row at any depth: a click highlights it and makes its layer current (new art goes there), Shift-click a range, Ctrl/Cmd-click toggles. Sublayers are no longer treated as objects: clicks, marquees, Select All and the Select menu take the art inside them, and each sublayer selects in its own colour. Selection squares on rows with selected art (click selects a row's art, Shift adds or removes; dragging the square moves the selection to another row, Alt copies), the eye and lock on every row with drag-down-the-column (one undo step), Ctrl/Cmd-click an eye for per-layer Outline, Alt-click an eye or lock to hide or lock the other layers (again: show or unlock them all), triangles with Alt to open or close everything inside, drag and drop rows above, below or into layers and groups with a drop line (Alt copies) and a dimmed copy of the row under the pointer (layers dropped in the empty space under the last row go below the bottom layer, #2260; dropped on the trash rows are deleted, on New Layer duplicated, as in Illustrator), inline rename, Delete key on highlighted rows. Buttons and the full panel menu: New Layer/Sublayer (Alt: options, Ctrl: on top), Duplicate, Delete, Options for Selection, clipping mask, isolation, Locate Object, Merge Selected, Flatten Artwork, Collect in New Layer, Release to Layers (Sequence and Build), Reverse Order, Template, Hide/Outline/Lock Others and Show/Preview/Unlock All, Paste Remembers Layers, Panel Options (row size, thumbnails per kind, Show Layers Only). Layer Options: name, colour (presets, each with a chip of its colour, or custom), Template, Lock, Show, Print, Preview (outline drawing and clicking) and Dim Images to %. Every operation is a command (`layer.move`, `layer.highlight`, `layer.merge`…) with validation against cycles and invalid nesting. A document opens with only its top-level layers open; the rows left open are saved in the native file (nothing is written for the default) and reopen that way. Only the rows scrolled into view are laid out, from a row list made once per change: a layer of 5,000 groups of 10 paths, all open, draws the panel in 0.4 ms a frame instead of about 29 s (#638).
  The Filter button at the right of Search All keeps the rows that are of an object kind ticked under By Object (paths, shapes, text, images, effects, groups, linked files, guides) and in a state ticked under By Layer (locked, hidden), with the rows that hold them; a section with nothing ticked takes every row. The filter combines with the search, the button is lit while a filter is on, and Clear All in its popup turns the filter off (`ui.layersFilter`). The filter lasts the session.
  The panel menu's Save Selection submenu has Save Selection…, Update Selection and Edit Selection…, enabled and run as in the Select menu, and lists the document's saved selections: choosing one selects its objects again (`select.recall`).
  `object.setProps` with `visible: false` or `locked: true` deselects every selected object that is then hidden or locked, the key object included, as the eye and lock columns do.
  Ctrl/Cmd+Alt-clicking an eye switches the other layers to Outline and the row's layer to Preview, or switches all layers back to Preview when the others are in Outline (`layer.outlineOthers`, `layer.previewAll`).
  Object › Arrange › Send to Current Layer returns the error "the target layer is locked or hidden" and leaves the selected objects where they are when the current layer is hidden or locked, or is inside a hidden or locked layer.
  Selected objects are deselected, the key object included, when a row drag moves them into a hidden layer or group, when `node.move` moves them into a hidden or locked layer or group, when Merge Selected moves them into a hidden or locked layer, when Collect in New Layer moves them into a new layer inside a hidden or locked layer, when Flatten Artwork moves them into a locked layer, and when applying a data set hides them.
  Panel Options › Locate Selected Objects (beyond Illustrator, off by default): when the last selected object changes on the canvas or by a command, the panel opens the layers and groups around it and scrolls to its row, as Locate Object does, without highlighting the row; when Show Layers Only, a search or the filter leaves the object without a row, the panel opens no rows for it and scrolls as with the option off.
- **Drawing aids:** Smart Guides and snapping (moving, with the Selection, Group Selection or Direct Selection tool, and resizing by the bounding-box handles with the Selection or Free Transform tool, Shift and Alt too: the dragged corner or side lands on the other objects' anchors and centres ("anchor", "center") or lines up with their edges and centres (a line and "align"); with Smart Guides › Spacing Guides, a moved selection that lines up with nothing along an axis lands as far from its neighbour as two other objects of its row or column are apart, or halfway between its two neighbours, the equal gaps marked; with View › Snap to Grid on, a moved selection lands on the grid instead, by whichever of its edges is nearest a gridline on each axis (the center does not snap), #740, #1816; the Rotate, Scale, Shear and Reflect tools drag from the anchor they grab and snap the pointer the same way, so a corner dragged onto another object's anchor scales exactly onto it, #482; anchors dragged with Direct Selection: the one pressed on lands on other anchors, its own path's that stay put among them, on path segments or in line with them, the others following, Shift keeps 45° steps, and with Smart Guides off Snap to Point pulls it onto anchors; the Artboard tool snaps artboards, and their bleed, to other artboards, bleeds and art, the grid or whole pixels while moving, copying and resizing them, and the Transform panel shows and edits the active artboard's X/Y/W/H; drawn points, #506: hovering shows where the press goes, the point lands on the other objects' anchors, centres and paths ("anchor", "center", "path") or lines up with their anchors, edges and centres ("align"), the Pen's on the path being drawn too, near a construction guide through the anchor before it on that guide (Preferences › Smart Guides › Construction Guides and Angles), and with Shift kept to its 45° step or a square's diagonal it slides along that way into line; the targets are gathered once per document state, from the art in the window, and the anchors, centres and lines near the pointer are found by bisection, so hovering never rescans the document), guides dragged out of the rulers (#451: they snap as moved guides do, Shift to the ruler's ticks; with the Artboard tool they are artboard guides, which run across their artboard only and move, copy and delete with it, `guide.add {artboard}`) that the Selection, Direct Selection and Group Selection tools then pick and drag (#414: the selected guides highlight and move together, Alt copies them, Shift snaps the dragged one to the ticks, otherwise it snaps to pixels, the grid or the edges, centres (so the sides' midpoints) and anchors of the art and the artboards, or with Smart Guides off Snap to Point pulls it onto anchors; Shift-clicked they join the selected art, and Shift-added art keeps them, so guides and art are selected together in either order, Delete then deleting both in one step; the arrow keys nudge them, Delete deletes them, dragging one back onto its ruler deletes it, Lock Guides and Hide Guides leave them alone; `guide.list`, `guide.select`, `guide.move` and `guide.remove` reach agents), a right-click on either ruler or the origin box to pick the document's units (the current one checked; `document.setUnits`, one undo step, #528), and Draw Normal / Behind / Inside modes. Smart Guides: a point drawn with the Pen or a shape tool, and an anchor dragged with Direct Selection, snaps to where paths and ruler guides cross, labelled "intersect" (#1658, part of #1602; a moved selection's own anchors don't).
  A move that Shift keeps level, upright or diagonal stays on that line when it snaps, with the Selection, Group Selection or Direct Selection tool. It slides along the line until the selection lands on the grid or on whole pixels, lines up with the other objects or is spaced evenly with them, or until the line passes an anchor or crosses a ruler guide near the point the selection was grabbed by. A level or upright move snaps along its own axis only.
  Distance Guides: with Smart Guides on (View › Smart Guides and Preferences › Smart Guides › Invoke Distance Guides, on by default), something selected and the Selection tool, holding Alt/Option over another object shows the distances between the selection's bounds and that object's: on an axis on which they lie apart, one line across the gap between their facing edges; on one on which they overlap, the offsets of their left and right (top and bottom) edges, each line running across the middle of where they overlap, with a dashed line out to the other object's edge when it passes beside it. Over an empty part of an artboard it shows the selection's distances from the artboard's left, right, top and bottom edges. Each line has ticks at its ends and its length in a pill of the smart guide colour, in the General unit; letting Alt go, pressing (a pan or zoom press too), moving off them, leaving the canvas or a floating panel, menu or dialog over the pointer takes them away, and with the pointer still they follow what lies under it as the view scrolls, zooms or turns, as the document, the tab or the selection changes, and when the Selection tool is switched to. Behaviour from the public [Use Distance Guides for accurate placement](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/measure-and-align/grids-and-guides/use-distance-guides-for-accurate-placement.html) and [Smart Guides options](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/measure-and-align/grids-and-guides/smart-guides-options.html) pages, which describe hovering only: nothing shows while moving or nudging. Tests: `select::tests::alt_over_*`, `select::tests::distance_guides_need_alt_a_selection_and_smart_guides`, `tests_prefs::invoke_distance_guides_measures_the_selection_to_the_object_under_alt`, `canvas::tests::alt_over_another_object_draws_the_distance_guide_label`, `canvas::tests::distance_guides_go_when_the_hover_ends`, `canvas::tests::distance_guides_follow_what_lies_under_a_still_pointer`.
  A move pressed on a path's stroke, or within 6 px of its outline away from its anchors and center, is held by the nearest point of that path, with the Selection, Group Selection or Direct Selection tool, and a straight segment Direct Selection drags is held by its own nearest point. That point is what snaps, so the path lands exactly on a ruler guide (with "align") instead of the pressed spot landing there and the path a few pixels beside it, an offset that showed only zoomed far in (#3701). A press in the middle of a fill still snaps the pressed spot: the public [Align objects with guides](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/measure-and-align/grids-and-guides/align-graphic-objects-with-guides.html) page has Snap to Point align the point under the pointer, which is placed exactly where the object should meet the guide.
  A bounding-box handle dragged with the Selection or Free Transform tool snaps what it moves as a dragged point snaps (#2054). With View › Snap to Grid on, it snaps to the nearest gridline, and with Snap to Pixel on, it snaps to whole pixels. With Smart Guides off and Snap to Point on, it snaps to the other objects' anchors and the ruler guides within the Snap to Point distance. With Smart Guides and Snap to Point both on, it lines up with the ruler guides as well as the other objects. Shift still keeps the proportions, and Alt still scales about the center.
  A user slice's edge or corner handle dragged with the Slice Selection tool snaps as the Slice tool's drag does. With View › Snap to Grid on, it snaps to the nearest gridline, and with Snap to Pixel on, it snaps to whole pixels. Otherwise, with Smart Guides on, it lands on or lines up with the anchors, centers and edges of the art and the artboards, and with Smart Guides off and Snap to Point on, it snaps to the art's anchors and the ruler guides within the Snap to Point distance. Then a ruler guide within 5 px, shown and unlocked, moves the side or corner onto it. Shift still keeps the proportions, and Alt still resizes about the center.
- **Artboard click-to-fit (#1227):** a plain click fits the topmost editable object or group to a new artboard, including its stroke like Fit to Selected Art, and makes the new artboard active. Art and its selection stay unchanged; creation is one undo step. Handles, modified clicks, drags, Escape and tool changes retain their meaning. Tested inside an artboard and on the pasteboard (`crates/engine/tests/it/artboard_click.rs`); the public [CS6 Printing Guide](https://helpx.adobe.com/content/dam/help/en/indesign/pdf/CS6_PrintGuide.pdf) documents the object-click gesture. This legacy gesture adds evidence without regrading the 2026 canvas controls.
- **Rotated views:** with the view rotated, Fit Artboard in Window, Fit All in Window and the status bar's artboard navigator fit the artboard or the art as the view turns it, and a Zoom tool marquee (Animated Zoom or GPU Performance off) zooms to the area dragged across. Ruler guides on no artboard turn with the view. The canvas draws the selection marquee where the tools select, Show Hidden Characters draws the marks of type partly inside the canvas, the Contextual Task Bar stays under the selection, and the Navigator's red box outlines what the window shows.
- **Views:** the status bar's artboard navigator (first, previous, next, last; `view.goToArtboard`) goes to an artboard, fits it and synchronizes the Artboard tool selection when that tool is active; ordinary object selection is preserved. Actual Next-button regressions cover keyboard/Properties deletion and Undo in `chrome.rs`. Fit Artboard in Window and Actual Size show the navigator's artboard. The Artboards panel highlights that active artboard: clicking a row makes it active (the Artboard tool's too, while it is chosen) as does clicking an artboard with the Artboard tool, double-clicking its number also fits it in the window and double-clicking its name renames it. Duplicate Artboards, or a row dragged onto New Artboard, copies the artboard with its art (#446). Escape leaves Presentation Mode, `view.screenMode` from it goes back to Normal Screen Mode, and the screen mode isn't saved with the preferences: the app always starts in Normal Screen Mode with its menus and panels (#472). View › Pixel Preview shows the art as the document pixels it rasterizes to, one per point and hard-edged when magnified, turning with a rotated view (it used to draw the smooth vectors, with only the pixel grid over them). In Outline view a template layer keeps drawing in Preview, dimmed, so a picture placed to be traced stays visible under the outlines (#1505, fixes #1486).
  In Presentation Mode, → and ← go to the next and the previous artboard, and a click anywhere goes to the next one, as the status bar navigator's Next and Previous do (`view.goToArtboard`): on the last artboard → and a click leave the view as it is, and so does ← on the first. The arrow keys do not move the selection there, and the tool does not receive a click, so a click selects and draws nothing (behavior reference: [View artwork](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/viewing-artwork.html)).
  In Presentation Mode no key press other than ←, → and Escape runs a command or reaches the tool (tool keys, Delete, Enter, Tab, F, Shift+F and every command shortcut, the macOS menu bar's key equivalents included), a right click or a long touch opens no context menu, a tap of two or three fingers undoes or redoes nothing, and the pointer over the canvas is the default one instead of the tool's cursor.
  Align to Artboard uses the active artboard, the one the Artboards panel highlights (`object.align {artboard}`). A press with a selection tool inside an artboard makes that artboard active; with the Selection tool, a Shift-click on an empty spot inside an artboard makes it active and keeps the selection. One selected object is aligned to the active artboard too, whatever Align To says (a lone object is never the key object). When an action plays, its Align to Artboard, All on Active Artboard, Paste in Place, Paste in Front and Paste in Back steps that name no artboard use the artboard that is active then.
  With the Artboard tool in use, a Shift-click on a row of the Artboards panel selects the artboards from the last row clicked without Shift to the clicked row, and the clicked row's artboard becomes the active one. When the artboard of the last row clicked without Shift is no longer selected, the range starts from the active artboard, and later Shift-clicks start from there too. A Ctrl/Cmd-click still adds or removes one artboard. A Shift-click used to add or remove one artboard as well. The public [Select artboards](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/create-manage-artboards/add-edit-artboards/select-artboards.html) page lists Shift-click in the Artboards panel for selecting several artboards.
  In the Artboards panel, a click on the active artboard's options icon, or a double-click on another row's icon, opens Artboard Options for that row's artboard, and the panel menu's Artboard Options… opens it for the active artboard (part of #1876). Both used to choose the Artboard tool instead. Opened while another tool is in use, the dialog moves the art with a new X or Y when the Artboard tool's Move Artwork with Artboard option is on.
  With several artboards selected with the Artboard tool, the Artboards panel menu's Rename opens an empty name field on the active artboard's row (on the first selected row when the active artboard is not selected), and the name typed there goes to every selected artboard, numbered in panel order (abc-1, abc-2, abc-3), in one undo step (`artboard.setProps {artboards}`). A double-click on a name with Shift or Ctrl/Cmd held that leaves several artboards selected opens the same field; a Ctrl/Cmd double-click on an unselected row's name adds its artboard to the selection first. Both used to rename the active artboard only. With one artboard selected, Rename still gives it the name as typed. The public [Rename artboards](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/create-manage-artboards/add-edit-artboards/rename-artboards.html) page numbers the name the same way for several selected artboards.
  Artboard Options has X and Y fields beside a reference point locator (#1876), so an artboard's position can be typed as well as its size. X and Y are where the reference point lies, counted from the ruler origin (#1212), as the Transform panel and the Control bar show an artboard's position, and the locator is the one they and Properties share. A typed X or Y moves the artboard so that its reference point lands there, and a new Width or Height keeps the reference point in place; OK applies everything in one undo step. The shape dialogs still keep their X and Y to themselves (the click position). Pointer and key tests in `dialogs/tests.rs` cover both. Public references: [Resize artboards](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/create-manage-artboards/add-edit-artboards/resize-artboards.html) and [Create and add new artboards](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/create-manage-artboards/add-edit-artboards/add-new-artboards.html) (a reference point in a nine-point grid, then X and Y).
  Alt-clicking New Artboard in the Artboards panel opens Artboard Options for the new artboard, and OK adds it and makes it the active artboard (`ui.newArtboard`; behavior reference: [Default keyboard shortcuts](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/default-keyboard-shortcuts.html), Use panels). A plain click still adds the artboard at once.
  With Align to Artboard chosen, the Align panel's Distribute Objects and Distribute Spacing buttons use the active artboard (`object.distribute` and `object.distributeSpacing` with `to: "artboard"` and `artboard`). The first object's left or top edge goes to the artboard's left or top edge, and the last object's right or bottom edge goes to the artboard's right or bottom edge. Distribute Objects spaces the other objects evenly by its button's line, and two objects are enough. Distribute Spacing makes the gaps between the objects equal. With anchor points selected, the buttons space the points among themselves and do not use the artboard. When an action plays, its Distribute Objects and Distribute Spacing steps with Align to Artboard use the artboard that is active then.
  With a key object, the Align panel's Distribute Objects buttons use the Distribute Spacing value (`object.distribute {spacing}`): the key object, or the compound path or selected group that contains it, stays in place, and the objects' left edges, centers or right edges (top edges, centers or bottom edges) end up that far apart, outward from the key object's, in their order. With the field's default value of 0, a click puts every object on the key object's line (behavior reference: [Ask Mordy: Distributing Objects](http://rwillustrator.blogspot.com/2008/01/ask-mordy-distribute.html)).
  Choosing the Artboard tool (Shift+O, its toolbar button, Edit Artboards in Properties or Document Setup, or the Artboards panel menu's Artboard Options…) starts it on the active artboard: the canvas outlines that artboard, and Delete, Cut, Copy, the Transform panel and Artboard Options act on it.
  Object › Artboards › Fit to Selected Art resizes the active artboard (`artboard.fitToSelection {index}`). It used to resize artboard 1 whichever artboard was active. When an action plays, its Fit to Artwork Bounds and Fit to Selected Art steps that name no artboard resize the artboard that is active then.
  Object › Artboards › Fit to Artwork Bounds and the Artboards panel menu's Fit to Artwork Bounds fit each selected artboard (those the Artboard tool has selected, else the active one) to the art on it, as the public [Use the artboard context menu](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/create-manage-artboards/organize-manage-artboards/use-artboard-context-menu.html) page describes (`artboard.fitToArt {indices}`). An object partly on an artboard counts for each artboard it overlaps, and an artboard with no art on it keeps its size and place. They used to fit the active artboard to all the art in the document.
  The Artboards panel menu's Duplicate Artboards copies each selected artboard (those the Artboard tool has selected, else the active one) with its art, in one undo step, and the copies are then selected, as the public [Use the artboard context menu](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/create-manage-artboards/organize-manage-artboards/use-artboard-context-menu.html) page describes. With the Artboard tool, Copy and Cut take every selected artboard with its art, as the public [Cut, copy, and paste artboards](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/create-manage-artboards/organize-manage-artboards/cut-copy-and-paste-artboards.html) page describes, and Paste brings them all back in one undo step (`artboard.duplicate`, `artboard.copy` and `artboard.cut` with `indices`). The copies keep their places relative to each other, together right of the last artboard. All three used to act on the active artboard only.
  With the Artboard tool, Paste and Paste in Place make the first pasted artboard the active one (the navigator's and the Artboards panel's), and Cut makes the artboard before the first cut one active (the new first artboard when artboard 1 was cut). A command that chooses another document (`document.activate`) starts the tool on that document's active artboard, as choosing its tab does, and File › Revert keeps the active artboard and starts the tool on it. Paste used to leave the active artboard where it was while the tool had the pasted artboard active, and Cut left the active artboard on the artboard after the cut one while the tool had the one before it.
  With the Artboard tool, an action that reverts the document or switches to another document and back (`command.batch`), and the Actions panel menu's Batch… over a folder whose files it closes or over data sets with a Revert step (`action.batch`), keep the active artboard and start the tool on it, as File › Revert does. They used to make artboard 1 the active one.
  The Artboards panel menu's Convert to Artboards turns the geometric bounds of each selected object that has an area into a new artboard and removes those objects, in one undo step, as Object › Artboards › Convert to Artboards does (`artboard.convertToArtboards`). It is disabled when nothing is selected. It used to be disabled always.
  The canvas draws the active artboard's edge in black, as the public [Select artboards](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/create-manage-artboards/add-edit-artboards/select-artboards.html) page describes. It draws the other artboards' edges in gray. With several artboards selected by the Artboard tool, the canvas draws the black edge around the active one, which the tool shows with handles and its name. It used to draw artboard 1's edge in black whichever artboard was active.
  View › Rotate View turns the view to the status bar's preset angles (`view.rotate {angle}`, which takes any angle). View › Rotate View to Selection turns the view to the angle of the selected objects' bounding box, so the box is square to the window (`view.rotateToSelection`).
  When the view angle changes (a Rotate View drag, the status bar's angle menu, Reset Rotate View or a saved view) and the desktop app renders the frame at the new angle on the render worker, the canvas draws the last frame turned to the new angle until that frame is ready. It used to draw no art until then.
  With the view rotated, a second Escape less than a second after the first resets the rotation, as Reset Rotate View does. The first Escape may end something else, such as isolation mode or a path being drawn. The second resets the view only when it has nothing else to end, and an Escape that closes a menu does not count. After a click, or a press of another key that is not a modifier (Shift, Control, Alt/Option or Command), the next Escape counts as the first. With the Rotate View tool chosen, one Escape resets the view.
  A two-finger rotation on a Mac trackpad turns the view about the pointer once it reaches 5° (Preferences › General › Trackpad Gesture to Rotate View, on by default).
  The status bar navigator's field shows the active artboard's number and name, and its drop-down lists every artboard by number and name, as the Artboards panel does. Choosing an artboard in the list makes it the active artboard and fits it in the window (`view.goToArtboard`). The list opens on the active artboard's row and lays out only the rows in view and at most one more.
- **Geometry and effects:**
  - **Open-path anchor Delete:** Delete/Backspace removes selected anchors and their adjoining segments, leaving drawable runs as separate open subpaths of the original object. Surviving curves and appearance stay intact; one Undo restores the document and selection, and a second Delete removes the selected remainder. Explicit Remove Anchor Points still reconnects/refits. Four core regressions, one full-frame Delete/Backspace regression and three existing removal/segment controls pass, covering these distinctions, multiple deletions, transformed geometry and mixed whole-object selection. Behaviour references: the legacy public [Illustrator reference guide, Add or delete an anchor point](https://helpx.adobe.com/content/dam/help/en/pdf/illustrator_reference.pdf) distinguishes keyboard deletion from dedicated removal; the current [Add or remove anchor points](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/draw-shapes-and-paths/modify-paths/add-or-remove-anchor-points.html) describes the dedicated tools. Other G11 gaps and scores/hours remain unchanged.
  - Pathfinder (10 exact curve booleans; single-result shape operations retain source names and SVG IDs, #1293), Offset, Outline Stroke, Simplify, Clean Up, Split Into Grid, Divide Objects Below. With one group selected alone, the Pathfinder panel's buttons work on its members (among other selected objects a group still acts as one shape), and a greyed-out button says what it needs (#1450; behaviour reference: [combine objects using Pathfinder effects](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/manage-objects/reshape-transform-objects/combine-objects-using-pathfinder-effects.html); one plain path selected alone stays disabled, which the documentation doesn't settle). Split Into Grid takes the number, height or width, gutter and total of the rows and of the columns, Add Guides and Preview, and several selected paths become one grid painted as the topmost one (#1462, `object.path.splitIntoGrid`; behaviour reference: [divide or split objects](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/manage-objects/edit-objects/divide-or-split-objects.html); a typed height or width keeps the gutter and changes the total, our choice). Object › Path › Remove Anchor Points (`path.removeAnchors`) removes the direct-selected anchors without opening their paths (the Delete key still deletes them with their segments): the neighbours keep their handle directions and their facing handles are refitted so one cubic follows the two old segments, and straight sides stay straight. The Delete Anchor Point tool uses the same refit. The Control bar, the contextual task bar, the Properties quick actions and the canvas context menu offer it when anchors are selected. With anchors selected, the Control bar and the Properties panel also convert them to corner or smooth (`path.convertAnchors`), connect end points (Join) and cut the path at them (`path.cutAtAnchors`, also on the task bar and the context menu): a closed path opens there and an open one becomes one path per piece, each cut leaving one of its two coincident anchors selected so a drag pulls the path apart. In the Pathfinder panel a group selected alone counts its nested shapes, so an expanded stroked object keeps the Shape Modes enabled (#1642, #1635).
  - Divide uses open lines, bent paths and curves as cutting edges (#1307), preserving the frontmost filled face's appearance and holes. Engine tests cover implicit closure of filled open contours and unrelated objects; native automation confirms independent piece movement, one Undo/Redo, canvas/window captures and an exact saved-document read by a separate CLI process. The shared planar map keeps a segment cap (65,536 since #937, was 4,096) and its filled-area fallback; other Pathfinder operations are unchanged.
  - Type that Transform effects only move and copy (no scale, rotation, reflection or Random) exports as type in each place, and PDF export writes every copy as selectable, searchable text, when its characters are in solid colors without underline or strikethrough, the type object has no fills or strokes of its own, no inline graphics and no perspective, its transform does not scale or shear stroked characters, and the copies do not overlap. When the effect is on the type itself, the type can also have transparency, an opacity mask and raster effects. When the effect is on the group or layer holding the type, the type has no transparency or effects of its own and is not in a clipping path, the group or layer has no fill, stroke or Pathfinder effect of its own, and no group between them has a fill, stroke, Pathfinder or geometry effect. Type still exports as outlines when the effect stops its copies early, or when the copies would number more than 10,000 or take more than 20,000,000 bytes of document data, and so does other type under a geometry effect.
  - Extrude & Bevel and Inflate treat strokes as outlined: each visible stroke builds a solid from its outline in its own paint beside the top fill's ([three-d.md](three-d.md#fills-and-strokes)).
  - Extrude & Bevel, Inflate and Rotate (Effect › 3D and Materials): live effects in the `three-d` crate with depth, twist, taper, solid or hollow caps, five original bevel shapes (width, height, repeat, spacing, inside, both sides), Inflate's volume, both sides, twist, taper and cap, Rotate's turned fills and strokes, Position presets, the rotation and light gizmos, SVG/PDF vector output and Expand Appearance; one 3D effect per object; covered by geometry, effect, canvas-versus-export, command and dialog tests ([three-d.md](three-d.md)).
  - Initial live Revolve (#605, #846): a portable geometry and shading crate (`three-d`), editable path and compound profiles, compact options with artboard rotation and light gizmos, SVG/PDF vector output and Expand Appearance that can trim covered faces. Open ends have continuous caps by default, shading is smooth with one to ten colored lights, and intersecting surfaces' visibility is approximate ([revolve.md](revolve.md)).
  - Live effects with previewing dialogs: Distort & Transform, Path, Convert to Shape, 15 Warp styles, Round Corners, Scribble, Effect → Pathfinder (all 10 operations, live on groups; several loose objects are grouped first, in one undo step), Color Adjustments (Brightness/Contrast, Curves, Levels, Hue/Saturation, Shift to Color, Temperature/Tint, on vectors, live type and embedded images), and raster drop shadow, glows and feather. SVG and PDF export keep live effects (geometry baked; SVG raster effects as filters). Zig Zag spaces its ridges evenly along each segment, so lines and curves get a regular wave in Corner and Smooth (#1558). Warp › Arc (the effect and Envelope › Make with Warp) bends in the object's real proportions: a circular arc with concentric edges and no fold-over at 100%, so Arc on art that isn't square draws differently from before (#1581, fixes #1578). `effect.apply` and `effect.setParams` give an error for a misspelt or wrongly typed effect parameter instead of running the effect with its default (#1623, #1592). Roughen with Smooth keeps turn-backs smooth instead of making cusps that draw as spikes (#1646, #1643). Scribble draws one zig-zag per region, with no lines across holes and notches; convex shapes are unchanged (#1651, #1648). On the canvas, in Expand Appearance and in exports, Effect → Pathfinder uses the glyph outlines of type in the group, and results painted like the type keep its opacity and blend mode.
  - Pathfinder › Trap ([trapping](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/trapping.html), [Pathfinder panel](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/pathfinder-panel-overview.html)): the Pathfinder panel menu's Trap… (`object.pathfinder.trap`) and Effect › Pathfinder › Trap… (`pathfinder.trap`, live on groups) add, where two objects' visible areas of different solid colours meet, a strip of the darker one's area along the edge, filled with the lighter colour at the Tint Reduction percentage and set to overprint (Reverse Traps: the darker colour spreads instead, but not a rich black); Thickness 0.01–5000 pt across vertical edges, Height/Width scales it across horizontal ones, Traps with Process Color paints a swatch colour's trap with its CMYK equivalent; the effect also has Precision and Remove Redundant Points. The panel's Trap is one undo step and groups the traps above the topmost selected object, selected; with no adjoining edges of different colours it says so and changes nothing. Tests: `crates/pathops/src/trap.rs`, `crates/effects/src/trap.rs`, `group::tests::trap_effect_adds_an_overprinting_strip_above_the_members`, `crates/engine/src/tests_trap.rs`, `panels::pathfinder::tests::trap_opens_its_options_and_ok_traps_the_selection`.
  - Effect › Path › Outline Object has no options. Type that carries it is drawn, exported (PDF and SVG as paths, with no font) and expanded as its glyph outlines while it stays editable, and the effects after it reshape those outlines. Paths and images draw as before. With Use Preview Bounds on, type is measured by its glyph outlines. Public reference: [Summary of effects](https://web.archive.org/web/20210901011839/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/summary-effects.html) (archived copy).
  - With Use Preview Bounds on, the bounding box, the Transform panel, Align, Distribute, Distribute Spacing and `object.setBounds` measure each object after its geometry effects. A path is measured by its effected shape, and a fill or stroke with geometry effects of its own is measured by the shape it paints. Type, images, live objects and symbol instances are measured by their reshaped art, and a symbol instance is also measured by its reshaped art when its symbol's art has geometry effects. A group or layer with geometry or Pathfinder effects, or with a fill or stroke of its own that has geometry effects or paints members with geometry effects, is measured by its evaluated art. A blend, envelope or repeat whose objects have geometry effects is measured by its evaluated art, with those objects measured after their effects. A 100 pt square without a stroke, with Offset Path 10, measures 120 pt, and type with Outline Object aligns and sizes by its glyphs. Raster effects are not measured. Public reference: [Create text](https://web.archive.org/web/20220127090642/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/creating-text.html) (archived copy).
  - Initial live Revolve (#605, #846): a portable geometry and shading crate (`three-d`), editable path and compound profiles, compact options with artboard rotation and light gizmos, SVG/PDF vector output and Expand Appearance that can trim covered faces. Cap is on by default with continuous curved vector rims; shading uses vector gradients automatically, with sharp profile corners, uniform caps and round seam joins. One light and approximate visibility remain ([revolve.md](revolve.md)).
  - Effect › Path › Outline Object has no options. Type that carries it is drawn, exported (PDF and SVG as paths, with no font) and expanded as its glyph outlines while it stays editable, and the effects after it reshape those outlines. Paths and images draw as before. With Use Preview Bounds on, type is still measured by its layout box. Public reference: [Summary of effects](https://web.archive.org/web/20210901011839/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/summary-effects.html) (archived copy).
  - Initial live Revolve (#605, #846): a portable geometry and shading crate (`three-d`), editable path and compound profiles, compact options with artboard rotation and light gizmos, SVG/PDF vector output and Expand Appearance that can trim covered faces. Cap is on by default with continuous curved vector rims; shading uses vector gradients automatically, with sharp profile corners, uniform caps and round seam joins. The Lights list, Add Light and Delete Light manage one to ten independent colored lights; ambient is shared and visibility remains approximate ([revolve.md](revolve.md)).
  - Live effects with previewing dialogs: Distort & Transform, Path, Convert to Shape, 15 Warp styles, Round Corners, Scribble, Effect → Pathfinder (all 10 operations, live on groups; several loose objects are grouped first, in one undo step), Color Adjustments (Brightness/Contrast, Curves, Levels, Hue/Saturation, Shift to Color, Temperature/Tint, on vectors, live type and embedded images), and raster drop shadow, glows and feather. SVG and PDF export keep live effects (geometry baked; SVG raster effects as filters). Zig Zag spaces its ridges evenly along each segment, so lines and curves get a regular wave in Corner and Smooth (#1558). Warp › Arc (the effect and Envelope › Make with Warp) bends in the object's real proportions: a circular arc with concentric edges and no fold-over at 100%, so Arc on art that isn't square draws differently from before (#1581, fixes #1578). `effect.apply` and `effect.setParams` give an error for a misspelt or wrongly typed effect parameter instead of running the effect with its default (#1623, #1592). Roughen with Smooth keeps turn-backs smooth instead of making cusps that draw as spikes (#1646, #1643). Scribble draws one zig-zag per region, with no lines across holes and notches; convex shapes are unchanged (#1651, #1648).
  - Scribble (Effect › Stylize › Scribble…) has a Variation for each of Path Overlap, Curviness and Spacing ([Scribble options](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/creating-sketches-mosaics.html)) (`overlapVariation`, `curvinessVariation`, `spacingVariation`), shown in its dialog and in the Appearance panel. A Scribble saved with the earlier single `variation` reads it as the Path Overlap and Spacing variations and draws as before. The angle is stored above -180° and up to 180°, so 270° is stored as -90°.
  - **Simplify feedback and component selection (#1272):** the existing tolerance dialog previews from the original interaction snapshot and shows original/new anchor counts. Preview off and Cancel restore the document and selection; OK is one Undo. A refit or Add Anchor Points clears component indexes only on paths whose geometry changes, keeping their objects selected whole and unchanged paths' components intact. Engine and real-egui frame regressions cover document/selection restoration and grouped paths.
    Public references: [Simplify benefits](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/draw-shapes-and-paths/modify-paths/simplify-path-benefits.html) and [advanced options](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/draw-shapes-and-paths/modify-paths/simplify-paths-advanced-options-overview.html).
    Nearly unchanged appearance is expected when reducing points. The checklist is partial, without raising scores.
    Simplify and Add Anchor Points record no undo step when they change no path, and a path they leave as it is keeps its live shape.
    The Simplify dialog also has Corner Point Angle Threshold, Convert to Straight Lines and Show Original Path. The threshold is a slider from 0° to 180° and opens at 150°: an anchor whose corner is sharper than the threshold stays a corner, so moving the slider right keeps more corners, and the dialog sends `cornerAngle` as 180° less the threshold. While Preview is on, Show Original Path draws the paths as they were before the preview in a wide, faint band of their layer's color under the selection's outlines.
    Object › Path › Simplify opens a slider under the selection ([Manually simplify paths](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/draw-shapes-and-paths/modify-paths/manually-simplify-paths.html), [Auto simplify paths](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/draw-shapes-and-paths/modify-paths/auto-simplify-paths.html)) with Auto-Simplify, a rail from the fewest anchor points to the closest fit, and More Options, which opens the dialog at the slider's tolerance. The rail's levels are VectorCraft's own scale (`object.path.simplify {level}`): level 50 is 1 pt, and every 10 levels halve or double the tolerance, from 32 pt at 0 to 1/32 pt at 100. Auto-Simplify picks the lowest level whose tolerance is at most 1/400 of the selection's longer side, or level 100 when that side is under 12.5 pt; the slider opens at that level, with its result previewed, as the manual-simplify page describes. The dialog's "Open this dialog with these settings next time" makes the menu item open the dialog on the settings of its last OK.
    With anchors or segments of a path selected with Direct Selection, Simplify acts on just that part of the path, as the [Manually simplify paths](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/draw-shapes-and-paths/modify-paths/manually-simplify-paths.html) page puts it: the slider, Auto-Simplify and the dialog refit only each run of selected segments, between its end anchors, which keep their place and their handles on the side away from the run. The anchors and segments outside the runs stay exactly as they were, a closed path's run may cross its start point, separate runs on one path are refitted independently in one undo step, and the runs stay selected. A path with only lone anchors selected is still simplified whole, and `object.path.simplify {wholePaths: true}` simplifies partly selected paths whole. Tests: `crates/engine/src/tests_simplify_part.rs` and `simplify_slider_and_dialog_simplify_only_the_direct_selected_part_of_a_path`.
- **Devanagari shaping:** with an OpenType Devanagari font, Ka, virama and Ssa (क्ष) form one conjunct glyph, Ra and virama before a consonant (र्क) become a reph drawn after it, the i matra (कि) is drawn before its consonant, and Ka with a nukta is drawn like the precomposed क़ (U+0958), as [Microsoft's Devanagari shaping specification](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/script-development/devanagari) describes. Each syllable is one cluster of its source bytes, and the arrow keys stop at its ends. A click inside a syllable drawn with several glyphs puts the caret at the syllable's nearer end, in point, area and path type. Tests: `crates/text/src/tests_devanagari.rs`; they print SKIPPED when no such font is installed.
- **Vertical punctuation:** fullwidth `！` (U+FF01) and `？` (U+FF1F) use their nominal glyph upright when no vertical alternate is present, following the Tu fallback in [Unicode UAX #50 §3.1](https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr50/#vo). Code-built test fonts cover point and area type with and without `vert` alternates, retain the rotated fallback for a bracket and long vowel mark, and leave horizontal type unchanged. Tests: `crates/text/src/tests_vertical.rs`.
  - Free Distort's dialog (Effect › Distort & Transform › Free Distort…) shows a box in the proportions of the first selected object's bounds with a handle on each corner.
