Dragging a handle moves that corner. A handle focused by a click or Tab moves 1% of the box with each arrow key, and 10% with Shift. Reset puts the four corners back on the box. The preview and OK run `effect.apply`, or `effect.setParams` when the dialog edits an applied effect, and the Appearance panel's inline editor opens the dialog with Edit…. Behavior reference: Illustrator CC Help (2014, [PDF](https://help.adobe.com/archive/en/illustrator/cc/2014/illustrator_reference.pdf)), page 285 (PDF page 291).
- **Kerning across style runs:** characters that differ only in fill, stroke, underline, strikethrough, overprint, character style name, leading, baseline shift, rotation, Character Alignment, kerning, or tracking that keeps or drops ligatures alike are shaped together, so restyling one character keeps the font's kerning pairs with its neighbors. A character with manual kerning that follows one with automatic kerning keeps the font's kerning with it (unless All Caps or Small Caps sets it as two letters, as ß becomes SS), and its value replaces the font's kerning after it. A ligature does not form across a change of style, and a change of font, size or OpenType features still shapes the characters apart. Behavior reference: [Line and character spacing](https://web.archive.org/web/20260916050333/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/line-character-spacing.html) (public documentation). Tests: `crates/text/src/tests_typo.rs`, `crates/text/src/tests_bidi.rs`.
- **Recent font pickers (#3515):** The shared Character, Properties, Glyphs and Find Font family picker lists recently applied families first, once each, in most-recent order and limited by Preferences › Type › Number of Recent Fonts. Search and filters apply to both sections; unavailable families are omitted. Section headings cannot be selected or previewed. Confirmed character-range font edits update the same saved history; previews and failed edits do not. Requirement: [issue #3515](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/issues/3515).
- **Type:** Character size, leading, baseline shift and horizontal-scale controls account for object/group transforms (#1034): exact document-point sizes, mixed-value display and keyboard increments, range edits, resettable horizontal stretch, undo/redo and native save/reopen (`tests_typescale`, Character panel tests). Point size is the transformed em-height axis, independent of glyph ink bounds; affine rotation, reflection and shear are retained. Group scaling still scales text; preserving font sizes is a separate enhancement. Behaviour reference: [Transform text](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/design-with-text/edit-format-text/transform-text.html) (public documentation). Text Wrap, Type on a Path effects (Rainbow/Skew/3D Ribbon/Stair Step/Gravity) and Options (Flip, Align to Path, Spacing; OK keeps the type where it is), type on a path's start, centre and end brackets (Selection and Direct Selection drag them to set where the type runs, slide it along its path and, across the path, flip it: #429), Character and Paragraph Styles (override-preserving redefine), paragraph attributes per paragraph (alignment, indents, spacing, hyphenation, hanging punctuation, tab stops, paragraph style, direction, mojikumi and leading model; the Paragraph, Tabs and Paragraph Styles panels act on the paragraphs the Type tool's selection or caret touches, Return continues the paragraph's style, threads and SVG keep them), Area Type Options (rows/columns/inset/first baseline, vertical Align Top/Center/Bottom/Justify per row/column, reflowing non-rectangular frames and text wrap), threaded text across any closed shapes, Fit Headline, the Every-line Composer for justified and ragged text (paragraph-wide breaks for an even rag, Single-line per object from the Paragraph panel menu or `text.setFormat {composer}`). Area type resizes like Illustrator's type areas: a bounding-box handle drag (Selection tool) or Area Type Options Width/Height size the frame and the text reflows at its size (threads too); Direct Selection drags a frame corner or edge (`text.reshapeArea`), and an anchor of type on a path's path, the type reflowing along it (`text.reshapePath`, #3980). Point type still scales. Auto Size: the frame height follows the text after every edit, in the same undo step (rectangular frames of horizontal type in one row; columns get the least height that holds them; a height set by hand or threading turns it off), and the "Auto Size New Area Type" preference gives it to new area type. Shrink Text to Fit (beyond Illustrator): overflowing area type scales its sizes, leading and baseline shifts down by the largest factor (in 0.1 pt steps of the first run, down to a minimum percentage) that fits, at layout time so every export sees it. `text.areaOptions` and `document.inspect` report overflow and the shrink factor. The Selection tool shows the type widget beside selected type's bounding box (hollow on point type, filled on area type); double-clicking it converts between them (Type › Convert To Area Type / Convert To Point Type), keeping the text and its styles in place. Variable fonts list every named instance as a style of their family (Figtree Light to Black and their italics, Bahnschrift, Segoe UI Variable), and the instance chosen is shaped, drawn, outlined and measured at its axis settings; PDF and SVG embed it as that instance. The Character panel's Variable Font sliders set each axis (see Fonts). Beyond Illustrator: inline graphics (`text.insertInline`, Type ▸ Insert Inline Symbol) set a document symbol in a run of type as one character that flows, wraps and justifies like a glyph (InDesign-style inline objects, e.g. mana symbols in card rules text): sized to a multiple of the font size, centred on the cap height, opening up tall lines, following Redefine Symbol; a character of its run's size for Character Alignment and Top-to-Top leading, placed by the bidi reordering in right-to-left text (a neutral U+FFFC); drawn on the canvas, kept as live text plus a `<use>` in SVG and as vector art in PDF; Backspace removes it whole. Hebrew and Arabic are laid out right to left with the Unicode bidirectional algorithm (embedded Latin and numbers keep their direction, lines put in visual order after wrapping) in point, area and path type, with caret, selection and arrow keys in visual order; each paragraph's direction comes from its first strong character unless Paragraph Direction sets it (Paragraph panel with Show Indic Options, `text.setFormat {direction}`), and new type aligns to the start of its direction. SVG export outlines right-to-left text. Arabic typefaces: builds made with a craft-fonts checkout that holds its Arabic families (Noto Sans Arabic, the Arabic fallback, plus Cairo, Tajawal, Almarai, IBM Plex Sans Arabic, Noto Kufi Arabic, Amiri, Alexandria, Fustat, Reem Kufi, Aref Ruqaa and Gulzar once craft-fonts adds them, storytold/craft-fonts#11; releases get them when their craft-fonts pin moves) list them in the font menus on desktop; the web build fetches them from beside the wasm (Noto Sans Arabic before start, so Arabic never shows as boxes, the rest in the background). Font Size and Leading are combo boxes in the Character and Properties panels (Font Size in the Control bar too, beside the Character link, font family and style): type, step with ↑/↓ or the spinner, scrub the label, or pick a preset (6–72 pt, shown in the type unit; Leading also Auto), each pick one undo step; Kerning and Tracking list -100…200; a size, leading, kerning or tracking the selected text doesn't share shows blank (#458). Type › Bold and Italic (beyond Illustrator, as page layout apps have them; Cmd+Shift+B / Cmd+Shift+I while the Type tool edits text) switch the selected type to its family's own Bold or Italic face and back, keeping its width (a Narrow face stays Narrow); a family without that face says so (#724). The commands that make or restyle type (and the MCP `add_text` tool) say in their result when area type does not fit its frame, and `add_text` takes Auto Size and Shrink Text to Fit (#1500, fixes #1471). Cmd+Shift+C (Align center) works on Windows and Linux too (#1940). A double-click on area type's bottom middle handle turns on Auto Size (#1940). Print and Print Preview warn about the area type and type on a path that prints without the text that doesn't fit, and give their ids. A tab stop in the Tabs panel drags from where the press landed, a stop just added included (#1487, fixes #1458). Area type in a non-rectangular shape moves a word too wide for the top lines down to the first line that holds it instead of breaking it (#1617, fixes #1615). Stylistic sets (ss01–ss20), stylistic and titling alternates, proportional and lining figures, and superscript and subscript glyphs can be turned on as OpenType features of a character style (`text.setStyle {features}`), and the OpenType panel keeps them (#1611, fixes #1607). Escape while typing ends the edit, keeps the type selected and switches to the Selection tool (#1802, #1686, #1656). Select › Same matches type on its characters' fill and stroke (#1746, #1737). `text.create`, `text.createInPath` and the MCP `add_text` tool take `justify`, so point type can be centred on or end at its point (#1752, #1748).
  The Every-line Composer composes a paragraph whose characters differ in line metrics (type size, font, leading or vertical scale, or an inline graphic taller than the text) in rectangular area type, rows and columns included. In area type of another shape, or with text wrap, such a paragraph is broken with the Single-line Composer.
  The Character panel's Small Caps, Superscript and Subscript buttons and the panel menu's items of the same names turn small caps and the superscript or subscript position on and off for the selected type, or for the text the Type tool has selected (`text.setFormat` or `text.setRangeStyle` `{smallCaps, position}`), in Document Setup's proportions. Turning Superscript on turns Subscript off, and turning Subscript on turns Superscript off. A button or item shows as on when the first selected character (at a caret, the character before it) has its attribute.
- **Paragraph alignment:** the shared Paragraph/Properties alignment row leaves every button unselected when the paragraphs it acts on differ. Auto resolves per paragraph; choosing an alignment uses the existing command. Headless paragraph_mixed_alignment_* regressions exercise mixed → Center → Undo, caret/uniform states, Unicode range boundaries, Auto/direction, split runs and grouped text. These regressions and full integration CI pass. Original captures confirm mixed → Center → Undo in the existing alignment-button layout. The [public Paragraph panel guide](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/design-with-text/edit-format-text/paragraph-panel-overview.html) lists the seven controls, but does not specify mixed-state rendering. Other paragraph fields remain outside this change; scores and hours unchanged.
  For Auto Size area type in columns, the bisection for the frame's height runs on the lines of the one-column layout, and its result is checked with at most two layouts of the columns. When the text wraps around objects or does not fit the one-column layout, or when the check fails, the columns are laid out at every step of the bisection, as before. Typing at the start of a story of 50,000 characters in 2 columns took 1,670 ms a keystroke and now takes 292 ms (release build, `auto_height_in_columns_typing_timing`).
  Exports to PDF, EPS, SVG, EMF, WMF and the raster formats warn about the area type and type on a path that they draw without the text that doesn't fit, and give their ids, as Print and Print Preview do.
  An edit copies a thread's story only when it changes one of the thread's frames: with a story of 50,000 characters threaded through 8 frames with a style change at every word, moving another object took 7.8 ms and now takes 0.013 ms, and a frame of a drag took 7.2 ms and now takes 0.012 ms (release build, `threaded_story_edit_timing`).
  A paragraph that continues from one threaded frame into the next has its first-line indent and bullet or number in the frame where it starts; in the next frame its first line starts where its wrapped lines start. In frames that are no longer threaded, copies of a frame and point type converted from one, the first paragraph has its indent and bullet or number again.
  Type › Convert To Point Type on a frame of threaded text makes point type of the text that frame holds and takes it out of the thread; the story flows through the other frames without that text, so each character is in the document once.
  Type › Create Outlines, Object › Expand and Object › Expand Appearance on a frame of threaded text take it out of the thread with the text it shows, which the outlines draw, and the other frames keep the text they hold. When the last frame is outlined, the text it has no room for goes after the text of the last frame that stays. When Expand Appearance keeps the frame as type in a group with its shadow, outer glow or Crop Marks, the type stays in the thread.
  Object › Flatten Transparency takes a frame of threaded text out of the thread in the same way when Convert All Text to Outlines outlines it or when the frame becomes flat regions or an image, and the other frames keep the text they hold.
  With Optical Margin Alignment on, or Roman Hanging Punctuation on in the first paragraph, the glyphs at the ends of left-to-right type on a path hang outside its brackets, measured along the path. The type hangs at the start bracket when its line is placed there, hangs at the end bracket when the line is placed there, and hangs at both when it is centered. Glyphs that hang past the end bracket do not make the type overflow, and a hang stops at an open path's end. SVG export writes such type as outlines.
  The frames of threaded text share one Optical Margin Alignment setting: turning it on or off in one frame sets it in every frame, threading frames gives the thread its first frame's setting, and frames taken out of a thread keep it.
  Type › Optical Margin Alignment (`type.opticalMarginAlignment`) hangs the punctuation and letter edges at the ends of a type object's lines outside its margins: at the left of left-aligned lines, at the right of right-aligned lines, and at both ends of centered and justified lines, in point and area type of left-to-right paragraphs. Quotation marks, hyphens, full stops and commas hang wholly; asterisks, tildes, ellipses, en and em dashes, colons and semicolons hang by half; and A, V, W, Y, v, w and y hang by a tenth of their width. It is off by default and saved with the type object. Justification's Glyph Scaling leaves the glyphs that hang at their width, so they hang exactly their share, and Standard burasagari counts what hangs at a line's start as room before hanging a comma; `crates/text/src/tests_hang.rs` checks whole paragraphs with both composers, ragged, centred and justified, with Line-end Punctuation Half Width and bidirectional lines.
  Optical Margin Alignment and Roman Hanging Punctuation hang right-to-left paragraphs of point and area type, and type on a path whose first paragraph runs right to left, too. Auto aligns a right-to-left line at its right, or at the end bracket of a path, so it hangs there. A right-to-left line is read from right to left: where it hangs at its left margin, `."` ending it hangs both glyphs.
  The Paragraph panel menu's Hyphenation… (`ui.hyphenation`, `text.setFormat {wordsLongerThan, afterFirst, beforeLast, hyphenLimit, hyphenationZone, hyphenateCapitalized}`) sets each paragraph's hyphenation limits: the shortest word that breaks, the fewest letters on each side of the hyphen, the most hyphenated lines in a row, a zone at the right edge where the Single-line Composer breaks before a word instead of hyphenating it, and whether capitalized words break. The defaults are words longer than 5 letters, 3 letters on each side, no limit or zone, and capitalized words hyphenated; paragraph styles and the native file keep the options.
  PDF export with type as text writes the hyphen that ends a line broken inside a word as a hyphen character where the line draws it, and the file opens with the hyphen in the line's text; kashidas are drawn as paths.
  The Paragraph panel's Insert Kashidas (with the Indic options; `text.setFormat {kashida}`) lengthens each Arabic word of a justified horizontal area type line with a kashida, a tatweel between its last pair of joined letters, before the word spaces widen: Short, Medium and Long kashidas are at most a quarter, half and a whole em long, Stylistic ones are whole tatweels up to an em, and None (the default) leaves the line as before; paragraph styles and the native file keep the setting.
  The Paragraph panel's Bullets button, Type › Bullets and Numbering › Apply Bullets and the context menu's Apply Bullets (`text.setFormat {list, bullet}`, `type.applyBullets`) make paragraphs a bulleted list with the documented presets (none, filled dot, dash, hollow circle, filled square; [Create bulleted or numbered lists](https://web.archive.org/web/20260417034638/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/design-with-text/edit-format-text/create-bulleted-or-numbered-lists.html)): the bullet starts each paragraph's first line in its first character's font, size and color, the first line's text starts at the next tab stop after the bullet (the left indent counts as a stop), the lines it wraps to start at the left indent, a paragraph with no indents gets 18 pt and -18 pt, and Return continues the list; Reset Panel turns it off, and paragraph styles and the native file keep it. The Bullets and Numbering dialog, levels, list detection while typing and Convert to Text are not built yet.
  The Paragraph panel's Numbered List button, Type › Bullets and Numbering › Apply Numbers and the context menu's Apply Numbers (`text.setFormat {list, number}`, `type.applyNumbers`) make paragraphs a numbered list with the documented presets (1, A, a, I, i, 01, 001, and None, which turns the list off; [Bullets and numbering](https://web.archive.org/web/20250807202418/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/bullets-numbering.html), [Create bulleted or numbered lists](https://web.archive.org/web/20260417034638/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/design-with-text/edit-format-text/create-bulleted-or-numbered-lists.html)): each paragraph starts with its number and a period, counted through the list paragraphs of the story and its threaded frames, with the text and indents as in a bulleted list; letters go on from Z to AA, and roman numerals go on from III to IV, an empty paragraph is not numbered, and a paragraph in no list starts the count again at 1.
  The Character panel menu's Character Direction (with the Indic options; `text.setFormat {charDirection}`, `text.setRangeStyle {charDirection}`) sets the selected characters left to right or right to left inside their paragraph, as a Unicode bidi embedding: a date set Left to Right keeps its order in right-to-left text, and a word set Right to Left keeps the punctuation after it on its left. Default (the default) leaves the characters to the bidi algorithm; character styles and the native file keep the setting.
  In vertical type, the Tabs panel names its alignment buttons Top-Justified Tab, Center-Justified Tab, Bottom-Justified Tab and Decimal-Justified Tab, in their tool tips and for screen readers, and labels the position field Y. In horizontal type the buttons keep the names Left-Justified Tab and Right-Justified Tab, and the field keeps the label X.
  The Tabs panel's ruler is numbered in the General unit with the canvas rulers' label steps and a tick every tenth of a step. With the panel menu's Snap to Unit on, or Shift held, a tab stop placed by a click on the ruler or dragged on it lands on the nearest tick (`text.tabs.set`).
  With Snap to Unit off and Shift not held, a tab stop placed by a click on the Tabs panel's ruler or dragged on it lands on the nearest whole point. A position typed in the X or Y field keeps its hundredths of a point.
  When a drag on the Tabs panel's ruler or a value typed in its X field moves a tab stop past another stop, the moved stop stays selected.
  The Tabs panel menu's Clear All Tabs (`text.tabs.clear`), Delete Tab and Repeat Tab (`text.tabs.set`) can be chosen while the panel's ruler shows tab stops. Delete Tab removes the stop selected on the ruler. Repeat Tab replaces the stops after the selected stop with up to 20 copies of it. The copies are spaced by the selected stop's distance from the stop before it, or from the paragraph's left indent when it is the first stop, and no copy is placed at 2,000 pt or beyond. Clear All Tabs removes every stop, so the default stops every ½ inch apply again.
- **Interface languages, vertical type:** Preferences ▸ User Interface (or VectorCraft ▸ Language on macOS) picks Automatic (the system locale) or a registered language, persisted as `interfaceLanguage`. Translations come from per-language catalogs (`i18n/*.tsv`): Traditional and Simplified Chinese, Japanese, German (every `de-*` locale), Spanish (neutral international Spanish, for every `es-*` locale), French (every `fr-*` locale), Italian (every `it-*` locale) Russian (every `ru-*` locale) and Ukrainian (every `uk-*` locale) cover the whole interface, Czech every menu label; Czech, German, Greek, Spanish, French, Hungarian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese, Polish, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Swedish, Ukrainian and Finnish also translate status-bar and error messages as they are shown (`@msg` templates, every message literal tested; the messages themselves stay English for agents); untranslated text stays English. Japanese and Chinese glyphs come from the craft-fonts build input (release builds) or the installed fonts, Czech, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Russian and Ukrainian ones from the bundled UI fonts. The web app follows the browser's languages (or `?lang=`). The Basic toolbar's Type button holds Vertical Type in its flyout. Vertical Type, Vertical Area Type and Vertical Type on a Path create vertical text (columns right to left, upright CJK glyphs and marks with `vert` alternates, Latin and longer numbers on their side, two- and three-digit numbers set as tate-chu-yoko in one em of the column (kept whole when justified), upright glyphs centred on the column (tracked or justified too), point type's anchor on the first column's centre line); kinsoku applies to horizontal and vertical Japanese (Paragraph panel › Kinsoku Set, `text.setFormat {kinsoku}`: Hard, the default, keeps closing marks, iteration marks, the prolonged sound mark and small kana off the line start and opening brackets off its end; Soft lets 々, ー and small kana start a line as JLREQ's level 3 rules do; None turns it off), and justified Japanese lines spread their room between characters (not inside Latin words); Paragraph panel › Mojikumi Set (shown with Preferences › Type › Show East Asian Options, `text.setFormat {mojikumi}`): None or Line-end Punctuation Half Width (new type's default, as in Illustrator; older documents and imported text keep None) shares one half-em space between consecutive punctuation, sets a closing mark ending a line half width and an opening bracket starting a line flush with its start (a paragraph's first line at its first-line indent, JIS X 4051's principle in JLREQ 3.1.5), and puts a quarter em between Japanese and Latin letters or digits; Paragraph panel menu › Top-to-Top / Bottom-to-Bottom Leading measures leading from em box top to top (area type's first line touches the frame) or from baseline to baseline (new type in a Japanese interface starts top to top, with em box centre character alignment, #432); Paragraph panel menu › Burasagari None / Regular / Force (`text.setFormat {burasagari: "none"|"standard"|"forced"}`) hangs an East Asian comma or full stop (、。，．､｡) ending an area type line outside it, Regular (new type's default) when it doesn't fit and Force always (the rest of the line then fills the measure; closing brackets and Latin punctuation don't hang); Character panel menu › Character Alignment (with the East Asian options; `text.setFormat` or `text.setRangeStyle {charAlign}`) lines characters smaller than the largest on their line up on the Roman baseline, the em box top/right, centre or bottom/left, or the ICF (ideographic character face) top/right or bottom/left, from the font's BASE table or, without one, the average ink box of some ideographs and kana; Proportional Metrics (the same menu; `{proportionalMetrics}`) sets full-width glyphs on the font's proportional widths (OpenType `palt`) in horizontal type and upright glyphs on its proportional heights (`vpal`, shaped top to bottom; fonts without vertical metrics keep their cells) in vertical type, and Line-end Punctuation Half Width takes nothing more off the punctuation they re-spaced; Type ▸ Type Orientation switches existing text; caret, selection, hit testing and arrow keys follow the writing direction. Vertical text exports to PDF as real text and to SVG as outlines. The interface is available in Polish (`pl`): menus, panels, dialogs and messages, with one/few/many plurals; AI-drafted, native review pending (#1498).
- **Transparency:** opacity masks (clip/invert/disable/link), exported as SVG `<mask>` and PDF soft masks. The constant alpha soft mask that PDF and `.ai` export draw a CMYK page with transparency through is white, so applications that read every soft mask by its luminosity show the page too (#1359, part of #1286).
  Disable, Enable, Unlink and Link Opacity Mask and Opacity Mask Options (`transparency.setOpacityMask`) record no undo step when every mask they act on already has the flags they set.
- **Image Trace, thin closed outlines:** generated `fit::snap_area_tests` verify nonzero interiors after straightening, opposite closed-boundary winding and Noise controls; see [quality notes](image-trace-quality.md#thin-closed-outlines-with-snap-curves-to-lines). Scores and hours unchanged; open-piece fitting is unchanged.
- **Image Trace, flattened slivers:** in a Color, Grayscale or Black and White trace with Fills, a traced region whose outline straightens onto one line (a single pixel, or a one-pixel row along an edge, its pieces shared with the regions beside it) is left out instead of becoming a selectable path with no area, which paints nothing. Snap Curves To Lines straightens more outlines, so it leaves out more of these. Without Fills, the region's 1 px stroke draws it, and it is kept. Code-drawn tests in `crates/trace`.
- **Image Trace, Auto Color rare colours:** the Automatic palette keeps colours too rare for its area count when they are distinct (Oklab) and drawn as coherent regions, at most six, protected from mixed-colour merging and Noise; code-drawn stem, highlight, low-contrast and scattered-noise tests (see [quality notes](image-trace-quality.md#auto-color-keeps-rare-colours)).
- **Image Trace, source image on hold:** while the eye button next to the Image Trace panel's View is held down, the canvas shows the selected Image Trace objects' source image whatever their View, and shows their View again on release, with no change to the document or the undo history.
- **Image Trace, large images:** images over 1500 px on a side trace with a warning in the result and the status bar; the anchor limit is 8,000,000 (2,000,000 on the web), measured at about 90 bytes an anchor (see [quality notes](image-trace-quality.md#large-images)).
- **Image Trace, Flat Logo working size:** Flat Logo traces at most 1024 px on a side; a larger decoded raster (the 64-megapixel copy for a bigger image) is averaged down in whole-number blocks first, and the trace's `warnings` name the size it was traced at and the image's own size, in place of the slower-trace and 64-megapixel notes; code-drawn 1024 and 1025 px tests in `crates/trace` and `crates/engine`.
- **Image Trace, Flat Logo working size:** Flat Logo traces at most 1024 px on a side; a larger image is averaged down by a whole factor first, and the trace's `warnings` name the size it was traced at and the image's own size, in place of the slower-trace and 64-megapixel notes; code-drawn 1024 and 1025 px tests in `crates/trace` and `crates/engine`.
- **Image Trace, Preview:** the Image Trace panel's Preview checkbox, before Trace, is on by default, and a setting change traces the selected Image Trace object again at once. Off, changes wait in the panel until Trace applies them as one undo step, or until Preview is turned on again. Preview is kept with the UI preferences, and Reset to Default leaves it.
- **Image Trace small contours:** closed fits too small to form an editable subpath retain their positioned outline, including holes. Source-generated island, hole/winding and stepped-region regressions cover Corners and Noise; defaults, parity scores and estimates are unchanged.
- **Create Strokes baseline (2026-10-17, measured):** the ignored centre-lines class covers 23 exact code-drawn scenes in aa and hard variants, including junctions, crossings, fills meeting strokes and varying widths. [Baseline and metric definitions](image-trace-quality.md#centre-lines). Topology is recovered from emitted geometry; width-profile metrics remain unavailable. No behaviour change or score increase.
- **Image Trace, collapsed loops keep few segments:** a loop whose fit collapses to one cubic keeps the fewest segments that hold its area and course, so a higher Paths gives no fewer segments; a code-drawn Paths sweep in `crates/trace` (see [quality notes](image-trace-quality.md#collapsed-loops-keep-few-segments)).
- **Image Trace, notches read only their own piece:** the notch rule of `subpixel::outline` reads only the shared piece, so both regions of an edge cut a corner pixel alike and leave no gap; a code-drawn noisy multi-colour coverage test in `crates/trace` (see [quality notes](image-trace-quality.md#notches-read-only-their-own-piece)).
- **Image Trace, same shift from either side of an edge:** a crack's sub-pixel shift is averaged from its two sides, so abutting regions on one- and two-pixel slivers get the same points and leave nothing uncovered; code-drawn regressions in `crates/trace` (see [quality notes](image-trace-quality.md#same-sub-pixel-shift-from-either-side-of-an-edge)).
- **Image Trace, cut-out edges:** in Color and Grayscale, a semi-transparent pixel (alpha 128 to 254) on the edge of a cut-out image, beside a pixel that is less than half opaque, traces as a color of the fully opaque pixels within two pixels of it when its own color is that color or a darker shade of it, and of several such colors, as the one the most of those pixels have (art across a transparent gap does not count), so a darkened edge tone no longer traces as a 1 px sliver of an unrelated palette color, while a thin semi-transparent outline of another color keeps its own; code-drawn cut-out, opaque-edge and thin-outline tests in `crates/trace`.
- **Image Trace, simpler contour walk:** `contour::trace_mask` works out each turn from the pixels during the walk, with no precomputed direction table and no assertion; identical loops to the previous walk on every 4 × 4 mask (see [quality notes](image-trace-quality.md#a-simpler-contour-walk)).
- **Image Trace, measured:** `crates/trace/tests/quality` traces drawings made from known vector art with every preset and [`image-trace-quality.md`](image-trace-quality.md) records the numbers against the baseline. Black and White, Grayscale and Color place each edge by the blend of the pixels across it (to a fraction of a pixel on anti-aliased and blurred images; hard-edged images are read as staircases) and fit outlines as Flat Logo does. *Measured* on each preset's own inputs, all sizes and variants: Default's outlines went from 0.31 px off on average to 0.09 (largest 1.51 to 1.02), Black and White Logo's from 0.27 to 0.06 with 0.3 kinks per trace where it had 15, and the gaps between abutting paths from 64 px to 22. On clean curved shapes Black and White Logo is 0.02 px off (the open tracer measured beside it: 0.20). The palette is made of the picture's own colours (blends along edges take none of it, colours that noise made of one colour merge, a blend pixel goes to one of the two colours it lies between; #1504): 16 Colors on flat art, all variants, went from 70 paths to 4.2 and from 5.1 px off to 0.13, with no path left in a colour the art doesn't have (5.9 before). Photos are smoothed within their tones before they are quantised and stacked layers go by lightness (#1516): High Fidelity Photo went from 3,653 paths to 121 with its colour error down from 2.30 to 1.75, and a 16 megapixel photo-like image is traced in 3.5 s where 4 megapixels were refused. Since then, by the same harness: outlines are cut at their junctions and each shared piece is fitted once (#1535: gaps and overlaps between abutting paths 22 to 50 px of area down to under 2); layers are traced within the box of their pixels and a few at a time (#1546: a 16 megapixel photo 3.9 GB to 0.9 GB); black and white are read against the image's own black and the paper near each edge (#1563, for thin lines in blurred and scanned art); Ignore Color and the Auto Color and Outline presets (#1574); Snap Curves To Lines levels lines within 2.5 degrees of level or upright (#1593, the angle our choice); Create: Strokes puts centre lines in the middle of their ink and makes them as wide as it (#1595: Outline 0.295 to 0.052 px from the true centre line, 18.4 to 2.7 anchors a stroke); sharp corners whose pixel is mostly outside the shape stay corners (#1609: Default 69% to 76% kept). Three options, each off unless asked for as the legacy presets have them: Shapes (#1609: 57 to 62% of plain circles, ellipses, rectangles and regular polygons come out as live shapes, rounded rectangles rarely), Auto Grouping (#1618: paths grouped with what lies inside them, the same picture) and Gradients (#1627: linear gradients traced as one gradient-filled path; on gradient inputs 6 Colors' colour error 2.12 to 0.62 with 6.4 to 3.4 paths, none found in flat art). Snap Curves To Lines moves no end of a line by more than 1.6 px, so long lines a degree or two off stay as the image has them (#1647: Technical Drawing's largest distance 4.21 px to 1.46). Flat Logo takes the tones a scan's uneven paper makes of one colour for one colour (#1657: on scans 470 paths and 21 px off to 8.5 paths and 0.09 px). Shapes finds rounded rectangles and shapes in aliased, blurred and scanned art (#1845: 57 to 62% of the plain shapes up to 98 to 100%, no false shape but one line 2 px wide). Stroked lines get square caps where their ink is cut square, and a wide end that turned towards a corner goes back on its line (#1846: Outline's largest distance 2.94 px to 0.88, 14 anchors to 10). Each of the 14 documented presets has an enhanced version with Auto Grouping and, in all but High Fidelity Photo, Shapes (#1847), measured beside its preset: equal or better within 0.005 px and 1% of edge ΔE on every preset's own inputs (Default 0.091 to 0.083 px); Auto Grouping keeps traced order in its groups, which removed a light seam along the counters of letters. Gradients grows a gradient over the pixels noise and soft rims took off it (#1848: blurred and noisy linear gradients 3 to 11 paths beside the gradient down to 0.5 with 6 Colors, 24 to 56 down to 0.5 to 1.5 with High Fidelity Photo). Silhouettes is 0.52 px off because its threshold is 200 (0.11 px at 128). Still weak, by the same numbers: rounded rectangles and other line-and-arc outlines take 12 to 16 anchors (the fitter does not split lines from arcs), blurred and scanned polygons lose corners, hairlines under half a pixel are lost to the threshold, aliased art is about 0.25 px off, a scan's uneven paper splits into tones when more colours are asked for than the art has, stroke junctions stay at their skeleton pixels, a three-stop gradient in a small or scanned disc is not found, radial gradients stay bands (a draft, #1849, traces them; the documented option is for linear ones, so it waits for a decision), near-regular polygons a few dozen pixels across are made regular with Shapes (up to 0.5 px off), and aliased stroked lines are 0.8 px off at worst.
- **Gradient mesh from an image:** Object › Create Gradient Mesh (`object.mesh.create`) on an embedded image makes a mesh of 1 to 50 rows and columns over the picture's rectangle, placed with the image's transform; each point takes the alpha-weighted average colour and the opacity of the area around it, and Appearance and Highlight apply. A linked image is refused with a message to embed it (#1676). Scores and hours unchanged.
- **Image Trace Flat Logo mode:** a fourth mode beside Black and White, Grayscale and Color, for flat-colour logos. Each pixel is read as a blend of the logo's colours (found automatically or named), the blend is interpolated smoothly and every outline is placed where two colours are equally present, so edges are accurate to a fraction of a pixel. Outlines are then cleaned: corners the blur rounded are put back, near-straight runs and near-circular arcs become exact lines and arcs, the rest is fitted with as few Béziers as the tolerance allows, touching colours overlap by a hair so no gap opens, and an outline that strays from the raw contour is fitted plainly instead. Gradients and photos are refused with advice to use Color. Line art whose only solid area is white paper (strokes a pixel or two wide) takes its colours from the strokes' cores, with the lighter shades along a stroke's anti-aliased edge folded into its ink; a page whose ink (a channel at least 48 below white) covers under 1% of it traces to nothing, as blank paper does. *Measured* (a local experiment, not run in CI): a flat-colour logo's vector original was rendered down to a soft 199 × 100 px transparent PNG, traced, and the result compared with the original at 1600 px wide. The built-in colour presets (6 Colors, 16 Colors, High Fidelity Photo, Low Fidelity Photo) had a mean edge error of 2.5 to 3.4 px and region overlap of 0.88 to 0.91; Flat Logo had 0.78 px and 0.966 (0.48 px and 0.975 from a crisp source), in about 0.1 s. Limits: flat-colour art only; needle-thin sharp tips are shortened by about 1.7 source pixels because the blur erases them; it works at no more than 1024 px on the long side (larger images are averaged down first); only one logo family has been scored against a vector original.
- **Advanced art:** live Blends (steps/distance/smooth colour, editable spine, anchor-targeted Blend tool, faithful interpolation, knockout), Envelope Distort (warp/mesh/top object, Reset, full Envelope Options, mesh handles, Edit Contents; type, images, symbols, gradients, patterns and appearance distorted everywhere), Liquify tools with options and pen pressure, Puppet Warp with rotating pins, Perspective Grid with presets, movable planes and projected type (choosing a perspective tool shows the grid; Hide Grid hides it with the tool still chosen), Gradient Mesh, Shape Builder (stroke-only open paths and lines cut the regions they cross and enclose regions of their own, and regions they bound merge without seams where the lines cross at rounded coordinates (#893); filled open paths count as closed; erase mode while Alt/Option is held: a minus pointer, red highlights of what will go, a click or drag deletes the regions touched, the pieces of open lines and the edges (outline pieces between the points where paths meet, opening their paths there) it passes over, one undo step, `shapeBuilder.merge {erase}` and `shapeBuilder.regions` edges over MCP), Live Paint (every path an edge, open lines included), Image Trace (12 presets, colour layers traced in parallel; a trace past two million anchor points is refused with advice rather than running out of memory, an image over 64 megapixels is traced scaled down to that size (aspect kept, paths at the image's own size) and one over 192 megapixels is refused, and a selection too large to outline shows its bounds (#525); Object › Image Trace › Make and Make and Expand trace at once with the Default preset, #543; with an image selected the Control bar and the Properties panel show Image Trace, whose arrow traces with any preset, Mask (`object.maskImage`: a clipping path on the image's outline, selected so its handles crop), Crop Image (a crop box on the image, starting on its part over the artboard, dragged by its handles or inside it, the outside dimmed, with X/Y/W/H, Apply and Cancel in the Control bar, Enter and Escape, #734; `object.cropImage {rect}` for agents, `{trim: true}` cuts an image to its pixels that aren't fully transparent, pixel for pixel) and Embed or Unembed in place of Fill and Stroke; with an Image Trace object selected, its Preset (choosing another traces again), View, the Image Trace panel and Expand, plus Release in Properties; the five View modes (Tracing Result, with Outlines, Outlines, Outlines with Source Image, Source Image) redraw a trace on screen without tracing again, are saved with it and `imageTrace.setView` sets them, while exports and Expand keep the result; the panel's Advanced section is a header that stays open or closed as it was left (part of #641); Color mode's Palette: Limited, Full Tone (as many colours as the tones need, Less … More), Automatic (flat art with its own colours, else Full Tone; a heuristic) and Document Library (the most used colours of the document's swatches or a swatch library, filled with the swatch colours as they are), part of #641; Advanced › Create: Fills and/or Strokes, where lines up to the Stroke width trace as stroked centre lines (distance transform, thinning, a skeleton graph with spurs pruned, curve fitting; one width per line; without Fills, wider areas become stroked outlines), part of #641), pattern swatches with pattern editing mode, live Repeat (radial/grid/mirror). A single selected mirror repeat shows a prominent axis with a center move handle and two rotation handles. Drag the line or center to change spacing, or an end to change angle; Shift snaps rotation to 45°. The original artwork stays in place, the reflected copy previews live, Escape cancels and each drag takes one undo step through `object.repeat.options`. Controls follow zoom/view rotation and hide with edges or the bounding box. Engine and headless canvas regressions passed for gestures, history and visibility; native move, rotation and Escape screenshots were reviewed. [Public mirror-repeat reference](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/paint-and-fill/create-and-edit-patterns/set-mirror-repeat-options.html). Object › Expand turns radial, grid and mirror repeats into groups of their instances (#1765, #1756).
  Window › Blend exposes easing Type, Ramp and independent color Shift through `object.blend.options`.
  The four polynomial distributions are original approximations of the public description, not measured
  numeric parity. See [Blend panel overview](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/manage-colors/apply-transparency-and-blending/blend-panel-overview.html).

  - Create Strokes uses exact squared Euclidean distances and Guo–Hall thinning in bounded per-blob crops. Maximal-disc pruning, split-crossing merges and degree-two joins simplify its skeleton graph. The whole-blob width rule and ink fitting remain; 46 code-drawn inputs measure ends and junctions in [`image-trace-quality.md`](image-trace-quality.md#centre-lines). Junction degrees measure 44/45 correct in each input variant; remaining spurs are recorded. This is a measured skeleton improvement; the Image Trace score, missing per-feature selection and width controls, and estimates remain unchanged.
  Object › Live Paint › Merge adds the other selected paths and Live Paint groups to the bottom selected Live Paint group ([Live Paint groups](https://web.archive.org/web/20241230205225/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/live-paint-groups.html)), which keeps its id, the paint of its faces and edges, and its name, lock, visibility, transparency, appearance, opacity mask and graphic style link. Object › Live Paint › Make with a Live Paint group selected, and a Live Paint Bucket click on a selected path beside a selected Live Paint group, add the paths to that group the same way. Make, Merge and the Live Paint Bucket take paths, compound paths and groups of them; with type, an image or another object among the selection they report that it has to be converted to paths first and change nothing, as type and raster images can't go into a Live Paint group directly ([Create Live Paint groups](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/paint-and-fill/learn-painting-basics/create-live-paint-groups.html)); before, such an object went among the group's hidden sources and vanished from the canvas. Evidence: `tests_build::live_paint_refuses_type_and_images_and_changes_nothing`.
  Live Paint Gap Options (Object › Live Paint › Gap Options…, `livePaint.gapOptions`): with Gap Detection on, paint stops at the gaps that run from a loose end of a path to the nearest path, up to Small (3 pt), Medium (6 pt), Large (12 pt) or a custom size; Close Gaps With Paths adds an unpainted path across each gap; Preview applies the options live and draws the gaps in the Gap Preview Color. The options are saved, copied and undone with the group, and Merge keeps the bottom group's options when its Gap Detection is on, or else turns Gap Detection on with Small when another merged group has it on. When Gap Detection is off in every merged group, it stays off.
  View › Show Live Paint Gaps (`view.livePaintGaps`) draws the gaps of the selected Live Paint groups up to their Paint Stops At size, each in its group's Gap Preview Color, until Hide Live Paint Gaps or Hide Edges hides them ([Live Paint gaps](https://web.archive.org/web/20260105111201/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/paint-and-fill/learn-painting-basics/find-and-close-gaps-in-live-paint-groups.html)).
  Double-clicking the Live Paint Selection tool opens its Tool Options ([Live Paint Selection tool options](https://web.archive.org/web/20250904012025/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/selecting-objects.html)): with Select Fills off, a click selects an edge instead of a face; with Select Strokes off, Alt-click selects a face instead of an edge; Color and Width set the color and width of the highlight on the face or edge under the pointer (red and 4 px by default). The options last across tool switches and are saved with the preferences (`tool.setOption {tool: "livePaintSelection"}`).
  Window › Blend opens the Blend panel: Make, the selected blend's Spacing and Orientation (with no blend selected, the options new blends start with), Reverse Front to Back, Reverse Spine, Replace Spine, Expand and Release, each running its Object › Blend command. Make is dimmed until two or more objects are selected. Spacing and Orientation are dimmed until a blend or two or more objects are selected, and the other buttons are dimmed until a blend is selected.
  Objects on Path (#2545): a click with the Objects on Path tool (in Edit Toolbar's Modify section and the Blend tool's flyout; Object › Objects on Path › Attach and the context menu with two or more objects selected choose it) attaches the selected objects to the path clicked, open or closed, in an Objects on Path group with the path at its bottom. The objects go along the path column by column from left to right, spread evenly from its first anchor (the last one sits on the end of an open path), each turned to the path at its attachment point; Pivot and Rotate set where each one attaches and how far it tilts (`object.objectsOnPath.attach`, `object.objectsOnPath.options`). Editing the path moves the objects, an object moved on its own goes back, objects moved into or out of the group in the Layers panel join or leave the path, and Object › Objects on Path › Expand leaves a plain group. The group saves and reopens live and exports as plain art. The Space, Move All, Rotate All and Select/Move widgets, Detach, the tool's options dialog and the Properties panel section are missing.
- **Paint and appearance (M3):**
  - **CSS swatch libraries:** fractional linear and radial gradient stop positions are preserved, so nearby stops such as 12.5% and 12.890625% remain distinct instead of collapsing to 13%. Reference: [CSS Images 3 color stops](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-images-3/#color-stop-syntax). The original synthetic regression is `palette_io::tests::css_preserves_fractional_gradient_stop_positions` in `crates/color/src/palette_io.rs`. Scores and hours are unchanged.
  - **Swatches:** names follow the colour model and are unique; Swatch Options (process/spot, Global, Gray/RGB/HSB/CMYK/Web, live preview); editing a global or spot swatch recolours every linked fill, stroke and text run in one undo step; multi-select and delete with confirmation; New Swatch and New Color Group dialogs (a group from the selected artwork's colours); swatches in colour groups convert, separate and count like any other. The Swatches panel selects ranges and whole groups, has a find field, and drags swatches to reorder, regroup or paint art; Add Used Colors, Select All Unused, Merge, Ungroup and Sort by Kind; a CMYK document keeps applied colours in CMYK. Swatch libraries: nine generated colour libraries and five gradient libraries in a library panel, saved as `.vcswatches`, `.gpl`, swatch exchange (`.ase`) or CSS, and loaded from `.vcswatches`, `.gpl` and `.ase` files (`.ase` both ways: RGB, CMYK, Lab and Gray; global, spot and process; groups) and from color books (`.acb`, read only: the RGB, CMYK or Lab colors of a book such as a Pantone book a user owns, named with its prefix and suffix, spot unless it says process, #831); `swatch.library.copyToUser` copies a loaded library into the User Defined folder without replacing a file, and a file with the same extension and bytes as a User Defined library opens as that library. Tints of global and spot colours ("Name 40%") stay linked and separate as a percentage of their plate. Spot colours can be defined in Lab (Spot Colors options). A built-in [Registration] swatch prints on every plate.
  - **Missing library files:** a persistent swatch or graphic style library panel whose file is gone at startup reopens and stays in the preferences, showing the file's path with Locate Library… (`ui.libraryPanel.locate`), which reads the file from where it is now into the same panel.
  - **Colour:** a Color Picker (colour field, H/S/B/R/G/B channel slider, HSB/RGB/Lab/CMYK fields, hex, web-only snapping, out-of-gamut correction); the Color panel shows a selected colour in its own model and, with nothing selected, the new-art defaults in the mode picked last, which it keeps between sessions; Alt-click paints the other proxy; proxies look through groups and show "?" for mixed paint; Invert, Complement, Apply Last Color (`,`) and Apply Last Gradient (`.`) keep the colour model; every paint command feeds the recent colours. The Color Guide has 21 harmony rules, Steps and Variation options and Limit to Library. Adjust Color Balance (its Global mode shifts tints) and Saturate preview live; Edit Colors and Recolor also reach meshes, images and patterns. Recolor Artwork has colour reduction, five recolour methods, presets, Limit to Library, a colour-wheel Edit tab and Edit Color Group; a local Color Themes panel saves five-colour themes. Fill/Stroke chips open swatch and mixer popovers (the Properties panel has the Control bar's Fill and Stroke chips, Stroke link and weight spinner, with nothing selected too), panels have Illustrator's Window menu keys (Align Shift+F7, Transform Shift+F8, Pathfinder Cmd+Shift+F9, Layers F7, Character Cmd+T…; every panel can be given one in Edit › Keyboard Shortcuts), and Eyedropper Options pick up and apply chosen attributes (Alt and Shift+Alt, image pixels). An ICC CMYK profile converts straight into the RGB working space (not through sRGB, so a wider space such as Wide Gamut RGB keeps colours sRGB can't hold) with the colour settings' black-point compensation, on the canvas and in RGB exports alike (the built-in Generic CMYK compensates both ways, so RGB black separated to a rich black displays as black again). Fills and strokes can overprint (Attributes panel, Overprint Black options), and CMYK documents blend in inks on screen, in PDF and when flattening. Document Color Mode converts the art, symbols, pattern tiles and swatches through the colour settings: Gray stays Gray, RGB greys separate into four-colour greys and a rich black as Illustrator does, or go on the black plate only with `grays: "black"` (also for `document.open {colorMode}`).
    View › Proof Setup › Color blindness – Tritanopia-type turns Proof Colors on and proofs the canvas with the tritanopia simulation of Brettel, Viénot and Mollon (1997). The Separations Preview panel's Proof Setup list offers the same target (`view.proofSetup {target: "tritanopia"}`). Grays keep their value.
  - **Recolor Artwork layout (#3416):** the Edit chip list uses the modal scroll helper and its actual remaining height; the tab's minimum-height space scrolls with the chips. `tests_recolor` covers 5/20/200/400 colors, window resizing, 100/125/150/200% UI scaling, scrolling to and editing the final chip, Preview, Cancel, Confirm and Undo, alongside the existing #1733 drag regressions. Scores and estimates unchanged.
  - **Color Picker layout (#2008):** a centered draggable header, equal-width actions above aligned HSB/RGB/Hex and Lab/CMYK fields, compact field and slider, and warnings below the preview. No horizontal scrolling; narrow windows stack the sections with vertical scrolling. Tests in `dialogs/color_picker.rs` cover actual pointer/key input, typed values before OK/Enter, Cancel/Escape rollback, one Undo step, mode-size stability, warnings and layout at two UI scales. The screen sampler sits above the field and the upstream two-grid Tab order is retained. AccessKit regressions check the action names and each channel slider's displayed value, units and range. German and enlarged English UI renders were reviewed locally; no reference images are shipped. This is a layout improvement, with no change to scores or remaining-hour estimates.
  - **Eyedropper sources (#1251):** ordinary and Shift clicks, Shift+Alt appearance append, raster pixels and gradient-stop sampling can read visible locked/template art and sources outside isolation. Sampling leaves the source and selection intact; Alt reverse still uses editable hits, and hidden art stays excluded. Engine/tool/hit regressions cover the editing boundary, color models and one-step Undo/Redo. The general object/image workflow is described in [public HelpX](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/tool-techniques/eyedropper-tool.html); the lock/isolation expectations come from the user report and these regressions, without a new full-parity measurement.
  - **Eyedropper colors in a CMYK document (#2276):** a CMYK image (a four-component JPEG, or an 8- or 16-bit chunky CMYK TIFF) gives its ink amounts as they are, and an RGB image's pixel or an RGB color given to `paint.setFill`, `paint.setStroke`, `paint.sampleColor` or `swatch.new {color}` (hex input and gradient stops included) is separated through the color settings' CMYK working space and intent, as Document Color Mode converts it. With the default Generic CMYK, RGB 83/170/223 separates to C59 M12 Y3 K0, where the profile-free formula gave C63 M24 Y0 K13.
  - **RGB input to other commands in a CMYK document:** type colors (`text.create`, `text.setStyle`, `text.setRangeStyle`), a Shape Builder hex fill, `paint.editGradient` stops, freeform gradient points, gradient mesh points (the Mesh tool gives a new point the fill's color in its own model), the Symbol Stainer's color and the swatch commands (`swatch.new {colors}`, `swatch.newGroup`, `swatch.editGroup`, `swatch.edit`) separate RGB through the color settings as `paint.setFill` does: with Generic CMYK, `text.setStyle {fill: "#53aadf"}` gives C59 M12 Y3 K0. A color a swatch already has keeps its model, and a swatch color given with `mode` is converted into that mode only.
  - **Swatches made from a shown color in a CMYK document:** the Color panel menu's Create New Swatch, an Alt-click on the Swatches panel's New Swatch button, the New Swatch dialog for a gradient, a Fill or Stroke proxy or the Gradient panel's thumbnail dropped on the Swatches panel (or Alt-dropped on a swatch of its kind), and the Gradient panel's Add to Swatches and Save to Swatches keep each color's model, as the Color Guide's and Color Themes' saved colors do: an RGB object's color gives an RGB swatch, and a gradient's RGB stops stay RGB.
  - **Sample Color from Screen:** an eyedropper button in the Color Picker and `ui.sampleScreenColor` (which can be given a key in Keyboard Shortcuts) pick a color anywhere on the screen with the system's sampler: `NSColorSampler` on macOS, the EyeDropper API in browsers that have it. The color becomes the fill or the stroke as one undo step, or the Color Picker's color, converted from display sRGB into the working RGB space. Windows, Linux and other browsers have no sampler yet; the button is gray there.
  - **Stroke visibility (#1253):** adding paint to a previously unpainted zero-width stroke restores the existing 1 pt default (`PaintDefaults::default`, `Appearance::set_stroke`), for the selected appearance item, the new-art defaults and Swap Fill/Stroke. Positive widths are kept; recoloring a painted zero-width stroke keeps its explicit zero. A real Eyedropper-to-new-shape sequence reproduces the zero-width inheritance. Five engine regressions cover creation, defaults, targeted items, preserved widths and one-step Undo/Redo (`crates/engine/tests/it/stroke_visibility.rs`).
  - **Gradients:** lossless, validated gradient params; gradients follow rotate, reflect, shear, non-uniform scale and distortions; the Gradient tool edits the fill or stroke of the active proxy, type included; an interactive on-canvas annotator (move, length/angle, rotate, add/move/delete/duplicate stops, midpoints, a stop popover, Delete and arrow keys). The Gradient panel has the Fill/Stroke proxy, a gradient-swatch dropdown with Save to Swatches, midpoint locations, Alt-drag to copy or swap stops, swatch drops on the ramp and a stop eyedropper; copied appearances and graphic styles place gradients on each target's own bounds; gradient handles snap and honour Constrain Angle. Gradient stops stay linked to global and spot swatches. Freeform gradients (points and lines) are edited on the canvas; radial gradients have an extent ellipse, an aspect handle and an off-centre focal point (SVG `fx`/`fy`, PDF two-point radials). A stroke's gradient runs within, along or across it. Object ▸ Expand turns gradients into N objects or a gradient mesh.
    With a gradient stop or a freeform gradient point selected, Alt-clicking a color swatch in the Swatches panel recolors it instead of the inactive Fill or Stroke.
  - **Freeform gradient colors in their own model:** Object ▸ Expand and Object ▸ Create Gradient Mesh (`object.mesh.create`) mix a freeform gradient's points in the color model they share: points of C50 M20 Y0 K10 give mesh points of C50 M20 Y0 K10, and RGB points keep their values in a working RGB space other than sRGB. Points in different models mix in display RGB, and a CMYK document stores the result as CMYK through the color settings. Points colored along CMYK stops (`paint.editGradient {stops}`, or a CMYK gradient switched to freeform) are CMYK, and so are a point `paint.freeform.splitLine` adds between CMYK points and a point `paint.freeform.addPoint` adds without `color` to CMYK points. Public reference: [Gradients](https://web.archive.org/web/20250714042311/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/gradients.html) and [Meshes](https://web.archive.org/web/20250812201019/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/meshes.html), which do not state how colors in different models mix; the rule is VectorCraft's own.
  - **Strokes:** one stroke-geometry module shared by the canvas, SVG, PDF and Outline Stroke; dotted lines (zero-length dashes draw dots or squares); arrowheads with hollow outlines, tip-on-end or extend-past-end alignment and one opacity for line and head. SVG and PDF export arrowheads, width profiles, brushes and aligned strokes exactly as the canvas draws them; Outline Stroke and the live Outline Stroke effect outline every stroke item as drawn (dashes, heads, profiles, alignment); dashes can be fitted to corners and path ends; width profiles carry through dashes, and their corners take the join. The Stroke panel edits type's character strokes, follows the stroke units (its weight presets are round values in that unit: `0.25 mm`, `0.0625 in`, `1 px`, #426; fields show four decimals in mm, cm and inches, three in points), shows mixed values blank and opens from the Control bar. A width profile library, thirty more arrowheads, and Width Point Edit with multi-select and discontinuous points. Visual bounds and clicks cover the whole painted stroke. Scale Strokes & Effects, Scale Corners and Use Preview Bounds work everywhere, and new art inherits stroke options, a graphic style or the whole last appearance.
  - **Brushes (part of #852):** double-clicking a brush in the Brushes panel (or the panel menu's Brush Options…) opens Calligraphic Brush Options (Name; Angle, Roundness and Size, each Fixed, Random or Pressure with its Variation; live previews of the nib and of a light–heavy–light stroke) or Bristle Brush Options (Shape and the bristle sliders); OK edits the brush and every stroke painted with it. The Paintbrush records the pen pressure along each stroke (kept with the path, saved, and joined when a stroke continues a path); a Calligraphic value on Pressure goes from value − variation at the lightest pressure to value + variation at the heaviest, on the canvas and in SVG, PDF and the other exports. Brushes saved before keep their look. Scatter Brush Options (Size, Spacing, Scatter and Rotation, each Fixed, Random between two values or Pressure from the first at the lightest pressure to the second at the heaviest; Rotation relative to Page or Path), Art Brush Options (Width, Scale Proportionately, Stretch to Fit Stroke Length or Stretch Between Guides with the guides' start and end, the four Directions, Flip Along and Across) and Pattern Brush Options (Scale, Spacing, the five tiles shown, Flip Along and Across, Stretch to fit, Add space to fit or Approximate path) each have Colorization (None, Tints, Tints and Shades, Hue Shift with its Key Color picked from the art's colours) and a live stroke preview; values from files and commands are clamped to their ranges. Still to come: the Art brush's Overlap, auto-generated Pattern brush corners, new tile art picked in Pattern Brush Options, Stylus Wheel, Tilt, Bearing and Rotation, and pen pressure on macOS.
    Type in a scatter brush's art takes the brush's colorization as its paths do: Tints, Tints and Shades and Hue Shift recolor the characters' solid fills and strokes in each copy the brush draws, and Brush Options' Key Color list, whose first color is Hue Shift's default key, counts the characters' fills and their strokes wider than 0. The Brushes page says that a scatter, art or pattern brush takes its colors from the current stroke color and the brush's colorization method (<https://web.archive.org/web/20241230205225/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/brushes.html>) and does not mention type there; recoloring the characters' paints like the art's fills and strokes is VectorCraft's own rule. The Symbol Stainer mixes the characters' strokes of type toward the stain as it mixes their fills. Evidence: `tests::scatter_colorization_recolors_type`, `tests::art_colors_list_the_most_used_first`, `tests::stain_mixes_type_strokes_too` (vectorcraft-brush).
    Art Brush Options' Width (1% to 1000%) and Pattern Brush Options' Scale (1% to 10000%) each have a slider beside the field, over the same range in whole percents; screen readers name the slider as its row and read the field's value.
    Scatter, Art and Pattern Brush Options have the Tips button for Colorization that the [Brushes](https://web.archive.org/web/20241230205225/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/brushes.html) page (archived copy) describes, beside Method. It opens Colorization Tips, which shows each method's name and what it does beside a sample of the brush, as OK would make it, painted with that method on a blue stroke; Hue Shift's sample uses the dialog's Key Color. `ui.dialog.set {field: "tips", value: true}` opens it. Screen readers name the button, the popover and each sample.
    Hue Shift set by `brush.new` or `brush.options` without a key color takes the color the art's fills and strokes use most, as Brush Options already offers it, following the Brushes page, where the key color defaults to the color that stands out most in the art (<https://web.archive.org/web/20241230205225/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/brushes.html>). The page does not state how prominence is measured. Counting the fills and strokes that use each solid color, with the first one found winning a tie and black for art with no solid color, is VectorCraft's own rule. A `brush.options` edit that gives only the method keeps the brush's key color, and one that gives only an art brush's start guide keeps its end guide. Evidence: `tests_brushsym::hue_shift_without_a_key_takes_the_most_used_art_color`, `tests_brushsym::art_brush_options_keep_the_scale_fields_an_edit_leaves_out`.
    Bristle Brush Options and `brush.new` take a bristle brush name of at most 31 characters, as the Brushes page states for the Bristle Brush Options. The Name field stops taking characters at 31, and `brush.new` and `brush.options` refuse a longer new name with an error that names the limit. The page does not say how the limit counts characters or what happens to longer names already saved; counting characters and the number added to a taken name, keeping longer saved names, and leaving `brush.duplicate` unlimited are VectorCraft's own rules. A bristle brush that a document or a saved file already holds under a longer name keeps it, and the other brush types take a name of any length. Test: `bristle_brush_names_have_at_most_31_characters` in `tests_brushsym.rs`. Public reference: [Brushes](https://web.archive.org/web/20241230205225/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/brushes.html) (archived copy).
    In the Brushes panel, Shift-click selects a range of brushes and Ctrl/Cmd-click adds or removes one. Delete Brush and Duplicate Brush then act on all of them (`brush.delete {names}`, `brush.duplicate {names}`).
    Document Info has a Brushes category after Graphic Styles. It lists the Brushes panel's brushes, or with Selection Only it lists the brushes that the selected objects' strokes use. The Document Info report and Package's report list them too (`document.info {category: "brushes"}`, `brushNames`).
    Document Info has a Repeat Objects category after Embedded Images. It lists each radial, grid and mirror Repeat object by name with its kind and the number of instances it makes. For a grid it gives the rows and columns instead, followed by the number of instances it draws when that is fewer. With Selection Only it lists the Repeat objects in the selection. The Document Info report and Package's report list them too (`document.info {category: "repeats"}`, `repeatObjects`).
    The Brushes panel menu's Select All Unused selects the brushes that are not used in the document, as the [Brushes](https://web.archive.org/web/20241230205225/https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/brushes.html) page (archived copy) describes. A brush counts as used when a stroke paints with it in the art (opacity masks included), in symbols, graph designs, pattern tiles or graphic styles, or in the art of a used brush (`brush.unused`).
    A rename in Brush Options and Delete Brush change every stroke that paints with the brush: in the layers and opacity masks, symbols, graph designs, pattern tiles, graphic styles and the art of other brushes. A rename gives those strokes the new name, and Delete Brush makes them plain strokes, in one undo step.
  - **Appearance:** the Appearance panel's selected row drives every paint, stroke, gradient and transparency edit (`item` on the commands); effects apply to one fill or stroke; per-item Opacity popups, whose blend-mode list and opacity slider stay open inside them (#430; the Control bar's Stroke popover too); Mixed Appearances, Layers target dots and basic-appearance rules. Effects can be reordered, moved between items and copied by dragging; Show All Hidden Attributes; clicking an effect edits it in place; the object thumbnail drags onto art; effects render on type, images, symbols, blends, envelopes, meshes and repeats, and per-item raster effects export. Groups, layers and type have their own fills, strokes and effects (Contents and Characters rows); the Layers panel's target circles target layers, groups and objects; Expand Appearance turns fills, strokes, effects and brushes into objects.
    Fill and stroke paint (Fill, Stroke, None, Apply Last Color and Apply Last Gradient, also on characters selected with the Type tool), the Stroke panel's options, gradient and freeform point edits, Swap Fill and Stroke, Default Fill and Stroke, the Eyedropper, and the Appearance panel's item edits, Clear Appearance, Reduce to Basic Appearance, Remove Item, item reordering and Move Appearance record no undo step when they change nothing.
    An image's own fills and strokes draw the shape that a Convert to Shape or Outline Object effect on them gives them (the image's box or its frame, reshaped by the effects after it), under or over the image as its Contents row says, on the canvas, in exports and through Expand Appearance; new fills and strokes on an image go under it. Without one of those effects they draw nothing, and Use Preview Bounds measures an image by its frame.
    A geometry effect on one of type's own fills or strokes reshapes the whole outline that the fill or stroke paints, on the canvas and in exports; PDF, SVG, EPS and the other vector exports write such type as paths. On type that holds inline graphics, those effects are drawn and exported only when the type has a geometry effect or perspective of its own.
    The Appearance panel's inline effect editor labels each parameter as the effect dialogs' generic fields do, without the colon ("Max. Radius", "Channel 1", "Create New Fields by"). Roughen's and Zig Zag's Points, Offset Path's Joins, Inner Glow's Source and the menus of Radial Blur, Smart Blur, Sprayed Strokes, Glass, Mezzotint, Halftone Pattern, Grain, Texturizer and De-Interlace are dropdowns with the dialog's labels that send the dialog's values, and a plug-in's choice is a dropdown of the plug-in's values.
    Revolve's edge, Extrude & Bevel's bevel, every Warp style's orientation, Rasterize's Color Model, Background and Anti-aliasing and the channel of Levels and Curves are dropdowns too, with the labels their own dialogs show. `effect.apply` and `effect.setParams` refuse a Levels or Curves `channel` other than `rgb`, `red`, `green` or `blue` (or `r`, `g` and `b`, in any letter case).
  - **Masks and clipping:** opacity-mask controls work while the mask is being edited; transparency commands take ids and work without a selection; clipping sets clip by compound paths, even-odd paths, text and groups on screen and in raster export, matching SVG/PDF. Alt-click shows only the mask; SVG masks keep Clip and Invert; the transparency grid is per-document state; a clipping path's own fill and stroke paint behind and over the clipped art; layers can be clipping masks.
  - **Masks and clipping:** opacity-mask controls work while the mask is being edited; transparency commands take ids and work without a selection; clipping sets clip by compound paths, even-odd paths, text and groups on screen and in raster export, matching SVG/PDF. Alt-click shows only the mask; SVG masks keep Clip and Invert; the transparency grid is per-document view state saved in native files (#1968); a clipping path's own fill and stroke paint behind and over the clipped art; layers can be clipping masks.
  - **Transparency:** three-state Knockout Group (on, neutral, off), Opacity & Mask Define Knockout Shape, Page Isolated Blending and Page Knockout Group, on screen and in SVG/PDF. SVG export writes a knockout group of opaque art plainly, without masks, so shapes meeting edge to edge leave no seam; translucent, blended, masked or brushed art knocks out through masks. Blend modes match the standard formulas on screen, in SVG and in PDF, and non-isolated groups blend with the art below. Flatten Transparency with presets, a dialog and a Flattener Preview panel. Flattening for files without transparency (PDF/X-1a, PDF/X-3) in a CMYK document keeps the inks where it rasterizes, as under an image with see-through pixels: the images it makes hold ink amounts, not screen colours the file would separate again, so a C100 M6 Y41 K3 panel stays C100 M6 Y41 K3 there (#2160, `engine/src/cmd/fileio/tests_pdfx.rs`).
    On the canvas, the renderer no longer draws the picture of the art below back as an image each time it copies the backdrop of a non-isolated group that blends: it keeps that picture and draws the art that follows over it. At 2880 × 1800, 50 translucent groups with Multiply members take 65 ms a frame instead of 299 ms on 8 threads (`vectorcraft-cli bench`), and the frames have the same pixels.
    Type inside a group, layer, symbol instance, blend or repeat keeps its opacity, blend mode, opacity mask, Opacity & Mask Define Knockout Shape, own effects, perspective and visibility when the effects on the container outline it. Hidden type with a geometry effect of its own is left out of exports.
  - **Graphic styles:** styles keep opacity and blend mode, capture groups and type, apply on top with Alt, and link to the objects using them; Redefine, Break Link, Graphic Style Options, Select All Unused, Sort by Name, and Select > Same Graphic Style / Appearance Attribute. The panel has list and thumbnail views with rendered previews, merge, reorder and drag and drop, plus a Control bar Style picker; six generated style libraries save and load as `.vcstyles`.
    In the Graphic Styles panel, Shift-click selects a range of styles and Ctrl/Cmd-click adds or removes one.
  - **Neutral wording:** labels, MCP tool text, docs and packaging use neutral names, and `cargo xtask brands` (part of `cargo xtask ci`) fails on vendor names.
- **Colour, type and file workflows:** Recolor Artwork (dialog with harmonies), Edit Colors, Find & Replace, Change Case, Smart Punctuation, Guides, Lock/Hide Above, Transform Each, Rasterize.
  Object › Lock › All Artwork Above and Object › Hide › All Artwork Above deselect the selected objects they lock or hide, the key object included.
  Liquify (its brush Width, Height and Angle, Intensity, Detail, Simplify, Twirl Rate, Complexity, Horizontal and Vertical), Puppet Warp (its Expand and each pin's angle), Transform in Perspective (its depth), Nudge in Perspective (its direction) and Move Plane (its location or distance) refuse a value other than a number or null, such as "40", Draw in Perspective refuses a click point that is not two numbers, and Width Profile refuses a point that is not three numbers; each leaves the document and its undo history as they were.
  Object › Lock › All Artwork Above and Object › Hide › All Artwork Above go through each top-level layer once, checking each object that is not selected against the selected objects below it: with 100 tiles selected under 25,000 rectangles, Lock took 6.4 s and now takes under 0.1 s, and with all of 5,001 objects selected it took 8.8 s and now takes under 0.1 s.
  Lock Grid, Lock Station Point, Snap to Grid and Show Rulers (View › Perspective Grid) and Import Perspective Grid Presets (its choice to replace saved presets of the same names) refuse a value other than true, false or null, such as "true", and leave the grid and the saved presets as they were.
  All Artwork Above and Other Layers (Object › Lock and Object › Hide), Transform Each, Rearrange All Artboards, the width point and width profile commands, Liquify, Puppet Warp, Define Perspective Grid, Attach to Active Plane, Release with Perspective, moves and transforms in perspective, Move Plane and Move Plane to Match Object record no undo step when they change nothing.
  Move in Perspective (its copy, perpendicular and Snap to Grid choices), Transform in Perspective (its copy), Nudge in Perspective (its ×10 and copy), Draw in Perspective (Snap to Grid), Define Perspective Grid (its reproject choice), Show Perspective Grid, Width Point (Adjust Adjoining Width Points), Liquify (its pen pressure, Simplify and Affect choices) and Puppet Warp (its pins' rest shape) refuse a value other than true, false or null, such as "true", and leave the document and its undo history as they were.
  Create Object Mosaic (its columns and rows), Transform Each (its reference point and Random seed) and Rearrange All Artboards (its columns) refuse a fraction, a negative number or a string, such as 2.5, -1 or "4"; 4.0 counts as 4.
  Move, Rotate, Scale, Reflect, Shear, Transform Again, Nudge and the Transform panel's values (their copy, Scale Strokes & Effects, Scale Corners, Transform Patterns, Transform Objects and area type options), Align, Distribute and Distribute Spacing (Transform Patterns), Object Properties (visible, locked, Isolate Blending and Opacity & Mask Define Knockout Shape) and Live Shape Properties (Invert Pie, Make Sides Equal and relative rounding) refuse a value other than true, false or null, such as "false", and leave the document as it was.
  Object Properties (its opacity), Live Shape Properties (corner radius and polygon sides), the Transform panel's reference point and Align, Distribute and Distribute Spacing to an artboard (the artboard's number) refuse a value other than a number or null, such as "50", and leave the document as it was.
  Transform Each (its scales, moves and rotation), Rasterize (its resolution), Create Object Mosaic (its new width and height and its spacing), Create Trim Marks (its offset, length, bleed and weight) and Rearrange All Artboards (its spacing) refuse a value other than a number or null, such as "50", and change nothing. Crop Image refuses a rectangle that is not four numbers, such as "0, 0, 20, 20".
  Transform Each (Reflect X, Reflect Y, Random, Copy, Scale Strokes & Effects, Scale Corners, Transform Objects and Transform Patterns), Create Object Mosaic (gray tiles and deleting the image), Crop Image (its trim), Create Trim Marks (all artboards) and Rearrange All Artboards (by column, Move Artwork with Artboard and Transform Patterns) refuse a value other than true, false or null, such as "false", and change nothing. Create Trim Marks refuses a style that is not text, such as 5.
