  Artboard Options (Move Artwork, Scale Artwork, Scale Strokes & Effects, Scale Corners, Transform Patterns, locked and hidden art and the lock), Move Artboard (Move Artwork, the copy and Transform Patterns), Duplicate Artboards (Transform Patterns) and Duplicate, Copy and Cut Artboard (the art) refuse a value other than true, false or null, such as "true", and Artboard Options and Move Artboard refuse a position, size or move given as text, such as "10"; each leaves the document, its undo history and the clipboard as they were.
  Change Case, Smart Punctuation, Find and Replace, Convert To Area Type, Convert To Point Type, Type on a Path Options, the Type on a Path effects and Fill with Placeholder Text record no undo step when they change nothing.
  The commands that take `keepModel` (fills and strokes, Appearance rows, Live Paint, Shape Builder fills, gradient stops and freeform points, gradient mesh points, type colors, the Symbol Stainer and the swatch commands) refuse a `keepModel` other than true, false or null, such as "true". Toggle Fill/Stroke Focus (`fill`), Invert, Complement, Apply Last Color and Apply Last Gradient (`stroke`), `paint.setFill` and `paint.setStroke` (`focus`, `none`), and `appearance.setItem`, `livePaint.fill`, `livePaint.strokeEdge`, a `shapeBuilder.merge` `fill`, `swatch.new` and `swatch.edit`'s `paint` (`none`) refuse such a value too. Each leaves the document, its undo history and the defaults for new art as they were.
  The shape tools' commands (Rectangle, Polygon, Star, Flare, Spiral, Arc, Rectangular Grid and Polar Grid), `path.create` (with `anchors` or `d`), the type commands (new type, type in a path, character formats, the byte range a text command takes, Touch Type, font size steps, `text.getRange`, Optical Margin Alignment, System Layout, Fractional Widths, Ruby and Area Type Options), the symbol commands (Place, Delete, the Symbol Sprayer and the symbolism tools), the swatch commands, the Appearance panel's commands, the gradient and freeform gradient commands, Shape Builder, Live Paint and Image Trace refuse an option other than true, false or null and a number given as text, such as "true" or "40", and leave the document and its undo history as they were.
- **Fonts:** a font is found by any of its names (family and style in every language of its name table, legacy family/style pairs, PostScript name), so documents from other apps open with the font they name; Find Font and `text.fonts` say for each font whether it was found exactly, by another name, substituted or missing, and how many glyphs are missing. PDF and `.ai` import brings Japanese text back as live type: CID fonts without a ToUnicode map read through the standard CMaps, vertical columns (WMode 1) as vertical type, letter spacing as tracking; a glyph is live type only when the installed font (in the closest style of its family) draws the same glyph, and text in a font that isn't installed comes in as live type shown in the fallback font until the font is installed (exports that draw it — PDF, EPS, EMF/WMF, raster, SVG outlines or embedded fonts — warn that they wrote the fallback font, and Print and Print Preview warn about the type that prints in it; `textAs: outlines` keeps the PDF's embedded glyphs). Two installed versions of one family and style (a font library keeping an old file beside a new one) both load, the first staying the one the family and style resolve to; PDF and `.ai` import tries each version when the glyphs differ, and type set in a version other than that one names it (`CharStyle::font_version`), which layout, the substituted-glyph highlight, Find Font, Package and Document Info follow. Fonts outside the font folders are listed too: those font services such as Adobe Fonts load on Windows, through DirectWrite, and those apps and font managers register with CoreText on macOS (#579). When a document opens with fonts that aren't available, fonts used only in symbols included, a Missing Fonts dialog lists them after the linked-file questions, with Find Fonts (Type › Find Font on them) and Close. Its Find in Folder… (in Find Font too) searches a folder on several threads, reads only what the font scan reads of font files and skips app packages, the Program Files and ProgramData folders, the system's folders and the app data folders in a home folder; Add Fonts copies the font files the user chooses, suitcase fonts with their resource fork, into VectorCraft's own Fonts folder, which the desktop app and `vectorcraft-cli` read (`text.missingFonts`, `text.findFontFiles`, `text.addFontFiles`). The font scan on Linux also reads the folders fontconfig's configuration lists, such as TeX fonts under `/usr/share/texmf/fonts` (#1548, fixes #1529; not verified on Linux).
  A variable font's type gets one slider and field per variation axis under the Character panel's Variable Font button, each named as the font names the axis (Weight, Width), so the type can be set between or past its named instances: the settings stay with the characters (`CharStyle::font_axes`, `text.setFormat {fontAxes}` and `text.setRangeStyle {fontAxes}`, clamped to each axis's range; `text.fontList {family, style}` lists the axes), and layout, outlines, the substituted-glyph highlight and PDF and SVG export (`font-variation-settings`, embedded fonts) use the font instanced at them. Another font or style clears them; legacy `.ai` export writes the style and warns that they are left out.
  The font menu's Font Technology › Variable (under the kind filter, as [Find, apply, and adjust variable fonts](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/design-with-text/fonts-and-scripts/find-apply-and-adjust-variable-fonts.html) places Variable in the classification filter's Font Technology section) lists only the families with variation axes, a family with a variable file beside static ones included, and works together with the script, kind, ★ and search filters; it stays set from one opening to the next. Measured by `font_menu::tests::the_variable_filter_lists_only_variable_families`, `font_menu::tests::the_variable_filter_is_named_as_fonts_are`, `tests_axes::a_family_with_variation_axes_is_variable` and `tests_sysfonts::a_family_with_a_variable_file_beside_static_ones_is_variable`.
  The font database looks up a name that is neither a loaded nor an installed family among the other names of the loaded and installed fonts once for each style it is asked in, and keeps the answer until fonts are added or rescanned. Laying out a story of 1,000 paragraphs set in a font that is not installed, with 400 more fonts loaded, takes a median of 56 to 71 ms instead of 409 to 507 ms on Windows 11 (`CRAFT_FONTS_DIR=<craft-fonts checkout> cargo test --release -p vectorcraft-text --lib missing_font_story_layout_timing -- --ignored --nocapture`).
  A font family removed while the app runs leaves the font menus when the app scans the font folders again (when its window comes to the front after a font folder changed, or Refresh Font List), also when type had used it: that type then draws in the fallback font and Find Font lists the font as missing, until the font is installed again and the folders are scanned.
- **Files (M4):**
  - PDF export and print composition use the optional shared guarded writer ([pdf-backend.md](pdf-backend.md)); app drawing and output policy and desktop printer submission remain in their existing layers. The shared reader keeps the app-owned import adapter; synthetic tests cover layer and overprint state across windows, long operands, inline images, failed decoding, document limits and incomplete tails. Empty and populated metadata key presence is regression-tested, and CI checks the immutable backend source.
    Invisible text in a PDF (rendering mode 3, which carries a scanned page's recognized text over the scan) opens as type with no fill or stroke, a run of its own beside visible text on the same line; text that can't come in as type (opened as outlines, Type 3 fonts) is left out with a warning. PDF export, and printing, write characters with no fill or stroke as real text in rendering mode 3, so they draw nothing but stay selectable and searchable, also in PDF/X-1a and PDF/A-2b (#2675, `pdf/src/tests_import_fidelity.rs`, `pdf/src/tests_realtext.rs`).
    A PDF, or a `.ai` read through its PDF part, whose spot inks have the same values but different names opens with a spot swatch for each ink. The solid fills and strokes of paths and type, and the stops of gradients on paths, link to the swatch of the ink they are painted in, the points of a gradient mesh in one of these inks keep the ink's color, and PDF export writes each of these inks as its own separation (`pdf/src/tests_import_color.rs`). Paint in these inks inside pattern cells, soft masks and type 3 glyphs, and gradients on type in these inks, still import as RGB. Type in one of these inks can also import as RGB when type in another Separation or DeviceN ink is shown with no path drawn between them.
  - `.vectorcraft` (lossless JSON, compressed, atomic saves, save down to v1), Save As with a format chooser, Save a Copy, Revert, templates, Data Recovery after a crash (browser tabs hold their copies with Web Locks too, so a background tab's copies are never taken for a crash's, and a tab repairs copies another removed when it resumes: #367), background save and export. The desktop app writes its warnings and errors (graphics adapter, a lost graphics device, panics the guard recovered from) to standard error and to `logs/vectorcraft.log` next to the preferences, the two previous runs kept and each file capped at 16 MiB, so a launch without a terminal still leaves something to attach to a bug report (#465). Native documents with a lot of path data (traced or generated art, in layers, symbols or patterns) are saved as compact JSON, about a fifth of the size; small documents stay pretty-printed (#1492). Saving to a network drive on macOS falls back to a plain fsync when the share refuses a full flush (#1625, part of #1620; not confirmed on a real share), and a save still succeeds when a folder refuses the temporary file, the rename over the document or copying permissions: the content is written elsewhere first and copied in, and a failed copy keeps the temporary file and names it (#1649, part of #1620). A document opened by a relative path finds its relatively linked images, and `vectorcraft-cli convert` lists what reading the input left out as `importWarnings` (#1606, fixes #1604).
    A name typed in the desktop save panel without the file type's extension gets it, and when a file of that name exists, which the panel did not ask about, Save, Save As, Save a Copy, Save as Template, the exports and every other write through a save panel ask before replacing it (dialog `replaceFile`; Cancel writes nothing).
    A name returned by the desktop save panel with the extension of a format the save does not write has it replaced with the saved format's: Save As of a new document saves `card.ait` and `card.png` as `card.vectorcraft`, and Save as Template saves `card.pdf` as `card.vctemplate`. An extension that names no format stays part of the name (`notes.v2` is saved as `notes.v2.vectorcraft`).
    Export As, Save as PDF, Save for Office Documents, Save for Web, Text Export Options, print to file, the presets' Export… and the library, swatch and Document Info saves replace a typed extension of another format than the one they write in the same way: Export As PNG writes `card.svg` as `card.png`, Save as PDF writes `card.png` as `card.pdf`, and `document.exportSelection` with a `format` suggests and adds that format's extension. An extension of the written format stays as typed in any letter case (`photo.JPEG` for JPEG), Export As SVG writes `art.svgz` compressed, and `document.exportSelection` without a `format` writes the format the typed extension names (`tests_saveext.rs`).
  - macOS: the save sheet of Save As, Save a Copy, Save as Template and the first Save of a new document has a Format menu that lists each format the save can write, with the suggested file's format selected. Choosing a format changes the extension in the name field, and a name typed without an extension gets the chosen format's. A name typed with another listed extension is saved in that format. The menu is set up before the sheet opens; a save panel with one file type is shown by rfd as before (#866, `apps/vectorcraft/src/mac_save_format.rs`).
  - Linux and the BSDs: the save dialog of Save As, Save a Copy, Save as Template and the first Save of a new document is asked of the desktop portal, starting on the suggested file's type, and the file type picked in it decides the format. A name typed without an extension, or with the suggested file's in any letter case, gets the picked type's extension; a name typed with another save format's extension (for Save as Template, a template format's) is saved in that format, another format's extension is replaced with the picked type's, and any other extension gets the picked type's added. rfd shows the dialog when the portal can't (#2679, `apps/vectorcraft/src/portal_save.rs`).
  - Save as Template writes a PDF-compatible `.ait` as well as a `.vctemplate`, which stays the default: the save panel and the web build's Save as Template dialog list both, and New from Template opens the `.ait` as an untitled document with its layers and art (`file.saveAsTemplate {format: "ait"}`, or a path ending in `.ait`).
    Save as Template always writes a file named with its template type's extension: `file.saveAsTemplate` saves a path ending in another format's extension (`card.png`) as `card.vctemplate` (or `card.ait`), the desktop save panel does the same with a Save As format's extension typed in it (`card.pdf` is saved as `card.vctemplate`), and `file.saveAs` and `document.save` refuse `ait` with an error that names `file.saveAsTemplate`. A `.ait` is PDF-compatible only: `aiVersion: "7"` is an error for it, and the web build's dialog shows no Version row for it.
    Exports refuse a `.ait` with an error that names `file.saveAsTemplate`, and `vectorcraft-cli convert in.pdf out.ait` and `run --export out.ait` write the template as `file.saveAsTemplate` does.
  - SVG/SVGZ in and out with SVG Options, Preserve Editing, symbols, filters, rich text and physical units (SVG type under a transform or `viewBox` scale opens at the size it draws at, the scale moved into its size, leading, baseline shift and strokes, a stretch, skew or rotation kept as its transform: #396; a top-level group with a clip path, such as a clipped Inkscape layer, opens as a layer with a clipping mask, its name kept: #420; hidden objects written hidden on Save and `convert`, and `data-*` attributes kept as the objects' own data: #522; top-level groups open as layers named from `data-name`, else the id, also when one more group (a transform on all the art, a `<switch>`) wraps them, hidden ones hidden, and a file whose art sits loose under a root `<svg>` with an id (or `data-name`), as one-layer exports write it, opens with its one layer named from it; nested groups stay groups, except the sublayers VectorCraft writes, marked `data-vc-layer`, and Inkscape sublayers, which open as sublayers in their layer's colour: #372); PDF and PDF-compatible `.ai` in and out (layers, with hidden ones kept hidden with their art and nested ones as sublayers, on pages of up to 64 million operators, art whose layer can't be told going to a hidden, non-printing layer rather than showing or printing: #419; strokes kept live, a fill and a stroke of one outline as one object; a type object's stroke written as each glyph's outline stroked back on the type, so it stays one editable object; lines wrapped in a frame (each wrapped line ending in a space, one left edge, leading and font) back as one area type object, left aligned or justified with its paragraph spacing, where laying it out breaks the lines where the file does; glyphs set apart by gaps wider than a space (a barcode's digit groups) keeping their places; layers stacked as the pages mark them even when one first paints on a later page, art ending a layer's marked content or a clip closing in a later layer kept in its own layer, and layers with no art kept empty: #508; art reaching past a plain PDF's page clipped to its crop box, as PDF viewers show it, each such object in a clip group of its own (a PDF-compatible `.ai` opens whole: #675); a `.ai` on its trim boxes with the bleed boxes round them as the document's bleed, as Crop To › Trim opens a PDF (#1266); masks, editable text with type set along a curve coming back as type on a path, each artboard's art on its own page only, an `.ai`'s white page under its layers left out rather than coming in as art, spot colours, presets, security, marks and bleed, ICC output intents, raster effects, subset fonts, PDF/X, PDF layers, overprint, page thumbnails, fast web view, PDF 1.3). CMYK images keep their ink amounts from PDF import (and from placed CMYK TIFFs) to PDF export: a CMYK JPEG passes through unchanged, others stay CMYK (DeviceCMYK, or ICC-based CMYK in PDF/X-3/X-4) unless the Output settings convert them; the canvas shows them through the working CMYK profile (#320). Overprint is kept from PDF import (opened, the PDF part of an `.ai`, placed) to PDF export: the graphics state's `/OP` and `/op` become the overprint of fills, strokes and type, so a spot colour over a process colour still overprints; a page whose overprint can't be read for certain knocks out with a note, as does `/OPM 0` being read as nonzero overprint (#1388; hand-written fixtures, `pdf/src/tests_import_overprint.rs`). A masked CMYK image (`/SMask`, `/Mask` or a colour key) keeps its inks too, its alpha coming in as a greyscale opacity mask.

    In imported PDF type, a space glyph the file draws between two words also keeps the next word where the file has it when the gap beside the space is wide, as VectorCraft's own export draws a tracked space: the space gets tracking of its own, and the wrapped lines of a justified paragraph still come back as one area type object when the word gaps on each line are alike (part of #2384).
    Letter-spaced PDF type, whether set with character spacing (`Tc`) or glyph by glyph, keeps its word spaces and gains none between its letters: the spacing a line's letters share is taken off each gap before a gap reads as a space. That holds on a line that also shows where its words break, with spaces the file draws or gaps wider than the rest; evenly spaced glyphs alone, which could be words of one letter, keep every gap as a space, as do glyphs set more than half an em apart, such as figures in columns.
    A function-based PDF shading (type 1) whose colour changes along one axis only, as a browser writes a repeating linear gradient, comes in as a linear gradient over its domain, each hard colour change two stops at one offset; one whose colour changes in two directions comes in as its average colour, with a warning. Either paints only over the shading's domain. Both came in as a flat grey that wasn't in the file (#3621). Each such shading is read once per import, and all of them within one budget of 200,000 function evaluations, so a file filling thousands of paths with long functions still opens in about a second (it took minutes); past the budget they come in as their average colour, then grey, with a warning.
    A gap between glyphs of two sizes is measured against the smaller one, so a word set beside a much larger one with no space glyph between them (a browser's margin between two sizes, as in `≤ 4` and a small `hours`) keeps its word space (#3623).
    SVG import's style cascade, used for hidden objects, non-scaling strokes and type, tests each element only against the `<style>` rules for its id, its classes and its element name, and the rules whose selector ends in none of these (`*`, `[x]`).
    A `.svgz` file copied in a file manager pastes as its art, as a copied `.svg` file does.
    SVG import keeps attributes in other applications' XML namespaces (`plotter:pen="2"`) on the objects and layers they belong to, as it keeps their `data-*` attributes: copies, duplicates and `.vectorcraft` files keep them, and SVG export writes them back with each namespace declared once on the root (the rest of #522; `crates/svg/tests/it/foreign_attributes.rs`, `tests_attributes.rs`).
    In a `.ai` or EPS opened from its editing data, type has its text object's opacity and blend mode, whether it is made from the file's text document or taken from the page. Where such type has transparency and comes in with other art (the rest of its look, or page type and strokes that go with it), a group of them has it. Where the page draws its type, or the strokes around it, with transparency that is neither its text object's nor its text object's combined with that of the objects around it, the page's type and strokes keep their own instead (`crates/eps/src/import/tests_native.rs`). Where the page draws type of no text object over text objects made from the text document, that type is left out only when, for each piece of it, one of those text objects has the piece's Latin letters and digits in its text, in capitals or not; other such type is kept as the page's other type of no text object is.
    In SVG export without Fewer `<tspan>` Elements, each character of live type that justification or Mojikumi moves (the letter gaps of a Justify All line without word spaces, the gaps between the characters of a justified Japanese line, closed-up punctuation, the space between Japanese and Latin letters) starts its own positioned `<tspan>`, and type scaled horizontally on a justified line is stretched to its own width (`crates/svg/tests/it/text_layout.rs`).
    SVG export (live text), legacy `.ai` saves (text objects), DXF export (`TEXT` entities) and the CSS Properties panel write area type that Shrink Text to Fit scales down at the size it draws at, and scale its tracking, kerning, leading and baseline shifts the same way where the format holds them.
    A PDF saved with Illustrator's editing data opens through it as a PDF-compatible `.ai` does, with its layers and groups and with art reaching past its page unclipped; such a PDF holds the data in `AIPDFPrivateData` streams (part of #868). A shape a PDF or `.ai` paints with a gradient (a clip path round a shading) opens as one path filled with the gradient, not a clip group round a rectangle, so Shape Builder, Live Paint and Pathfinder work on its outline (#1304).
    In a `.ai` opened from its editing data, a text object on a layer that shows and doesn't print stays on that layer, made from the file's text document, even where the page doesn't draw it (`crates/eps/src/import/tests_native.rs`). Such a `.ai` opens without the PDF part's warnings that text was kept as outlines when no outlined glyphs come in, and a warning counts the text objects that hold the page's type next to glyphs the page has only as outlines, which don't come in (`crates/engine/src/cmd/fileio/tests_aiimport.rs`). Where the art of a `.ai` or EPS opened from its editing data differs a little from the file's page, the warning gives the share of the page that differs away from type. When that share is 0.2% or less, the warning names the type and gives the share of the page that differs where the type is (`crates/eps/src/import/tests_native.rs`).
    PDF text opens with every glyph where the file draws it (#722): the font's kerning or none, whichever the file followed, word and character spacing, `TJ` adjustments and horizontal scaling kept per character as tracking, text rise as baseline shift within its line, vertical glyphs narrower than an em centred on their column (`/W2`, `/W`, `/DW`), justified text boxes with word spacing back as justified area type (`tests_text_placement`, fixtures written from ISO 32000-1 §9).
    A `.ai` or PDF whose editing data holds a variable library opens with a warning that its variables and data sets weren't read, with how many of each it has, whether its layers are read or it comes in as its PDF part (`crates/engine/src/cmd/fileio/tests_aiimport.rs`).
    A PDF page whose `UserUnit` (PDF 1.6) is above 1 opens at its size in points, its numbers times the `UserUnit` (one above 75,000 counts as 75,000), and `document.pdfInfo` gives its size and boxes in points too. A `.ai` whose editing data has its artboards in the units of such a page opens from that data at the page's size, with its layers, and when the layers can't be read its pages still take the artboard layout of the data, scaled the same way (part of #1482).
    When the editing data of a `.ai` or EPS is for a page of another size than the file's, the warning that its layers weren't read gives both sizes in points, and the scale of the editing data's page to the file's page (1:10 for a tenth of its size) when their sides are in proportion (#2034; `crates/eps/src/import/tests_native.rs`).
    A `.ai`, or a PDF saved with Illustrator's editing data, whose editing data can't be decompressed opens from its PDF part with a warning that its layers weren't read and why, and an export or Save As to its own path asks first (`acknowledgeLoss`), as for a file whose layers the reader can't read (`crates/eps/src/import/tests_native.rs`, `crates/engine/src/cmd/fileio/tests_aiimport.rs`).
    PDF export and `.ai` saves write a page with a side longer than 14,400 pt with a `UserUnit` (PDF 1.6), its longer side divided by 14,400 and rounded up to the next thousandth, so that no side is longer than 14,400 units (ISO 32000-1, Annex C.2); in PDF 1.3 to 1.5 files and PDF/X files such a page is written in points.
    Placed (linked) files in a `.ai`'s editing data come in as linked images in their place, each showing the low-resolution preview the file keeps of it until its file is found or relinked in the Links panel (a file found next to the document or at its path is read as the document opens). A file with them no longer falls back to its PDF part, so its guides, sublayers and hidden objects open (#1264; `crates/eps/src/import/ai/tests.rs`, `crates/engine/src/tests_links.rs`). In a file opened that way, a gradient with stops in the middle runs its whole ramp across its shape and a gradient object no longer passes its fill to the next path (#1390); text objects with an appearance keep their own text and frame, type of hidden layers stays hidden, and type on later artboards lands on its text objects (#1391); area type whose frame is too short for a line of the fallback font shows its first line, the frame made taller with a warning in the open result (#1392).
    A `.ai` saved without PDF compatibility (its PDF part only a placeholder page) is placed and pasted from its editing data, as it opens: File › Place places the art of the layers that show on the first artboard (`file.place`'s `page` places another one), and Paste of it as PDF data (`clipboard.importPdf`) takes every object. `document.open` with `pages` naming every page of such a file opens it the same way (`crates/engine/src/cmd/fileio/tests_aiimport.rs`).
  - EPS and DXF in and out, EMF/WMF in and out; PNG (with PNG-8), JPEG, WebP, GIF, TIFF, BMP, Targa and layered PSD export; grayscale TIFFs with an alpha channel or other extra channels place, relink and open, the alpha as the image's transparency (#1466 in part; CCITT Group 3 and planar files with extra channels are not read); PSD and PSB files open and place, linked or embedded, as their merged image in every colour mode and depth (#918). EPS import runs a PostScript Level 3 interpreter written from the PostScript Language Reference: resource categories and `resourceforall`, local and global VM (`currentglobal`/`setglobal`/`gcheck`), `clipsave`/`cliprestore`, subarrays and substrings that share storage, the standard dictionaries in `systemdict`, `dictstack`, `internaldict`, executable filters and strings, `load` by any key, `//name` immediate names, `token`, `execform`, user paths, `cshow`, `rootfont`, `cachestatus`, colour rendering and halftone queries, file `status` and data read with `flushfile`, and `pdfmark` marks dropped (Discord feedback, #466, #469, #474). Masked images (`ImageType 3` in its three interleavings) and reusable streams are read, and an image's several data sources are read in turn, as the reference defines (procedures that read one file get their own rows: such images came in banded, #498). `restore` puts dictionaries back as they were at the `save`, so programs that count their saves in a dictionary read to their end (part of #505). Tiling patterns come in as pattern swatches, uncoloured ones too; Type 3 fonts' glyphs as their outlines, spaced by `ashow`/`widthshow`/`xshow`/`kshow`; mesh and function-based shadings (types 1, 4–7) as gradient meshes; sampled functions (type 0) and Flate/LZW predictors are read. It is tested with programs written from the specification in the ways common generators use these features; Inkscape/cairo EPS files open as vectors. When a file's PostScript still can't be read, it opens as its TIFF preview, its Windows metafile preview (as vectors) or its EPSI preview, and the warning (in the status bar, `document.open`/`app.open`/MCP `open_file` replies and `vectorcraft-cli info`) names the error, the operator that raised it and the procedures it ran in. Legacy PostScript `.ai` files (Illustrator 3–8, written with the prolog that defines their operators) keep their groups and nested groups (`u` … `U`), between and inside clipping groups; EPS and EMF/WMF import nest clips (and groups) at most 128 deep, so a hostile file can't exhaust the stack. DXF TEXT justified Fit or Aligned spans its two points (stretched, or scaled as a whole). PDF export writes type as real, searchable text in embedded subset fonts by default, as Illustrator's PDF presets do (Convert Text to Outlines is an option; printer's marks stay shapes), so text-heavy PDFs stay small (#733). DXF export writes each fill as its outlines followed by its hatch, so laser and cutter software, which skips hatches, gets filled art and type too (#546).
  - The Open and Place dialogs list PostScript `.ps` files and `.epsf` files. A `.ps` file opens and places through the EPS reader (its first page), also when its header is only `%!`, as the `ps` format, which exports don't write (Print to PostScript does); an `.epsf` file opens and places as EPS. Copied in a file manager, these files paste as EPS, and `clipboard.importEps` also reads PostScript whose header is only `%!` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/fileio/tests_epsimport.rs`).
    `document.pdfInfo` reads an EPS, a `.ps` file or a `.ai` in PostScript form as one page the size of its bounding box (a US Letter page without one), and its `thumbnail: 1` is a PNG of what that page prints (`crates/engine/src/cmd/fileio/tests_pdfimport.rs`).
  - EPS export with Use Artboards writes a central EPS file of the whole document, bounded by its visible art, beside the file of each artboard when it writes two or more artboards (`crates/engine/src/cmd/fileio/tests_eps.rs`).
  - Targa files (`.tga`, `.vda`, `.icb`, `.vst`) open, place linked or embedded, relink and update at their pixel size: color-mapped, true-color and black-and-white, raw or run-length encoded, in any of the four row orders. The image descriptor's attribute bits and the extension area's Attributes Type decide the transparency: a file with no attribute bits, or with attribute data the Attributes Type calls undefined, opens opaque; with one bit, a 16-bit true-color pixel takes that bit as its alpha, and a color-mapped pixel takes the bit of the 16-bit color map entry it indexes; premultiplied colors are divided by their alpha. Open and Place recognize a Targa file by its extension, and `clipboard.importImage` and Glass's Load Texture… by its header; a Targa file copied in a file manager pastes as a bitmap (`crates/engine/src/cmd/fileio/tests_tiffbmp.rs`, `crates/engine/src/tests_links.rs`).
  - EPS and DXF in and out, EMF/WMF in and out; PNG (with PNG-8), JPEG, WebP, GIF, TIFF, BMP, Targa and layered PSD export; grayscale TIFFs with an alpha channel or other extra channels place, relink and open, the alpha as the image's transparency (#1466 in part); PSD and PSB files open and place, linked or embedded, as their merged image in every colour mode and depth (#918). EPS import runs a PostScript Level 3 interpreter written from the PostScript Language Reference: resource categories and `resourceforall`, local and global VM (`currentglobal`/`setglobal`/`gcheck`), `clipsave`/`cliprestore`, subarrays and substrings that share storage, the standard dictionaries in `systemdict`, `dictstack`, `internaldict`, executable filters and strings, `load` by any key, `//name` immediate names, `token`, `execform`, user paths, `cshow`, `rootfont`, `cachestatus`, colour rendering and halftone queries, file `status` and data read with `flushfile`, and `pdfmark` marks dropped (Discord feedback, #466, #469, #474). Masked images (`ImageType 3` in its three interleavings) and reusable streams are read, and an image's several data sources are read in turn, as the reference defines (procedures that read one file get their own rows: such images came in banded, #498). `restore` puts dictionaries back as they were at the `save`, so programs that count their saves in a dictionary read to their end (part of #505). Tiling patterns come in as pattern swatches, uncoloured ones too; Type 3 fonts' glyphs as their outlines, spaced by `ashow`/`widthshow`/`xshow`/`kshow`; mesh and function-based shadings (types 1, 4–7) as gradient meshes; sampled functions (type 0) and Flate/LZW predictors are read. It is tested with programs written from the specification in the ways common generators use these features; Inkscape/cairo EPS files open as vectors. When a file's PostScript still can't be read, it opens as its TIFF preview, its Windows metafile preview (as vectors) or its EPSI preview, and the warning (in the status bar, `document.open`/`app.open`/MCP `open_file` replies and `vectorcraft-cli info`) names the error, the operator that raised it and the procedures it ran in. Legacy PostScript `.ai` files (Illustrator 3–8, written with the prolog that defines their operators) keep their groups and nested groups (`u` … `U`), between and inside clipping groups; EPS and EMF/WMF import nest clips (and groups) at most 128 deep, so a hostile file can't exhaust the stack. DXF TEXT justified Fit or Aligned spans its two points (stretched, or scaled as a whole). PDF export writes type as real, searchable text in embedded subset fonts by default, as Illustrator's PDF presets do (Convert Text to Outlines is an option; printer's marks stay shapes), so text-heavy PDFs stay small (#733). DXF export writes each fill as its outlines followed by its hatch, so laser and cutter software, which skips hatches, gets filled art and type too (#546).
  - TIFFs that store each channel as its own plane (PlanarConfiguration 2) place, relink and open as the same image stored pixel by pixel does, 8 and 16 bits: grayscale with an alpha channel or other extra channels, and CMYK with or without them. A planar CMYK TIFF keeps its ink amounts and is stored as a CMYK TIFF with each pixel's inks together, at the file's resolution. A TIFF whose header claims more strips or tiles than can be counted is refused as too large to draw (#1466 in part; `crates/engine/src/cmd/fileio/tests.rs`).
  - 1-bit TIFFs compressed with CCITT Group 3 (ITU-T T.4) place, relink and open: Compression 2 (modified Huffman) and Compression 3 with one-dimensional rows or, with T4Options bit 0, two-dimensional ones, with or without fill bits, in strips or tiles, with either FillOrder and either polarity. Rows in T.4's uncompressed mode are not read. A file whose pixels would take more than the decoding allowance as RGBA is refused as too large to draw (#1466 in part; `crates/engine/src/cmd/fileio/tests.rs`).
  - EPS and PostScript import keeps a CMYK image's ink amounts, as PDF import does: the samples of `image` and `colorimage` in a CMYK color space, and of a CMYK JPEG read through `DCTDecode`, come in as a CMYK TIFF, read through the image's Decode array, and the pixels a `MaskColor` or `ImageType 3` mask hides become a grayscale opacity mask (`crates/eps/src/import/tests_images.rs`). Such images came in as RGB PNGs.
  - EPS and PostScript import reads image data through `CCITTFaxDecode`: Group 4 (ITU-T T.6) and Group 3 one-dimensional and mixed (ITU-T T.4) data, with the filter's `K`, `Columns`, `Rows`, `EndOfBlock`, `EndOfLine`, `EncodedByteAlign` and `BlackIs1` parameters, decodes to 1-bit rows for `image` and `imagemask`. Damaged data keeps the rows decoded before it (damage in the first row is a PostScript `ioerror`), and parameters out of range or past the 256 MiB limit on decoded data are refused (`crates/eps/src/import/tests_images.rs`). Reading such a file stopped at an error naming the filter, and the file opened from a fallback, such as its preview or the art drawn before the image, or did not open.
  - EPS and PostScript `.ai` import undoes the TIFF predictor (`/Predictor 2`) of `FlateDecode` and `LZWDecode` data at 1, 2, 4 and 16 bits a component as well as 8: each component adds the same component of the pixel to its left within its bit width, 16-bit components add as big-endian numbers, and each row starts again (ISO 32000-1 §7.4.4.4; `crates/eps/src/import/tests_images.rs`, `crates/engine/src/cmd/fileio/tests_epsimport.rs`). At those depths the image drew the stored differences instead of its samples.
  - DXF control-point SPLINE import honors its closed flag (#1299 follow-up after #1320 fixed export), including rational curves; open curves whose endpoints meet stay open. Own-fixture regressions cover controls/knots, fit-point fallback and all export versions (`crates/cad/src/import/tests.rs`, `crates/cad/src/tests.rs`); native save/read checked. Circular cubic paths export as native CIRCLE/ARC where stroke semantics permit; R12 weighted strokes remain POLYLINE, and a non-circular ellipse keeps the existing fallback (`crates/cad/src/tests.rs`); CNC preset and VCarve QA remain pending.
  - Affinity documents in (AF.1–AF.4): `.af` (Affinity 3) and `.afdesign`/`.afphoto`/`.afpub` (Affinity 1 and 2, container versions 8–12) open and place as editable art: layers and sublayers, groups (pass-through or isolated), artboards (with their names and backgrounds) and Publisher pages side by side, curves with live corners, parametric shapes (rectangles with corner radii, ellipses, polygons, stars, pies, triangles, trapezoids), compound shapes, solid/linear/elliptical gradient fills and strokes (weight, dashes, alignment, scale-with-object), clipping by nesting, vector and pixel masks, artistic and frame text with fonts, sizes, tracking, leading and alignment, placed images (their original JPEG/PNG) and pixel layers (8/16-bit RGB, CMYK), opacity, visibility, locking and blend modes, at the document's resolution in points. Effects, adjustments, brushes and pressure profiles, transparency gradients, master pages, symbol instances (imported as their cached picture), special shapes (cloud, heart, cog…, imported as ellipses) and Affinity-only blend modes are named in the import warning. A file whose native data can't be read opens as its embedded preview with the reason, and that preview can't be placed. Save never writes back over the Affinity file and there is no Affinity export. AF.5 (from DesignCraft's import, storytold/designcraft#291) adds master pages (on a locked layer behind the pages that show them), tables (area type per cell and a line per edge), each paragraph's alignment, indents, spacing and leading, horizontal text scale, outlined text, frame text sized by its text scale, drop shadows and outer glows as live effects (inner shadows as inner glows), outline effects as strokes, colour and gradient overlays baked into the paint, embedded Affinity documents as editable content (their artboards don't become artboards), pixel layers over 64 MP at a reduced resolution and HEIC photos from their stored pixels; automatic leading (size plus the font's line gap) fitted on thumbnails; underlines and strikethrough; strokes whose style is None (every shape stores one) left out, which also brings 6 public files closer to their thumbnails; line breaks inside a paragraph; table cell text centred as Affinity centres it, also where it is taller than its cell; CMYK pixel layers converted through the document's embedded CMYK profile (relative colorimetric with black-point compensation, as each layer's colour settings name), or kept as CMYK images when there is none; outline effects on stroked shapes around their stroke; artistic text whose paragraphs align differently aligned within its longest line, a frame's first baseline at cap height, and frames whose last lines' descenders hang out made tall enough to show them (all measured on a local document's own PDF export: baselines match to 0.1 pt); a local 56-artboard document's mean thumbnail difference went from 16.2 to 11.4, and its pages' mean difference from the owner's PDF export from 12.9 to 9.3. AF.4 adds Affinity 3 artboard recognition and actual-outline clipping, source-backed JPEG/PNG raster tiles, Unicode text-run recovery, stored fallback/exact installed fonts, OpenType feature flags and compound-geometry limits. 51 public CC0/MIT/Apache-2.0 files (33 current `.af`), pinned and sha256-verified (`cargo xtask corpus --affinity`), test native retention and every-board native/SVG/PDF/PSD output for current files; selected files compare their saved thumbnails. No Affinity reopen or independent paired PSD oracle was available; [source audit and complex-font gaps](affinity-validation.md); [scope, provenance and limits](../crates/affinity/README.md).
  - Placed documents: File › Place of a `.vectorcraft` file links to it by default (`file.place`'s `link`): one locked object showing an artboard of the document (or its art's bounds), read the way placing it without Link reads it, its symbols, patterns and images kept apart from the document's; without Link (or from bytes, not a file) it is an editable copy as before. It stays vectors in every output (SVG, PDF, EPS, EMF, DXF), and so do placed documents inside it, read from their own files up to 8 levels deep (documents that place each other stop there). On screen they draw from bitmaps cached per file and zoom step, shared by every copy and made in the background (a placeholder until ready), so a sheet of them redraws in about a millisecond; exports and prints draw them exactly. Like linked images, a save keeps only a preview of each (JPEG when opaque) unless Include Linked Files; output, and zooming past the preview, read the file again, falling back to the preview with a warning when it is gone or changed. Saves for older versions write them as plain art. Links check, update, relink, Update Links on open, Link Info (the artboard's size), Placement Options, Break Link (also Embed, Object › Expand: the editable copy placing without Link gives, its resources joining the document), Edit Original (the document in a new tab) and the Links panel cover them; saving a document updates the open documents that place it. The native format (v4) keeps data of 8 KB or more after the JSON instead of base64 in it.
  - Linked PDF and `.ai` pages: File › Place with Link (the default) places a page of a PDF, `.ai` or `.ait` file read as PDF pages as a placed document, as it links an image, the page and its box (`crop`) kept with the link: Links check, update and relink it, Break Link and Object › Expand give the group placing it without Link gives, every output draws the page's vectors, and Package copies the file. Without Link, or with a password or `textAs: "outlines"`, the page is embedded. EPS and PostScript `.ai` files are still embedded (`crates/engine/src/tests_placed_document.rs`).
  - File › Place with Bounding Box (`file.place {crop: "bounding"}`) measures the art that shows, with its strokes and effects, as an export does: hidden objects, guides and template layers do not count, a group whose only part on the page or artboard is hidden is not placed, and symbol instances are measured by their art, for `at`, `rect`, the place cursor and `file.place.info` (`crates/engine/src/tests_place.rs`).
  - Desktop print transport uses `craft-print` for CUPS and modern Windows. Sheet composition, copies, separations and colour management remain in VectorCraft; Windows 7 retains WMI and the installed PDF viewer. The Print dialog's Media list also carries the Japanese papers — JIS B4 257 × 364 mm, JIS B5 182 × 257 mm and JIS B6 128 × 182 mm beside the ISO B4/B5 (250 × 353 and 176 × 250 mm, kept so settings and presets saved before them keep their paper), and はがき 100 × 148 mm, 往復はがき 148 × 200 mm, 封筒 長形3号 120 × 235 mm, 長形4号 90 × 225 mm, 角形2号 240 × 332 mm, 角形3号 216 × 277 mm and 四六判 127 × 188 mm; the JSON id or the dialog label names a paper, any case and spacing (`B5 (JIS)` or `b5jis`) (`crates/pdf/src/print/settings.rs`, `crates/pdf/src/tests_print.rs`). The print-preview and physical-device fidelity gaps remain, so print scores and hours are unchanged.
  - A PDF, PDF-compatible `.ai` or `.ait` opened from its pages or its editing copy opens with the File Info that its XMP packet and its document information dictionary give: the author, description, keywords, copyright status, notice and URL, and the created and modified dates, the XMP packet's value where both give one; the title is not changed (`crates/pdf/src/tests_file_info.rs`, `crates/engine/src/tests_fileinfo.rs`).
  - PDF export and PDF-compatible `.ai` and `.ait` saves write the document's File Info created date as the file's creation date, or the time of writing when the document has none, and the time of writing as its modification date; the page information mark still prints the time of writing (`crates/engine/src/tests_fileinfo.rs`, `crates/pdf/src/tests.rs`, `crates/pdf/src/tests_marks.rs`).
  - PDF export and PDF-compatible `.ai` and `.ait` saves write File Info's copyright notice, URL and status to the XMP packet (`dc:rights`, `xmpRights:WebStatement`, `xmpRights:Marked`), so a PDF or `.ai` opened from its pages keeps them (`crates/pdf/src/tests_file_info.rs`, `crates/engine/src/tests_fileinfo.rs`).
  - Opening a PDF or PDF-compatible `.ai` whose XMP packet nests elements more than 256 deep no longer overflows the stack: File Info leaves the packet out and takes the document information dictionary's values (`crates/pdf/src/tests_file_info.rs`).
  - `file.print`, `print.preview` and `print.setup` take a print preset by name (`preset`: `[Default]` or a saved preset, in any case): its settings are used instead of the document's, with `settings` over them, `print.setup` saves them with the document, and an unknown name is refused with the list of presets.
  - Place and the Links panel, Package (placed `.vectorcraft` documents packaged with their own linked files and fonts, relinked to the copies: #777), File Info, Print with print presets, PostScript output and print tiling, slices and Save for Web, Export for Screens and Asset Export, CSS Properties, PNG/PDF/SVG/text clipboard flavours; files copied in a file manager paste as art (SVG, PDF, EMF/WMF, bitmaps) on every desktop platform, and Linux/Wayland reads the compositor's clipboard (#398); on Linux the Paste menu checks the clipboard off the UI thread, so an X11 owner that never answers can't freeze the window (#510); screenshots and other copied pictures paste as embedded images at the view centre everywhere, the web included (#457).
  - File › Place reads RTF files as area type with their formatting: each run's font, size, bold and italic, underline, strikethrough, caps, superscript or subscript, baseline shift and color, and each paragraph's alignment, indents, space before and after and direction. Table cells are separated by tabs; hidden text, pictures, headers, footers and notes are left out (`file.place`, `crates/engine/src/tests_textimport.rs`).
  - File › Place reads Word `.docx` documents as area type with the same formatting, taken from the document defaults, the paragraph and character styles (their toggle properties reversing each other) and direct formatting, the theme's fonts included. Table rows are paragraphs with their cells separated by tabs; hidden and deleted text, field instructions, pictures, headers, footers and notes are left out (`file.place`, `crates/engine/src/tests_textimport.rs`).
  - A Word paragraph justified with a low, medium or high kashida length places justified with Insert Kashidas set to Short, Medium or Long (`file.place`, `crates/engine/src/tests_textimport.rs`).
  - On the desktop, File › Place reads and decodes files off the UI thread, one at a time, and places each once it is read, with "Placing" in the status bar and the busy spinner until then: the Place dialog's OK, a file dropped on the canvas, a click or drag of the place cursor, and the OK of the PDF, DXF and text import options. The files and thumbnails the place cursor is loaded with are read the same way, and the Place dialog's lines about its files are read on a thread of their own. Files are placed in the order they were started; a file is not placed while a dialog is open or a drag is under way, and a file whose document was closed meanwhile is not placed. `file.place` and `file.place.queue` over MCP and scripts reply as before.
  - On the desktop, Copy and Cut make the system clipboard's formats (text, SVG, PDF, PNG) from a copy of the clipboard on the thread that writes background saves and exports, and write them when they are ready; while that thread has a save, an export, a print or a recovery copy to finish, they are made and written at once. Until they are written, Paste in VectorCraft takes the internal clipboard, and while a text field or the Type tool has the keyboard the app waits for them. Another Copy or Cut, or a copy of text in VectorCraft, drops them.
  - On the desktop with Enable Background Export on (Preferences › File Handling), File › Package… collects the linked files and fonts and writes the package from the document as it was at OK on the thread that writes background saves and exports, with "Packaging" in the status bar and the busy spinner until it is written; a save of unsaved changes that Package starts is written first. `file.package` over MCP and scripts replies as before.
  - On the desktop with Enable Background Export on, Export for Screens and the Asset Export panel's Export encode and write their files (into the folder, or one ZIP in it) from the document as it was at OK on the thread that writes background saves and exports, with "Exporting" in the status bar and the export progress dialog, which counts the files and whose Cancel stops before the next file. `document.exportForScreens` and `assets.export` over MCP and scripts reply as before.
  - Missing linked files can be looked for in a folder and its subfolders: Find in Folder… in the Linked File Not Found dialog and in the Links panel menu lists the files with each one's name, those with the size and contents saved with the link first, and relinks the files chosen, copying an image's file into the document's folder when asked, without replacing a file there (`links.findFiles`, `links.relink {copy}`). In the Links panel it looks for the selected linked files when any are selected.
  - On Windows, a document opened from a mapped network drive finds its links stored with the share's own path (`\\server\share\…`), as the same document opened from the share does; links on other computers stay missing.
  - On Windows, a link on a drive mapped to a network share other than the document's (`Y:\…`) is missing, with the reason that the path is on another computer, as a link stored with that share's own path is; links on this computer's drives and on the document's share are followed.
  - In the Links panel, Shift-click selects a range of links and Ctrl/Cmd-click adds or removes one.
  - Linked files another app changes while their document is open follow Preferences › File Handling › Update Links, as they do when it opens: Automatically reads them again (an Update Links undo step), Ask When Modified offers to, Manually leaves them modified in the Links panel. The desktop app compares the active document’s linked files by size and modification time every two seconds and when its window comes back to the front, on a worker thread; a file still being written is tried again (`links.updateChanged`).
  - Import and paste, 2026-10-13: a multi-artboard `.ai` with notes beside its artboards opens from its editing data, a page's art past its artboard no longer lying over the page before it (#1528); a `.ai` gradient whose stops are listed upwards keeps each midpoint on the stop that starts its part of the ramp (#1530); SVG text on a path follows basic shapes (circle, ellipse, rect, line, polyline, polygon) as their SVG 2 equivalent paths (#1531, fixes #1527); PDFs whose alpha soft masks are drawn as images import with the mask instead of empty art (#1551); EPS and PostScript type set in Type 42 (TrueType) fonts imports at its size instead of 1000 times too large (#1553); PDF and EPS import keep a clipping path whose bounding box covers the page but whose shape doesn't (#1544, fixes #1542). Opening or placing a file with an image too large to decode says so, and the Links panel shows it on the row (#1540, part of #1479). Paste takes a PDF or EPS another app copied as editable vector art: from the macOS pasteboard (with SVG), EPS on Windows beside PDF, and `.eps` files copied in a file manager, with the new command `clipboard.importEps` (#1538, fixes #1499).
  - A `.ai` or `.ait` file copied in a file manager pastes as its art: one that holds a PDF pastes the objects of its editing data, and one saved as PostScript pastes as a copied `.eps` file does.
  - A copied `.ai` or `.ait` file that holds a PDF pastes the objects of its editing data as File › Open reads them: every layer's objects go into the active layer in their stacking order, with their names, hidden objects and type objects, instead of the PDF page's art with its type as outlines. When the editing data can't be read, the file pastes its page as before (`clipboard.importPdf {editingData}`). The objects of a hidden layer come in hidden, from a pasted EPS too.
  - Import and export, later 2026-10-13 merges: SVGs that move objects with a CSS transform (`translate(100px, 0)`, `rotate(45deg)`) or style type with the `font` shorthand import as drawn (#1565); SVG symbols whose shapes use percentage lengths import at the size and place they are drawn, the percentages being of the symbol's `viewBox` (#1596); Inkscape's flowed text (`flowRoot`) opens as area type in its rectangle, a paragraph per `flowPara`, instead of being dropped, and a region that can't be read is left out with a warning (#1569, fixes #1568); the warning for an unsupported SVG filter names the filter, its primitives and the object, and says the object is drawn without it (#1599, fixes #1598); the pages of an Inkscape multi-page SVG become artboards, named by their labels (#1603, fixes #1601); SVG export with CSS classes or style entities stays fast in documents with many distinct styles (#1567); PDF and `.ai` import: evenly letter-spaced or tightened type on a path keeps its length along the path instead of closing up to the font's advances (#1586), and type on a path whose stroke is written glyph by glyph comes in as one text object with its stroke, not one object per glyph (#1585); the ICC profiles embedded in JPEG, TIFF and PSD exports have every tag on a 4-byte boundary (ICC.1 §7.1.2), so strict readers accept them (#1589, fixes #1584); GIF, PNG-8 and other indexed exports find each pixel's palette colour through an index instead of a scan, with identical output (#1576); a zero-length subpath draws its round cap as a dot and its projecting cap as a square, so dots in imported `.ai` and SVG files show (#1619, fixes #1613).
  - Files and untrusted input, 2026-10-14 merges: EPS import: a stitched shading keeps its hard colour changes (#1654, #1653). WMF/EMF import refuses an oversized embedded PNG or JPEG from its header, before any pixels are decoded (#1776). PDF open no longer takes exponential time on a crafted name tree with shared nodes when it looks for the editing data (#1781). The size limits on a native file's embedded data also apply to files read from memory, not only streamed ones (#1783). Saving over a private file on Unix no longer leaves a readable temporary copy beside it while the file is written (#1778). An Export for Screens suffix can no longer place files outside the export folder (#1777). Package refuses a folder where it would overwrite the open document or one of its linked files (#1786). ruzstd 0.9.1 fixes a decompression bomb (RUSTSEC-2026-0344) reachable from EPS/`.ai` and Affinity import (#1807). File Info dates are stamped only after a save succeeds, so a failed save no longer changes them (#1774). Linked files that change during a drag are updated after the drag instead of being missed (#1773).
- **Fields, search and window, 2026-10-14 merges:** Fields commit what was typed when you click away or move to another field, as Enter does; Escape still discards it (#1787). Up and Down move through the command search results and Enter runs the highlighted one (#1798, #1757). Slider rails show on Medium Dark (#1808, #1662). On Windows the custom title bar's window stays truly borderless, so the pointer lines up with what is drawn on systems where the hidden caption offset it (#1791, #1758; awaiting the reporter's confirmation).
- **Tools, panels and type, later 2026-10-14 merges:** the Transform panel's, Properties panel's and Control bar's X, Y, W and H show and edit the bounds of the anchor points selected with Direct Selection, and a whole-object selection is unchanged (#1839, fixes #1824). With Snap to Grid on, anchors and objects snap to the grid even when Snap to Pixel is also ticked: the grid wins (#1840; #1816 stays open until the reporter confirms). A marquee with the Selection or Direct Selection tool also selects the unlocked ruler guides it crosses (#1836). The toolbar shows no group labels by default (a preference brings them back) and runs on in one or two columns; the All Tools drawer lists the tools by flyout group with their shortcuts, has a menu (Reset, Basic, Advanced) and a Show section for the Fill/Stroke, Coloring, Draw Mode and Screen Mode controls (`toolbar.show`, #1751). An action clicked in the Actions panel stays selected, so Play Current Selection and Delete Selection act on it (#1853, part of #1629; editing actions and action shortcuts remain). Redo pressed during a drag keeps the drag as a step instead of losing the redone edit (#1856, #1719). Preferences are written as soon as OK is pressed, so they survive a session that doesn't end with a normal quit (#1857; #1747 stays open until the reporter confirms). New and Redefine Character Style take the format of the selected text range, also while typing (#1634). Type inside symbols, pattern tiles, graph designs and opacity masks gets its layout bounds back when a native file opens, so warped type in a symbol looks the same after save and reopen (#1833, #1738). Editing, renaming, deleting or merging a global swatch reaches the art of opacity masks, and a swatch used only in a mask is no longer listed as unused (#1830, #1735). On macOS, Save As, Save a Copy and the first Save show their sheet again; the Format menu on the sheet (#866) is withdrawn until the format can be set before the sheet opens, and #866 is open again (#1855; #1800, #1831 and #1518 stay open until confirmed on a Mac).
- **Files and untrusted input, later 2026-10-14 merges:** SVG import applies style sheet rules with `:not()` selectors, with their nesting bounded (#1799, #1557), no longer stalls on a style sheet with many stacked descendant selectors over deep nesting (#1834, #1703), and reads an SVG's linked files within the automation roots in force again (#1870). DXF export writes the VPORT record's view direction once (group code 36 was written twice, which strict readers reject, #1789). A deeply nested file no longer overflows the stack: nesting is capped at 32 objects (deeper groups are merged with a warning; SVG past 256 elements and PDF past 256 nested arrays are refused), symbols and patterns that use themselves open without the offending instance or paint, and a document nested more than about 40 deep can no longer be saved to a file that won't open again (#1852). PDF and `.ai` files nested deeply inside compressed streams, page trees holding themselves and functions or colour spaces built on themselves no longer crash the app (hayro 0.8; the import runs on a 16 MB thread, #1871); a decompression bomb or impossible predictor parameters are refused (#1873, #1700, #1701); a brush whose art draws the brush again through a symbol or pattern no longer crashes the app, and graph designs, Affinity, DXF, metafiles and plug-ins were probed with hostile input (#1872). Hostile EPS, Affinity and native files can no longer run memory or CPU away through ASCII85 data, PostScript objects holding themselves, flat-colour pixel layers or far and overlapping data offsets (#1863: #1715, #1714, #1704, #1699), and the save fallback for folders that refuse a rename keeps the old file's content until the new one is in (#1695). A file whose ids sit at their largest value no longer breaks new objects (#1718); a failed `command.batch` puts each document back whole, its file, history and a drag in progress included (#1697); a control request that timed out before the app took it never runs later, and the reply says which case it was (#1725, [control-protocol.md](control-protocol.md)); the Eyedropper and recolouring refuse an image too large as RGBA before decoding it (#1717) (all #1862). A save or export that fails is reported in a dialog that names the file and stays until closed, with the document left modified and the old file untouched (#1685); a browser download that can't start fails the save instead of marking it saved (#1693); a file that finishes opening waits while a dialog is open, so Save As options can't save the wrong document (#1694) (all #1865). krilla is built without its text shaping, so the unmaintained rustybuzz and ttf-parser don't ship (#1874, #1730); the CI gate compiles the web app for wasm, and the web's SVG nesting cap (34) follows from its 1 MiB stack (#1875).
- **Rendering, later 2026-10-14 merges:** copies, symbol instances and repeats that share an appearance keep their stroke outlines between frames (#1667). Wide drop shadows and glows at high zoom render within the raster budget (#1706); stacked Transform effects are bounded (#1705); 3D effects keep the area a nonzero compound path fills (#1724); pattern tiles redraw when a symbol, pattern or image their art shows changes (#1723); a template layer dims its images by its Dim Images percentage instead of fading the whole layer (#1683) (all #1864).
- **Tool cursors:** the Pen's pointer shows the new-path asterisk where a click starts a new path. While a
  path is being drawn it shows the pen without a badge, except over the first anchor (close), over the last
  anchor or with Alt held over a path (convert) and over another open path's end (join). The Eyedropper has an original pipette glyph with its tip at the hotspot;
  Use Precise Cursors restores the crosshair. The same glyph feeds OS bitmaps and painted
  cursors. DPI/hotspot and preference checks in `cursors.rs` and `tests_prefs.rs` cover #1269;
  actual OS display and Caps Lock remain unverified. Behaviour reference: [public tool-pointer documentation](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/tools.html#change_tool_pointers). Tool cursors are painted into the window on Wayland (#1652; not run on Linux, #1645 stays open until confirmed). A Precise Cursors command toggles the preference and can take a shortcut (#1663). On macOS the tool cursor is painted only while the window has the focus. Over a window behind another app, or under the File › Open… sheet, the system pointer shows alone instead of next to the painted cursor (#2020).
  In a rotated view the resize and rotate cursors turn with the view, to the nearest 45°.
- **Performance:** 20k shapes + 1k texts render in 27 ms per full-retina frame (7.8 ms zoomed), 7× faster than the first version. The UI thread never blocks. The web build is 7.1 MB gzipped. Print-size images (more than 512 MB decoded, up to 2 GB) draw in the canvas and in raster exports and can be trimmed with Crop Image; an image with a side past 65,535 px is shrunk to fit, a raster export says when an image could not be decoded, and Crop Image's trim leaves CMYK images alone (#1517). On Windows `vectorcraft-cli perf` reports the cores busy and, with `--deep`, its working set, and warns on a busy machine as it does on macOS and Linux (#1502).
  With `--deep`, each memory row of `vectorcraft-cli perf` also gives the peak so far: the peak working set on Windows and the peak resident memory (`VmHWM`) on Linux. A new last row gives the memory after the SVG export and the save → open → save at the end of the run.
  The renderer composes the two ink planes of a CMYK document that shows transparency into screen colors on up to as many threads as it rasterizes with, instead of on one. At 2880 × 1800 on 8 threads, a page of 300 shapes at 20% to 90% opacity takes 30 ms a frame instead of 55 ms, and 50,000 paths with one at 99% opacity take 258 ms instead of 361 ms (`vectorcraft-cli bench`), with the same pixels.
  With Overprint Preview or Separations Preview on, the renderer keeps the art it prepared for the preview from one frame to the next. It prepares again the objects that changed, and all of the art when Discard White Overprint changes or, with Separations Preview, when the plates shown, the proof setup, the swatches, the Spot Colors option or the color settings change or a profile is loaded. It draws the other objects from the art, geometry and stroke outlines it kept for them.
  The Pathfinder panel, Offset Path, Clean Up, Divide Objects Below, Make and Release Blend, Envelope Distort's Make and Release, Repeat (Radial, Grid, Mirror and Release), Vector Halftone, New and Redefine Symbol, Delete Symbol, erasing with the Symbol Sprayer, Rasterize, Convert to Artboards, Flatten Transparency, Clear Guides, Shape Builder, Live Paint, Release Image Trace, Make and Release Opacity Mask, Delete with direct-selected anchor points, Remove Anchor Points, Cut Path, and the Shaper, Knife, Eraser, Path Eraser, Line Cut, Rectangle Cut, Mirror & Cut and Blob Brush tools add and remove objects in one pass over each layer or group they change, and Outline Stroke and Expand write each new object in the place of the object it replaces (#1429).
  With more than 10,000 type on a path objects selected, the Selection and Direct Selection tools neither draw nor hit-test the objects' brackets.
  Type › Show Hidden Characters keeps the marks it places on each text object from one frame to the next. The canvas lays a text object out again when an edit changes it or its threaded story, or when the last frame that showed the marks did not draw it, and it lays out all type in view again when the fonts or the hyphenation exceptions change. With 1,000 two-line labels in view, drawing the marks takes 0.8 ms per frame in a release build instead of 19.7 ms.
  A selection with more than 100,000 points to outline shows its bounds instead of each object's outline and anchors. Paths count their anchors. Area type and type on a path count the anchors of their frame or path, and point type counts six: its box's corners and the ends of its baseline marker. Images, symbol instances, placed documents, and area type or type on a path in perspective count the four corners of their box, and gradient meshes and envelopes count their points and the ends of their mesh lines. The hover highlight leaves out an object past that count, and such an object shows its bounds as the key object. With 32,768 type objects, images, symbol instances, gradient meshes or envelopes selected, the selection's outlines and anchors add fewer than 100 vertices to the canvas's mesh (#2460).
  Delete, Cut, Group, Ungroup, Make and Release Compound Path, Make Clipping Mask, Send to Current Layer, Duplicate, Copy in the Move, Rotate, Scale, Reflect and Shear dialogs, Transform Each with Copy and each move of an Alt-drag take time in proportion to the size of the document (#1429).
  In the web build the status bar's render and UI times are measured with the browser's `performance.now()`, and the Layers panel stops rendering row thumbnails in a frame once they have taken 8 ms.
  In the web build, while a pan, zoom or rotation changes the view of a document whose last canvas render took more than 8 ms, the canvas draws the last frame moved with the view, and it renders the art again once the view has been still for 0.2 s.
  An Alt-drag with the Selection, Direct Selection, Group Selection, Rotate, Scale, Reflect or Shear tool copies the selection on its first move, and the moves after it transform those copies; the previews of the Move, Rotate, Scale, Reflect and Shear dialogs with Copy and Preview on copy the selection once in the same way (#1429).
  An Alt-drag of objects in perspective with the Perspective Selection tool, and an Alt-drag of a plane widget with that tool or the Perspective Grid tool, copy the objects on the first move, and the moves after it move those copies (#1429).
  When the desktop app opens a document on a thread of its own (#1245), that thread also reads the document's linked files and lays out its type, and the UI thread only adds the finished document: in release builds, the step left on the UI thread takes 0.02 ms instead of 1.04 s for a document with 12 linked 3000 × 2000 TIFFs, and it takes 0.1 ms instead of 0.85 s for one with 300 Auto Size area type objects, every second one in three columns.
  The Layers panel's Delete Selection, Duplicate Selection, Collect in New Layer, Merge Selected, Flatten Artwork, Release to Layers (Sequence) and row drags also take time in proportion to the size of the document, and so do Cut Artboard and Duplicate Artboard with their art and each move of an Alt-drag of one artboard with the Artboard tool while Move/Copy Artwork with Artboard is on (#1429).
  In Outline view the renderer draws paths and compound paths from the geometry it keeps for them between frames, and it culls the members of clip groups by the bounds it keeps for them. Layers with Preview off and the outlines of Image Trace objects are drawn the same way.
- **Graphics processor:** the canvas is rasterized on the CPU and the GPU only composites it, so any GPU that can show the window will do. Preferences › Performance › Graphics Processor (`gpuPreference`) is Automatic by default: the power-saving GPU on Windows and macOS (the integrated one on hybrid-graphics laptops, where presenting from the discrete GPU made the window flicker, #306), and the GPU the desktop runs on under Linux, where KWin on an NVIDIA GPU refused frames from a Ryzen's integrated GPU and 0.5.0 crashed at startup (#502). Power Saving and High Performance pick a kind of GPU; `WGPU_POWER_PREF`, `WGPU_ADAPTER_NAME` and `WGPU_BACKEND` override them. The app picks among the adapters that can present to the window (native backends before OpenGL, hardware before software, and on Windows a GPU's DX12 adapter before its Vulkan one: Intel's Vulkan driver made the whole window flicker black, #545), and if the window fails on one while starting up it starts again without it instead of crashing; after a start that a graphics driver crashed before its first frame, the next starts leave that adapter out, or list OpenGL's adapters alone when the crash came while the adapters were being listed (#2243; verified by unit tests, not on the reporter's Intel UHD Graphics 605); Help › About, `ui.inspect` and the log name the adapter in use. When the browser drops the page's WebGPU device or WebGL context, the web build writes recovery copies, starts again on new graphics with the same app and uploads its textures again; if it can't, it removes the stale canvas and says to reload, which offers the copies back. The desktop app writes the copies and says to restart (#369). On Windows and Linux the tools' cursors are OS cursors (bitmaps rasterized once per display scale), which the system moves itself: painted into the window, they trailed the pointer by the frames waiting to be shown, and the window now queues one frame instead of two (#444). macOS and the web still paint them (macOS sizes cursor bitmaps in points, eframe has no bitmap cursors on the web). Tool states have cursors of their own as the public manual describes them: Direct Selection shows a hollow or filled square on its white arrow over an anchor (path unselected or selected) and the Reshape Segment cursor over a curved segment, as do the Anchor Point tool and the Pen with Alt (whose caret it lends); Group Selection, and Direct Selection with Alt, show a plus; a drag shows the filled arrow, hollow while it snaps to a point or a guide, and an Alt-drag copy a double arrowhead; Curvature has its own pen and Free Transform's Cmd/Ctrl side-shear two arrows passing along the side. Lasso, Magic Wand, the freehand tools, Shaper, Live Paint Bucket, Measure, Print Tiling, the symbolism tools, vertical type, Scissors, Mesh and Puppet Warp return cursors of their own, which borrow the crosshair, the I-beam, the Pen's add cursor or not-allowed until they're drawn; there's no busy cursor yet. `crates/tools/src/cursors.toml` lists every cursor, when it shows and its hotspot, for whoever draws them. Pens and touch drive the tools as the mouse does, and a tap pressed and lifted within one frame clicks where it tapped (#491); pen pressure reaches the Paintbrush's pressure-sensitive brushes and the Liquify tools' Use Pressure Pen on Windows, on the web and on Linux under X11 and XWayland, while winit 0.30 reports none on macOS or native Wayland. On Linux, see `docs/development.md` for pens under Wayland.
- **Linux display server for pens (part of #2028):** Preferences › Performance › Linux Display Server has X11 (XWayland) When a Pen Is Attached (`x11WithPen`, off by default), which opens the window through XWayland on a Wayland session only when a pen is attached as the app starts. Under XWayland a drawing tablet's pen draws as a mouse. Below the choice, the Performance page tells users whose tablet pen doesn't draw to choose an X11 (XWayland) option.
- **Linux pen pressure (part of #764):** when the window is on X11, XWayland included, the desktop app reads a drawing tablet's pen pressure from XInput2 raw events on a second X connection, and the Paintbrush's pressure-sensitive brushes and the Liquify tools' Use Pressure Pen get it.
- **Linux pen eraser end (part of #764):** when the window is on X11, XWayland included, turning a drawing tablet's pen to its eraser end selects the Eraser tool, and turning it back to the tip selects the tool used before, unless another tool was chosen meanwhile. A turn during a press takes effect after the release, and a turn made while the pointer is over another window takes effect when it comes back over VectorCraft's window.
- **Pen barrel button on Windows:** with Windows Ink, a pen that touches down with its barrel button held acts as the right mouse button until it lifts, so a tap opens the canvas context menu; on Linux the barrel button is the right button (#3659). A touch with the tip alone is the left button, with pressure, as before.
- **Control transport:** idle sockets expire after 5 minutes, partial lines after an absolute 30 seconds from their first byte, and reply writes after 60 seconds (#1726). Real TCP regressions cover stalled peers and slot recovery; command execution has its separate existing timeout. MCP limits: 16 MiB lines, 64-message batches, 256-step `command_batch` with 8 MiB of kept results and 256 MiB control replies (#1764, fixes #1727). MCP requires the JSON-RPC 2.0 envelope and matches control replies by id, and an app refusal without an id reports the app's reason (#1768, fixes #1728). The MCP server reconnects to the app before a call when the connection was closed or holds stray bytes, after an app restart or an idle expiry (#1739).
- **MCP vertical type:** `add_text {vertical: true}` forwards to `text.create` or `text.createInPath`. Regression coverage checks point type, rectangular area type, type in a path and type on a path with true, false and omitted direction. This exposes an existing engine option; it does not change glyph orientation, CJK composition or the type/automation scores.
- **Malformed MCP replies:** invalid JSON from the app drops the connection, reports that the operation may have completed and leaves the next call to reconnect; it never replays the edit (#1761). TCP regressions cover malformed and uncorrelated replies, connection closure and a subsequent inspection. Envelope regressions also verify zero backend calls and unchanged initialization state for invalid versions.
- **Tests and robustness:** ~2,840 automated tests: model-based property tests, a junk-parameter sweep over every command, import fuzzing (SVG, PDF, libraries), golden renders, and MCP end-to-end tests over stdio. Shipped code never panics (workspace lints and a rollback safety net; see `docs/development.md`). Scatter graph data near the largest number is refused with a message instead of hanging the app (#1780). One very long Liquify stroke segment can no longer create an unbounded number of dabs (#1779). A drag whose last preview failed is no longer recorded as a committed command in the journal that actions and scripts read (#1775). Tests: text import fuzzing no longer searches installed fonts (#1785). Tests: render tests that add fonts no longer race the frame cache tests (#1795).
- **Raster-effect resolution in PDF:** when the 64 million pixel cap on an effect image renders an object's raster effects below the document's raster effects resolution, PDF export warns once per object with the requested and the lowest achieved ppi (`crates/engine/src/tests_pdfraster.rs`).
- **Rasterize effect:** Effect › Rasterize… (`rasterize`) draws an object as an image of square pixels at its own resolution or the document's raster effects resolution, with Object › Rasterize's color model, background, anti-aliasing, clipping mask and room around the object, while its paths stay editable. Expand Appearance and PDF and SVG export of an object whose only raster effect is Rasterize give the image Object › Rasterize gives (`crates/engine/src/tests_rastersettings.rs`, `crates/render/src/tests_rasterize.rs`). Behavior reference: [How to save artwork in Illustrator](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/saving-artwork.html), [Work with effects](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/effects.html).

- **Pattern tiles:** the renderer keeps a tile of each pattern for each scale it rasterizes the pattern at, until the tiles fill the tile cache's budget, and then drops the least recently used tiles first. Objects that show one pattern at different scales, such as a pattern scaled to 25% with Transform Pattern Tiles next to the same pattern at 100%, draw from tiles kept between frames.
