- **Pattern fills in Expand:** Object › Expand with Fill turns a pattern fill into the pattern's tiles in a clip group shaped like the object, with the fill's opacity and blend mode, and the object's other fills and strokes stay above or below it in paint order, in one undo step (`object.expand`).

- **Type with transparency or effects:** type at less than 100% opacity, in a blend mode other than Normal, or with raster effects such as a drop shadow keeps its glyph outlines between frames, as opaque type does, and is laid out again when it is edited or the fonts change. At 2880 × 1800 on 8 threads, a page of 1,000 type objects takes 13 ms a frame instead of 23 ms at 80% opacity, 31 ms instead of 41 ms in Multiply and 16 ms instead of 26 ms with a drop shadow, with the same pixels.

- **Brush art of copies:** symbol instances, inline graphics and repeat copies of a brushed path keep their own brush art between frames, as the same path on the page does. The renderer also keeps the stroke outlines of brush art and the evaluation of a live object in it, such as an envelope that a scatter brush places. The brush art is made again when the path, its stroke or the brush changes, and when the art of a symbol or pattern that the brush art can show changes. On one thread at 1000 × 1000 pixels (the median frame, with the median fastest frame in brackets), 2,000 paths on the page whose scatter brush art is an envelope take 94 ms (80 ms) a frame instead of 400 ms (306 ms), and 2,000 instances of a symbol whose art is a brushed path take 13.4 ms (12.0 ms) instead of 19.3 ms (15.6 ms), with the same pixels.

- **Live objects in symbols and masks:** symbol instances and inline graphics whose symbol is a blend, an envelope, a repeat, an Intertwine object or a gradient mesh, or a group that holds one, draw the evaluation the renderer keeps for that object between frames, as the same object on the page does. So do opacity masks whose art is such an object, and such objects in clip groups in Outline view. The object is evaluated again when the symbols, patterns, fonts or color settings it shows change. Symbol art with effects of its own, or that holds a symbol instance, an image, a placed file, type with an inline graphic or a raster effect, is still placed and evaluated again in every frame. At 1000 × 1000 pixels, a page of 2,000 instances of a symbol that holds an envelope takes 28 ms a frame instead of 126 ms, with the same pixels.

- **Live objects in documents with many symbols:** a live object, or an object with effects, that shows symbols or patterns is not walked again in a later frame to find them while the document's symbols and patterns stay the same. One that shows a placed file is walked in every frame. At 1000 × 1000 pixels, a page of 2,000 envelopes around instances of the last 2,000 of 10,000 symbols takes 30 ms a frame, and 83 ms when every frame walks them again, with the same pixels.

- **Type drawn as glyph outlines:** under a geometry effect, in EMF and WMF export, in DXF export when it is written as outlines, flattened with Convert All Text to Outlines, and inside an envelope, type keeps its underline and strikethrough, the weight and dashes of its character strokes when it is scaled, and the placement of its gradients and patterns, as the canvas draws it. A group's or layer's own fills and strokes also paint the underline and strikethrough of the type in it.

- **Texture redraws (#1257):** Craquelure, Mosaic Tiles and Stained Glass compare squared distances when finding their nearest cells; rounding/tie boundaries use the original distance ordering. Brute-force candidate tests and three 1800×1500 viewport comparisons preserve the old pixels. A CMYK rectangle move at 190.07%/DPI 1.5 is reproducible with `cargo test -p vectorcraft-render texture_drag_perf -- --ignored --nocapture`; idle-machine Windows interaction is still unverified.

- **Smart Blur modes:** Effect › Blur › Smart Blur… has a Mode menu with Normal, Edge Only and Overlay Edge (`blurMode`: `normal`, `edgeOnly` or `overlayEdge`; an effect saved without it draws as Normal). Edge Only draws the edges in white on black, and Overlay Edge draws them in white over the Normal blur. A pixel is on an edge when one of the pixels the search reads within Radius of it differs from it by more than Threshold in a channel and its channels, alpha included, add up to at least that pixel's. The search reads neighbors as the Normal blur does, kept within Radius, and always the four nearest pixels, so a color step gives a line about as wide as Radius, and at least one pixel wide, on the side with the larger sum (lines on both sides when the sums are equal). The white and the black keep each pixel's coverage. Behavior reference: [Summary of effects](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/summary-effects.html).

- **Dragging objects with raster effects when zoomed in (#2558):** during a drag with a tool on the canvas, the renderer draws filtered content (Gaussian Blur, Feather and the Photoshop-style filters) within 1,000,000 pixels, at a lower resolution where it would need more, unless it can draw the content from an earlier frame's raster. In the desktop app it does the same for drop shadows, outer glows and inner glows. No raster made that way is kept. The frame after the drag renders them as a still frame does, and a dialog's preview, exports and printing render as before. `zoomed_drag_perf` times a drag's frames at 100% to 6400%.
- **Dragging other art over a wide blur (#2558):** an effect raster too large to keep whole (a wide blur, a shadow or glow, or any blur zoomed in) is cropped to what can show in the view, or made at a lower resolution and resampled to the view's pixels, and kept while the view stays the same, so dragging other art over the object draws its effects from the still frame instead of re-rendering them at the drag's lower resolution. A drag stays on the render worker once the worker drew the frame shown, since only that renderer holds the rasters. `tests_viewraster` covers each effect, and `a_drag_over_a_wide_blur_draws_the_blur_from_the_still_frame` the canvas on and off the worker. Not yet: a worker frame shows one display frame after the overlays, and the first frame of an interaction can land on the renderer that has not made the rasters yet (follow-up: render every canvas frame on the worker, waiting briefly for fast ones).

- **Moving objects with raster effects (#1257):** during a drag or a dialog's preview, an object whose content only moved draws its cached drop shadows, outer glows and filtered content (Gaussian Blur, Feather and the Photoshop-style filters) from the rasters of an earlier frame at the nearest whole pixel, without running the effects again. The renderer first draws the moved content where the old content lies in its raster and compares the pixels. De-Interlace runs again. The frame after the drag runs the effects again and draws what a fresh renderer draws; on the desktop, the canvas renders that frame on the render worker. `texture_drag_perf` times a drag's frames and the frame after it.

- **Glass's Load Texture:** Effect › Distort › Glass… has a Load Texture… button that reads a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, TIFF, BMP, Targa, PSD or PSB file and adds Loaded Texture to the Texture menu (`textureImage`: `{path}` or `{name?, dataBase64}`, stored in the effect and saved with the document as a grayscale PNG in base64). The texture lies one image pixel per point at Scaling 100%, centered on the object and repeated; each pixel's luma is the surface's height, from 0 for black to 1 pt for white, and a transparent pixel counts as middle gray. Scaling and Invert act on it as on the built-in textures. A Glass saved without `textureImage` draws and saves as before.

- **Raster effects after document and view changes:** a cached drop shadow, outer glow or filtered content is made again when something its content reads from outside the object changes: a pattern's art or tiling, a symbol shown inside another symbol, a brush definition, an image's pixels, the raster resolution (De-Interlace), Page Knockout Group, Document Setup's substitution highlights, a layer's Dim Images, the color settings, the fonts, Pixel Preview, Anti-aliased Artwork, Overprint Preview and isolation mode. A thumbnail under Color Halftone or Mezzotint is made again when the document's color mode changes. Raster effects (blur, shadow, glow, grain) drawn after a pattern, radial or freeform gradient fill export at their place and size (#1541, fixes #1536).

- **Drop Shadow's Darkness:** Effect › Stylize › Drop Shadow… has Color and Darkness as radio buttons, each with its field, and the Appearance panel's inline editor has the two radio buttons in its Shade row (`shade`: `color` or `darkness`; `darkness`: 0 to 100%, 100 by default). Color is the default, and a shadow saved without these keys draws as before. With Darkness the shadow is the object's own colors with black added: in a CMYK document their cyan, magenta and yellow stay and their black K becomes K + darkness × (1 − K), and in an RGB document each channel is multiplied by 1 − darkness. Darkness 0% gives the object's color; 100% gives black in an RGB document and keeps the colors under 100% black in a CMYK one. SVG export writes the object blurred, moved and darkened with `feComponentTransfer` (screen colors, in a CMYK document too), and SVG import reads it back; CSS export leaves the shadow out and marks the object unsupported. When a `.ai`, EPS or PDF opens from its editing data, a Drop Shadow with Darkness in an object's art style is read as one with Color is, with the shadow's Darkness percentage (100% when the style gives none). Behavior reference: Illustrator CC Help (2014, [PDF](https://help.adobe.com/archive/en/illustrator/cc/2014/illustrator_reference.pdf)), page 428 (PDF page 434).

- **Live objects after document changes:** a blend, envelope or repeat, with or without an effect of its own, is evaluated again when one of these changes: the tiling of a pattern whose tiles an envelope bends (Distort Pattern Fills), a symbol shown inside a symbol, a pattern or an opacity mask, the fonts of its type, a placed document's file once the file is read, and the color settings. A gradient mesh, with or without an effect of its own, is colored again when the color settings change.

- **Blend, mesh and envelope points by number:** `object.blend.spine.moveAnchor`, `reshapeSegment` and `removeAnchor`, `object.mesh.setPointColor`, `movePoint` and `deletePoint`, and `object.envelope.setMeshPoint` refuse an `anchor`, `segment` or `index` that is not a whole number, and `object.envelope.setMeshPoint` refuses a negative `index`. Specified Steps (`object.blend.make`, `object.blend.options`) and the rows and columns of `object.mesh.create`, `object.envelope.makeWithMesh` and `resetWithMesh` must be whole numbers too.

- **Blend, mesh and envelope numbers given as text:** `object.blend.make` and `object.blend.options` (`steps`, `distance`, `value`), `object.envelope.makeWithWarp`, `resetWithWarp` and `options` (`bend`, `h`, `v`, `horizontalDistortion`, `verticalDistortion`), `object.envelope.makeWithMesh` and `resetWithMesh` (`rows`, `cols`, `columns`), `object.envelope.options` (`fidelity`), `object.mesh.create` (`rows`, `cols`, `columns`, `highlight`) and `object.mesh.setPointColor` (`opacity`) refuse a value other than a number or null, such as `"8"`, and change nothing. `object.mesh.create` refuses an `at` that is not `[x, y]`.

- **Blend and envelope options given as text:** `object.blend.make` and `object.blend.options` (`smooth`), `object.blend.spine.moveAnchor` (`independent`) and `reshapeSegment` (`perpendicular`), `object.envelope.makeWithWarp`, `resetWithWarp` and `options` (`horizontal`), `object.envelope.resetWithMesh` (`maintainShape`), `object.envelope.options` (`antiAlias`, `distortAppearance`, `distortLinearGradients`, `distortPatternFills`) and `object.envelope.editContents` (`editing`) refuse a value other than true, false or null, such as `"false"`, and leave the document and its undo history as they were.

- **Exporter plug-ins (G17):** a WebAssembly plug-in of kind `exporter` adds a write-only file format. File › Export › Export As lists it after the built-in formats, with Use Artboards greyed out (the plug-in writes the whole document) and its parameters in a generated dialog once the file is picked; `document.export` writes it by its format id, `plugin.<id>`, or by one of its extensions, and built-in formats keep theirs. The plug-in is given the native file's JSON (large images without their data) and `_context` (`mode`, `extension`, `name`), with 10 G instructions plus 4,000 per byte of input and 300 s, and Background Export's Cancel stops it between two slices of that budget. A decline or invalid output writes nothing; its warnings come back with the export's. Regressions: `crates/engine/tests/plugin_export.rs`, `crates/plugins/tests/abi.rs`, `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs/tests_plugin_export.rs`. Scores and hours unchanged.

- **Plug-in parameters as their manifest presents them (G17):** each parameter may have a `label`, a `unit` shown after its value, `help` on its label and a `helpUrl` page opened from a button, a `group` (sections that fold, after the parameters outside any group) and a `visibleWhen` that shows it only while the checkboxes and choices it names have one of the listed values (a hidden parameter still goes to the plug-in). `string` and `numberList` parameters join number, int, bool and choice, and a plug-in declares up to 256 parameters, at most 64 outside groups. The filter, live-effect and exporter dialogs use these keys, and the Appearance panel's effect editor the labels, units, help and conditions; hosts from before them ignore them. Regressions: `crates/plugins/src/dialog.rs`, `crates/plugins/src/manifest.rs`, `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs/tests_plugin_fields.rs`, `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/appearance.rs`. Scores and hours unchanged.
- **Live-effect plug-ins read their object's paints (G17):** a live effect is given the object's `fills` and `strokes` as a filter gets them, read only, and `_context.item` (`"object"`, or the fill or stroke whose own effects hold it); the result is cached by paint too, so a change of paint runs it again. Regressions: `crates/engine/src/tests_plugins.rs`, `crates/plugins/src/effect.rs`. Scores and hours unchanged.
- **Filter plug-ins set effects and stroke styles (G17):** a filter is given each object's effect records and its strokes' `join`, `cap` and `miterLimit`, and may return them; the records are admitted as `effect.apply` admits them (a known effect or installed live-effect plug-in, parameters it takes, one 3D effect that fits, no texture read from a file), and one refused refuses the output. Regressions: `crates/engine/src/tests_plugins.rs`, `crates/plugins/src/objects/tests.rs`. Scores and hours unchanged.
- **Plug-in data kept with the document (G17):** a filter writes JSON of at most 1 MiB with `documentData` (one undo step with its objects; `null` removes it) and reads it back in `_context.documentData`, which no other filter is given. It is the document's foreign data (`unknown.pluginData`, by plug-in id), as the perspective grid is, so the native file keeps it with no section of its own; an exporter is given the whole document, so it can read every plug-in's. Regressions: `crates/engine/src/tests_plugins.rs`, `crates/engine/tests/plugin_export.rs` (the exporter), `crates/doc/src/plugin_data.rs`, `crates/plugins/src/objects/tests.rs`. Scores and hours unchanged.
- **Heavy filter plug-ins (G17):** a filter's manifest may ask for `"budget": "heavy"`: 1 G instructions (20 times a light run's) and 300 s a run, for routing, packing or simulation. Install Plug-in… and File › Open ask the user first, `plugin.install` needs `allowHeavy: true` (`plugin.inspect` tells beforehand), the Additional Plug-ins Folder skips such filters, and the plug-in store keeps the answer. Its dialog has no Preview; the app runs it on a thread of its own with a progress window (Cancel, Continue in Background) and applies the result as `plugin.run` with the same parameters, one undo step, unless the document or the plug-in changed meanwhile. Regressions: `crates/plugins/tests/abi.rs`, `crates/plugins/src/manifest.rs`, `crates/engine/src/tests_plugins.rs`, `crates/ui-egui/src/tests_plugin_runs.rs`. Scores and hours unchanged.

- **Plug-in effects after a plug-in changes:** when a plug-in is installed for the first time, installed again or removed (`plugin.install`, `plugin.reload`, `plugin.remove`, File › Open of a `.wasm` file, the Additional Plug-ins Folder preference), the next frame the canvas draws uses the plug-ins then installed for objects with a plug-in effect and their raster effects, for the blends, envelopes and repeats that show such objects, and for pattern tiles and symbol instances whose art holds one.

- **Effect art after font and color settings changes:** when a font becomes available (fonts added, Refresh Font List, `text.rescanFonts`), the next frame the canvas draws outlines type in it where a geometry effect reshapes the type, a group that holds it or a symbol instance whose art holds it. When the color settings change (Edit › Color Settings, `edit.colorSettings`), the next frame shades objects with Revolve, Extrude & Bevel, Inflate or Rotate, and recolors objects and groups with a color adjustment, through the new settings.

- **Full font names (#1258):** OpenType name ID 4 identifies its face alongside family/legacy/PostScript names, including localized names, for loaded fonts, cataloged files and Missing Fonts searches. Synthetic name-table regressions cover full names distinct from their PostScript name, real-family precedence and variable fonts' default faces. Windows font-service activation remains unverified; scores and hours are unchanged.
### Corpus integrity evidence

`xtask/src/pngsuite.rs` verifies each file from the pinned PngSuite mirror against `xtask/pngsuite.sha256` before it reaches the corpus. Seven synthetic regressions cover substitution, oversize, cache repair, failure cleanup, nonregular targets, stale staging and manifest limits. The opt-in corpus remains gitignored; no PNGs are committed.

Evidence for the shared light Color: geometry tests in `tests_lighting`, effect paint tests, command/save/undo/expand and SVG/PDF checks in `three_d_light_color`, and headless picker/reset/preview tests in `tests_revolve`. Revolve keeps smooth colored vector ramps and continuous flat-lit caps. Inflate geometry tests check spherical lighting, shared vertex/edge continuity, concave cell coverage, puffed backs at perspective and legacy single-light/list equivalence; rendered command/export regressions cover smooth shading and editable expansion. Four legacy white-light PNGs match main byte for byte; [release measurements](3d-lighting-performance.md) record the colored solid-fill batch and the remaining source-gradient cost.

## Highlighted-text Eyedropper (2026-10-21)

Type/Eyedropper switches preserve highlighted characters; sampling changes only their enabled
font/paint attributes. Enabled non-neutral source or target object transparency is refused
atomically; disable Transparency to preserve object transparency while sampling the range.
`tests_eyedropper.rs` covers ranges, Unicode, history and transparency; tool tests cover brush-key
sampling coexistence. Scores and estimates unchanged. See [development.md](development.md#highlighted-text-eyedropper-2026-10-21).

## Drag artwork between document tabs (2026-10-22)

Selection drags activate another visible document tab after 400 ms, then copy editable artwork
on canvas release with the original grab point. Source and clipboard preservation, resource
rendering, swatch conflicts, cancellation, rotated/zoomed views and target Undo/Redo have regression
coverage (`tests_document_drag`, `tests_clipboard`). Overflow-menu and cross-window drag remain
separate. Scores and hours unchanged. [Behavior and command details](development.md#drag-artwork-between-document-tabs-2026-10-22).

## Gradient dither (2026-10-22)

Illustrator 30.0's gradient Dither ([public documentation](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/paint-and-fill/create-and-edit-gradients/control-dither-in-gradients.html)): the Gradient panel's Dither box sets
`dither` on the gradient (`paint.editGradient`, `paint.setFill`'s `gradient`, swatches, the native file; written only
when on, so older files open unchanged). A dithered linear or radial fill is drawn as pixels, a cell per device pixel,
each colour channel given seeded noise of up to a level before rounding: the same pixels on every render, banding
hidden, colours unchanged on average. SVG and PDF write it as an image at the Document Raster Effects resolution
(the documentation: the gradient converted to pixels with subtle noise, at that resolution); PDF with Preserve Editing
keeps the gradient editable. Strokes and freeform gradients ignore it (the documentation: fills only). Tests:
`render::tests_dither`, `engine::tests_gradient::dither_is_a_fill_gradient_option_that_saves_and_loads`,
`svg/tests/it/raster_paints.rs`, `pdf::tests::dithered_gradient_fills_export_as_images_and_strokes_as_shadings` and the
Gradient panel's `the_dither_box_dithers_the_gradient_fill_and_is_off_for_strokes`. Scores and hours unchanged.

## Gradient Method: Classic and Perceptual (2026-10-22)

Illustrator 30.0's gradient Method ([public documentation](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/paint-and-fill/create-and-edit-gradients/control-perceptual-interpolation-in-gradients.html)): the Gradient panel's Method menu sets
`method` on the gradient, Classic or Perceptual (`paint.editGradient`, `paint.setFill`'s `gradient`, swatches, the native
file; written only when Perceptual, so older files open as Classic). The documentation describes perceptual interpolation
as colour transitions matched to how the eye perceives differences between colours; VectorCraft mixes a Perceptual
gradient's colours in OKLab (lightness steps even, blue to yellow through a light blue-grey rather than mid grey), and
renderers that mix linearly draw it through stops placed on that curve, more where it bends, within half a colour level.
As documented, SVG and PDF exports rasterise it: fills and strokes are written as images at the Document Raster Effects
resolution, clipped to what they paint (a gradient along or across a stroke as slices through the curve's stops). Classic
gradients draw exactly as before. Freeform gradients mix their own way. With Dither, a Perceptual fill is the perceptual
mix with dither's noise, on the canvas and in the SVG and PDF images; a Perceptual stroke's image has no noise (dither
applies to fills). Tests: `color::gradient::tests` (perceptual midpoint, expansion, Classic unchanged, save format),
`engine::tests_gradient::method_is_a_gradient_option_that_saves_and_loads`, `render::tests_dither`,
`svg/tests/it/raster_paints.rs`, `pdf::tests::perceptual_gradients_export_as_images_and_classic_ones_as_shadings`,
`pdf::tests::dithered_perceptual_gradients_export_as_images_with_noise_on_the_fill` and the Gradient panel's
`the_method_menu_makes_the_gradient_perceptual`. Scores and hours unchanged.

aligning to a key anchor is still missing); Delete removes every selected anchor of a closed path (it used to remove the wrong ones), removes objects selected whole along with the selected anchors of others, and keeps the remainder selected so a second Delete removes it (#1674); In isolation mode Direct Selection and Group Selection pick only inside the isolated object (#1666); Escape cancels a Direct Selection drag (#1803, #1743); Escape while typing ends the edit, keeps the type selected and switches to the Selection tool (#1802, #1686, #1656); A filled Pencil path keeps a stroke of None (#1804, part of #1679); With the Pen, a press that moves under 3 screen pixels is a click (a corner without handles), and a Precise Cursors command toggles the existing preference and can take a shortcut (#1663); The [ and ] keys reach the Blob Brush, the Eraser and the Symbolism tools in the app (#1734, part of #1661); In the Pathfinder panel a group selected alone counts its nested shapes, so an expanded stroked object keeps the Shape Modes enabled (#1642, #1635); Object › Expand turns radial, grid and mirror repeats into groups of their instances (#1765, #1756); Select › Same matches type on its characters' fill and stroke (#1746, #1737); Fields commit what was typed when you click away or move to another field, as Enter does; Escape still discards it (#1787); Up and Down move through the command search results and Enter runs the highlighted one (#1798, #1757); Slider rails show on Medium Dark (#1808, #1662); On Windows the custom title bar's window stays truly borderless, so the pointer lines up with what is drawn on systems where the hidden caption offset it (#1791, #1758; awaiting the reporter's confirmation); Tool cursors are painted into the window on Wayland (#1652; not run on Linux, #1645 stays open until confirmed); Roughen with Smooth keeps turn-backs smooth instead of making cusps that draw as spikes (#1646, #1643); Scribble draws one zig-zag per region, with no lines across holes and notches; convex shapes are unchanged (#1651, #1648); correction to the 2026-10-13 rows: a guide's position in the Transform panel (#1659) is not established by the documentation found (help pages read again on 2026-10-14) and is kept as a convenience pending the owner's decision, with no parity claim; scores unchanged (estimated) |
| 2026-10-14 | minor | Files, untrusted input and automation: EPS import: a stitched shading keeps its hard colour changes (#1654, #1653); WMF/EMF import refuses an oversized embedded PNG or JPEG from its header, before any pixels are decoded (#1776); PDF open no longer takes exponential time on a crafted name tree with shared nodes when it looks for the editing data (#1781); The size limits on a native file's embedded data also apply to files read from memory, not only streamed ones (#1783); Saving over a private file on Unix no longer leaves a readable temporary copy beside it while the file is written (#1778); An Export for Screens suffix can no longer place files outside the export folder (#1777); Package refuses a folder where it would overwrite the open document or one of its linked files (#1786); ruzstd 0.9.1 fixes a decompression bomb (RUSTSEC-2026-0344) reachable from EPS/`.ai` and Affinity import (#1807); File Info dates are stamped only after a save succeeds, so a failed save no longer changes them (#1774); Linked files that change during a drag are updated after the drag instead of being missed (#1773); Scatter graph data near the largest number is refused with a message instead of hanging the app (#1780); One very long Liquify stroke segment can no longer create an unbounded number of dabs (#1779); A drag whose last preview failed is no longer recorded as a committed command in the journal that actions and scripts read (#1775); Tests: text import fuzzing no longer searches installed fonts (#1785); Tests: render tests that add fonts no longer race the frame cache tests (#1795); `text.create`, `text.createInPath` and the MCP `add_text` tool take `justify`, so point type can be centred on or end at its point (#1752, #1748); MCP limits: 16 MiB lines, 64-message batches, 256-step `command_batch` with 8 MiB of kept results and 256 MiB control replies (#1764, fixes #1727); MCP requires the JSON-RPC 2.0 envelope and matches control replies by id, and an app refusal without an id reports the app's reason (#1768, fixes #1728); The MCP server reconnects to the app before a call when the connection was closed or holds stray bytes, after an app restart or an idle expiry (#1739); #1684 and #1797 wrote their own evidence; scores unchanged |

| 2026-10-13 | minor | Files: SVGs that move objects with a CSS transform (`translate(100px, 0)`, `rotate(45deg)`) or style type with the `font` shorthand import as drawn (#1565); SVG symbols whose shapes use percentage lengths import at the size and place they are drawn, the percentages being of the symbol's `viewBox` (#1596); Inkscape's flowed text (`flowRoot`) opens as area type in its rectangle, a paragraph per `flowPara`, instead of being dropped, and a region that can't be read is left out with a warning (#1569, fixes #1568); The warning for an unsupported SVG filter names the filter, its primitives and the object, and says the object is drawn without it (#1599, fixes #1598); The pages of an Inkscape multi-page SVG become artboards, named by their labels (#1603, fixes #1601); SVG export with CSS classes or style entities stays fast in documents with many distinct styles (#1567); PDF and `.ai` import: evenly letter-spaced or tightened type on a path keeps its length along the path instead of closing up to the font's advances (#1586), and type on a path whose stroke is written glyph by glyph comes in as one text object with its stroke, not one object per glyph (#1585); The ICC profiles embedded in JPEG, TIFF and PSD exports have every tag on a 4-byte boundary (ICC.1 §7.1.2), so strict readers accept them (#1589, fixes #1584); GIF, PNG-8 and other indexed exports find each pixel's palette colour through an index instead of a scan, with identical output (#1576); Saving to a network drive on macOS falls back to a plain fsync when the share refuses a full flush (#1625, part of #1620; not confirmed on a real share), and a save still succeeds when a folder refuses the temporary file, the rename over the document or copying permissions: the content is written elsewhere first and copied in, and a failed copy keeps the temporary file and names it (#1649, part of #1620); A document opened by a relative path finds its relatively linked images, and `vectorcraft-cli convert` lists what reading the input left out as `importWarnings` (#1606, fixes #1604); A zero-length subpath draws its round cap as a dot and its projecting cap as a square, so dots in imported `.ai` and SVG files show (#1619, fixes #1613); scores unchanged (estimated) |
